  • Background in cybersecurity consulting, managed security services, or cloud transformation programs.
  • Relevant certifications (AWS, Azure and/or GCP Architect).
  • Familiarity with proposal development, capture support, and pricing of delivery programs.

Location:

  • Remote (U.S.)
  • Preferred: Virginia, Washington D.C., Maryland

About Quantum Sky

Compensation:

  • Compensation is unique to each candidate and relative to the skills and experience they bring to the position. The salary range for this position is typically between $165,000-$195,000. This does not guarantee a specific salary as compensation is based upon multiple factors such as education, experience, certifications, and other requirements, and may fall outside of the above-stated range.

Benefits:

You will work remotely from anywhere in the US, managing a team of internal and co-source resources, helping to modernize our audit function and support Avalara's approach to AI governance and responsible AI adoption.

What Your Responsibilities Will Be

You will:

  • Drive cross-functional audit strategy with executive stakeholders across Security, Engineering, Compliance, Product, Risk Management, and G&A — designing and executing a risk-based IT audit plan that spans financial, operational, IT, security and compliance domains.
  • Manage multiple concurrent audit engagements end-to-end — from strategic scoping and risk prioritization through fieldwork, reporting, and remediation tracking — delivering actionable insights to senior leadership and the Audit Committee.
  • Contribute to the enterprise risk assessment framework, identifying emerging technology, cybersecurity, AI/ML, and business risks — and translating them into a forward-looking audit roadmap that keeps Avalara ahead of the curve. Serve as a trusted advisor to the business on AI governance, algorithmic risk, and the control implications of deploying AI across Avalara's products and operations.
  • Manage and help transform Avalara's IT ICFR/SOX compliance program, helping to set the standard for control design, testing methodology, and regulatory readiness — including evaluating how AI and automation can be embedded into the control environment to increase coverage, reduce latency, and strengthen assurance across a complex, global SaaS environment, while working in sync with Business Process internal auditors to ensure alignment.
  • Manage relationships with IT external auditors and ensure continued alignment and communication to avoid audit fatigue to internal stakeholders.
  • Lead annual technology risk assessments that directly shape the company's audit and enterprise risk management strategies — partnering with the C-suite, ERM, Engineering and Avatech to align priorities with Avalara's growth trajectory.
  • Deliver compelling, executive-ready audit reports that translate complex findings into clear business impact, actionable recommendations, and risk quantification for senior leadership and the Board.
  • Help build and develop a high-performing audit team — attracting top talent, developing future leaders, and fostering a culture of intellectual curiosity, continuous improvement, and operational excellence.
  • Champion the next generation of audit technology — deploying AI-powered anomaly detection, predictive risk scoring, automated control testing, and continuous monitoring to fundamentally reimagine how internal audit delivers value at Avalara. Build the team's AI fluency and establish repeatable frameworks for evaluating and adopting emerging tools.
  • Play a central role in Avalara's public company readiness journey, partnering with internal stakeholders and external audit, to build the controls infrastructure, governance frameworks, and audit capabilities required to operate as a best-in-class public company.
  • Lead high-priority strategic initiatives, M&A due diligence, and special investigations, bringing audit rigor and business acumen to Avalara's most consequential decisions

What You'll Need to be Successful

You have:

  • A Bachelor's degree in Information Systems, Engineering, Risk Management, or related field.
  • 7+ years of progressive experience in IT audit (internal or external), with 3+ years in a people-leadership role within high-growth SaaS, FinTech, or technology companies.
  • CPA, CIA, CISA, CISSP, CCSP or CISM preferred — candidates holding multiple certifications or with deep IT audit and information security credentials are strongly preferred.
  • Deep expertise in internal auditing standards, ICFR/SOX compliance, GAAP, PCAOB standards, SEC regulations, COSO, and COBIT — with hands-on experience auditing cloud-native SaaS architectures, IT general controls, and cybersecurity frameworks (NIST, ISO 27001).
  • 5+ years managing complex ICFR/SOX compliance programs, ideally including experience standing up or transforming a SOX program during periods of rapid growth or M&A integration.
  • Exceptional project management and strategic planning skills, with a track record of managing competing priorities across a global audit portfolio and communicating risk to executive and board-level audiences.
  • Proven ability to recruit, develop, and retain top audit talent — building high-performance teams that punch above their weight in fast-paced, tech-forward environments.
  • Experience with Salesforce, NetSuite, Workday and modern audit/GRC platforms preferred. Hands-on experience with data analytics, AI/ML-driven auditing techniques, and emerging AI governance frameworks is highly valued. Familiarity with how large-scale SaaS companies deploy and govern AI — and the associated risk and compliance implications — is a significant differentiator.

Compensation

The compensation range for this role is as follows: $153,300 - $252,900. The successful candidate's actual salary/wage may be based on various factors, such as geographic location, candidate experience and qualifications, as well as market and business considerations.

This role is eligible for an annual bonus based on individual and company performance, depending on the terms of the applicable plan and the employee's role. This role is also eligible for an equity award, subject to the terms of the applicable plan.

Avalara is an AI-first Company

AI is embedded in our workflows, decision-making, and products. Success here requires embracing AI as an essential capability.

  • You’ll bring experience using AI and AI-related technologies, ready to thrive here.

  • You’ll apply AI every day to business challenges - improving efficiency, contributing solutions, and driving results for your team, our company, and our customers.

  • You’ll grow with AI by staying curious about new trends and best practices, and by sharing what you learn so others can benefit too.

How We'll Take Care of You

Total Rewards

In addition to a great compensation package, paid time off, and paid parental leave, many Avalara employees are eligible for bonuses.

Health & Wellness Benefits vary by location but generally include private medical, life, and disability insurance.

Inclusive culture and diversity Avalara strongly supports diversity, equity, and inclusion, and is committed to integrating them into our business practices and our organizational culture. We also have a total of 8 employee-run resource groups, each with senior leadership and exec sponsorship.

What You Need To Know About Avalara

We’re defining the relationship between tax and tech.

We’ve already built an industry-leading cloud compliance platform, processing over 54 billion customer API calls and over 6.6 million tax returns a year. Our growth is real - we're a billion dollar business - and we’re not slowing down until we’ve achieved our mission - to be part of every transaction in the world.

We’re bright, innovative, and disruptive, like the orange we love to wear. It captures our quirky spirit and optimistic mindset. It shows off the culture we’ve designed, that empowers our people to win. We’ve been different from day one. Join us, and your career will be too.

We’re JLL—a leading professional services and investment management firm specializing in real estate. We shape the future of real estate for a better world by using the most advanced technology to create rewarding opportunities, amazing spaces and sustainable real estate solutions for our clients, our people, and our communities. As a Fortune 200 company, we help real estate owners, occupiers and investors achieve their business ambitions. We have operations in over 80 countries and a global workforce of over 115,000 individuals. We believe a diverse and inclusive culture is one where everyone succeeds. That’s why we’re committed to creating an environment where we all feel welcomed, valued, and empowered to achieve our full potential.


What this job involves:


JLL is building a new division to service customers who are seeking technology forward facilities services solutions. We are seeking a transformational sales leader who will lead the sales effort to build, transform and grow this business, with technology as the enabler. The Head of US Sales, Work Dynamics Facilities Services, will be a pivotal member of the REMS global sales leadership team, responsible for growing the REMS Mid-Market FM business and accompanying technologies in the US. That means leading the sales effort behind JLL’s mid-market goal and winning technology-enabled integrated facilities management (IFM) services deals through a "One JLL" mentality that leverages our unique position serving occupiers in the commercial real estate ecosystem. The ideal candidate understands the distinct buying behaviors, decision-making processes, and value drivers for this segment of IFM services buyers and corporate occupiers, with proven ability to develop tailored go-to-market strategies for each segment. The candidate should be a coach and developer of people, process oriented and evangelist of the use of technology to better drive business outcomes across the entire commercial real estate value chain. The role must carry both the Mid-Market IFM services conversation and the software, technology and data conversation with equal credibility.


REMOTE: Can be located in a major metropolitan area near an airport.

Required Qualifications:

• Experience: 10+ years in a senior sales leadership role (CSO, SVP, or VP of Sales) in technology-enabled services, including IFM, or in the SaaS industry.

• Builder and Transformer: Has built, transformed and grown a sales organization or business line through a step change in scale, ideally in technology-enabled services.

• Matrix Management: Experience managing diverse teams, including BDRs, technical pre sales consultants and services pursuit teams, within a matrixed corporate environment.

• Collaborative DNA: A history of working successfully with Marketing, Product, Engineering, Finance and Operations to achieve shared organizational goals.

• Innovation: A history of defining new offerings and ways of working

Job Title: Global Transparency Disclosure Reporting and Data Analytics Specialist

Job Location: Remote

Job Location Type: Remote

Job Contract Type: Full-time

Job Seniority Level:

Job Description Summary

As a Global Transparency Disclosure Reporting and Data Analytics Specialist, you will provide leadership and oversight to business operations to assure adherence to all aspects of internal company and external regulatory compliance.

In this role, you will ensure appropriate mechanisms are in place to comply with relevant laws and regulations, and adherence to corporate programs and practices. Also, you will focus on data management and reconciliation, analytics and insight generation as well as leverage these insights to recommend and implement process improvements. During the disclosure periods, as a Global Transparency Disclosure Reporting and Data Analytics Specialist, you will manage all United States Federal and State Transparency Disclosure reporting/submissions and be the primary day-to-day point of contact for detailed preparation and readiness activities.

Job Description

Responsibilities -


Transparency Reporting

  • Serving as a subject matter expert on externally mandated US Federal and State transparency reporting requirements. Staying informed about external developments on transparency requirements and related enforcement.
  • Taking a support role with respect to external advocacy on transparency related issues with regulatory agencies and industry associations. In conjunction with the Global Transparency Leader, interpreting transparency laws and regulations for their applicability and impact to GE HealthCare.
  • Collaborating with multiple stakeholders including regional compliance and legal, controllership, finance, sourcing, and business operations to execute deliverables.
  • Developing a comprehensive understanding of GE Healthcare compliance policies, procedures, controls, systems and processes, as it related to Transparency Disclosure Reporting.

Data Management, Reconciliation and Analysis

  • Working with cross-functional business owners to resolve data issues, ensuring data is accurately collected and entered to the applicable source system, managing data reconciliation activities between the data repository and disclosure reporting.
  • Managing onboarding of new data providers.
  • Managing day-to-day disclosure activities during reporting period, investigating and managing remediation of any data issues identified.
  • Running data analyses on transparency data to help ensure completeness and accuracy, researching and generating insights based on the data, for example, trend and outlier analysis to identify areas for further research or remediation, identify and investigate data anomalies.

Apply LEAN Principles – Process improvement, efficiency and simplification

  • Partnering with cross functional business owners to create new business processes or close gaps in existing processes, identifying process gaps and working with appropriate Functions on corrective measures.
  • Creating and maintaining documentation for new and existing transparency processes, mapping upstream/source data processes to review for opportunities and improvement related to transparency data capture.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree, J.D./Masters degree preferred but not required.
  • Professional experience in transparency and/or data analytics related work in the life sciences industry, compliance, law, internal audit, controllership, or related field.
  • Strong oral and written communication skills.
  • Strong leadership with experience of managing and supporting a globally distributed team.
  • Player/coach who is effective in executing both individual responsibilities and team responsibilities.
  • Word, Power Point and Excel skills are required.
  • Professional fluency in English is required.
  • Foreign language skills a plus.

Desired Characteristics

  • Law degree, post-graduate degree in business or another relevant field, or a financial/controllership background.
  • Knowledge of key laws/regulations (e.g., FCPA and other global anti-bribery/anti-corruption laws/regulations, AKS/FCA) and/or core GEHC compliance processes, policies/procedures, tools, and controls.
  • Lean or Six Sigma experience.
  • Proven ability to digest large amounts of information and distill it into the essential elements.
  • Proven analytical, evaluation and problem-solving skills.
  • Process and detail-oriented, including strong organizational skills and ability to prioritize.
  • Self-motivated with ability to handle a large and varied caseload simultaneously, to multitask, and to work independently with minimal supervision.
  • Highest personal integrity with demonstrated ability to handle confidential matters in a discreet and respectful manner that inspires trust.
  • Strong communication, coaching, and interpersonal skills with the ability to work effectively with people at various levels of the organization. Proven ability to foster a team capable of flexing and collaborating across an organization.
  • Strong facilitation and presentation skills, with proven ability to clearly and concisely prepare, present, and discuss findings and recommendations at a senior level and produce clear and compelling report.
  • Ability to interface effectively with senior business and functional leaders throughout the organization.
  • High level of cultural sensitivity, flexibility and emotional intelligence in order to work effectively within a multicultural environment.

Inclusion and Diversity


GE HealthCare is an Equal Opportunity Employer where inclusion matters. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law.

We expect all employees to live and breathe our behaviors: to act with humility and build trust; lead with transparency; deliver with focus, and drive ownership – always with unyielding integrity.

jobs.description:
What You'll Do

As a Staff Software Development Engineer on the Connectors Engineering – SAP Portfolio team, you'll be the senior, hands-on technical resource for AvaTax's most complex SAP implementations. You'll work directly with Certified Implementation Partners (CIPs) and customer IT/Basis/ABAP teams to diagnose and resolve technical issues that arise while deploying AvaTax and related products across SAP ECC, SAP S/4HANA (Private Cloud), and SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud.

You'll own problems end-to-end rather than routing them — debugging ABAP code, dumps, and BAdI/enhancement logic, navigating SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud's Clean Core extensibility model (BTP, CDS views, restricted BAdIs), and resolving the large majority of issues yourself. You'll escalate to Connector Engineering only when an issue is a confirmed product defect, packaging it with the reproduction steps, logs, and traces engineering needs to act quickly. In doing so, you'll protect engineering's roadmap capacity, strengthen Avalara's credibility with high-stakes enterprise SAP partners, and help build the runbooks and mentoring that raise the broader SAP Tax Technology team's troubleshooting capability over time.

What Your Responsibilities Will Be

Technical Ownership & Direct Issue Resolution

  • Serve as the primary technical owner on partner-led and direct SAP implementation projects, joining CIP calls with the depth and authority to resolve issues on the spot.

  • Diagnose technical issues from functional consultants, partners, and customers — spanning connector behavior, ABAP customization, BTP configuration, BAdI/enhancement logic, SAP Basis, or customer-specific code — and resolve them directly in the majority of cases.

  • Escalate to Connector Engineering only for confirmed product defects, with full reproduction steps, logs, and ABAP traces included.

  • Own issues to full closure; success is measured by resolution, not hand-off speed.

SAP Technical Troubleshooting & Debugging

  • Debug live issues across SAP ECC, S/4HANA Private Cloud, and S/4HANA Public Cloud, including ABAP debugging, dump analysis, and connector/interface tracing.

  • Review and advise on custom BAdI implementations, user exits, and enhancement logic partners/customers use to extend Avalara connector functionality (e.g., FlexMapper custom field mapping, address validation BAdIs).

  • Navigate SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud's extensibility model (BTP, CDS views, restricted BAdI framework) to find compliant technical paths where standard extensibility is limited.

  • Apply first-principles troubleshooting to distinguish connector defects from customer configuration, custom code, or platform issues.

  • Understand tax calculation, VAT, and e-invoicing concepts — including country-specific mandates such as real-time reporting and clearance models — well enough to troubleshoot where they intersect with SAP tax determination and connector behavior.

Integration & API-Level Diagnostics

  • Use REST API tooling (Postman, SOAP UI) and log/trace analysis to reproduce issues with evidence, inspecting JSON/XML payloads, authentication, and sync vs. async processing.

  • Analyze connector, ERP-native, and internal logs/traces to pinpoint failure points and separate configuration, data, platform, and product-defect causes.

  • Prepare escalation-ready diagnostic artifacts (repro steps, payloads, logs, error codes, business impact) for the rare genuine engineering escalations.

Client & Partner-Facing Technical Engagement

  • Join customer- and partner-facing calls to explain technical analysis, progress, and options in clear, non-engineering language.

  • Build trusted relationships with CIP technical teams and customer ABAP/Basis resources, positioning Avalara as a strong technical partner on high-stakes, multi-year SAP engagements.

  • Proactively manage expectations on complex or long-running issues, keeping stakeholders aligned on status and next steps.

  • Communicate the boundary of support clearly — guiding on approach and diagnosis without taking ownership of partner/customer-owned custom code.

Collaboration & Enablement

  • Partner with Connector Engineering to keep engineering focused on product development rather than ad hoc firefighting.

  • Work with the functional SAP Tax Technology team to raise their independent debugging capability through runbooks, troubleshooting guides, and training.

  • Document recurring technical patterns (common ABAP errors, BAdI pitfalls, BTP/CDS restrictions) to build institutional knowledge and reduce repeat escalations.

  • Contribute technical input to roadmap and prioritization discussions based on patterns seen across implementations.

AI-Driven Impact

  • Identify and implement opportunities for AI to accelerate technical triage, such as AI-assisted analysis of ABAP dumps, logs, and traces.

  • Design and build AI-powered triage agents that auto-classify escalations, surface likely root cause, and recommend next steps or routing.

  • Integrate AI/LLM capabilities into troubleshooting workflows with appropriate safeguards, observability, and deterministic fallbacks — especially for compliance-critical tax processes.

  • Use AI-assisted tooling (e.g., Cursor or similar) to speed up documentation, runbooks, and issue write-ups, and continuously evaluate emerging AI tools relevant to SAP technical support.

Operating Model

  • Operate as a self-starter with minimal day-to-day direction, proactively identifying and acting on technical risk to go-lives, partner trust, or competitive exposure.

  • Exercise sound judgment on the rare cases that genuinely require engineering involvement — independent resolution is the strong default.

  • Maintain high accountability on time-sensitive, high-visibility implementations where delays can affect go-live dates and partner relationships.

What You'll Need to be Successful

Minimum Requirements

  • B.S. in Computer Science or Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 8–12+ years of experience in SAP technical roles, with direct, hands-on ABAP development and debugging experience, aligned to scope and level of this role.
  • Proven experience with SAP BTP, CDS views, and the SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud extensibility model (including its BAdI restrictions).
  • Direct experience with SAP ECC and SAP S/4HANA (Private Cloud) integrations, ideally including third-party/ISV connector or middleware integrations.
  • Demonstrated ability to debug in live customer/partner environments and to read and interpret ABAP dumps, traces, and enhancement/BAdI code.
  • Strong client-facing skills: comfortable leading technical conversations with enterprise customers and Certified Implementation Partner teams, translating deep technical detail into clear guidance for non-technical stakeholders.
  • Excellent troubleshooting instincts — able to quickly isolate root cause across a complex chain of SAP configuration, custom code, connector logic, and integration middleware.
  • Hands-on fluency with integration and API diagnostic tooling — Postman, SOAP UI, REST/SOAP API testing, and reading JSON/XML payloads, request/response cycles, and standardized error codes to reproduce and evidence issues.
  • Working knowledge of tax calculation, VAT, and e-invoicing concepts, including how country-specific e-invoicing mandates affect SAP document flows.
  • Self-starter who can operate with significant autonomy, manage competing high-priority issues, and drive them to resolution without constant oversight — and without defaulting to engineering escalation as the first move.
  • Demonstrated, hands-on applied AI capability: able to give specific examples of using AI to materially improve speed, quality, or scale of technical work, with the ability to explain tool/approach choices and relevant risk and governance considerations.

Preferred Qualifications

This role is a high-impact, hands-on individual contributor role focused on architecting mission-critical, high-throughput ELR platforms while fundamentally transforming how customers and partners connect to Avalara. A core pillar of this role is designing next-generation tooling, developer experiences, and automated platforms for frictionless customer onboarding, enterprise ERP integrations, and automated schema/format transformation.

You will collaborate closely with distributed engineering teams across the U.S., Europe, India, and Brazil, leading through architectural design, code prototyping, and technical mentorship.

What Your Responsibilities Will Be

Architect at Global ELR Scale

  • Lead the architecture, technical vision, and platform evolution for distributed, multi-tenant ELR cloud services supporting millions of real-time transactions across diverse global jurisdictions.
  • Design ultra-low-latency, fault-tolerant ingestion pipelines, format transformation engines (XML, JSON, UBL, CII), digital signature services, and automated tax authority dispatch gateways.
  • Architect systems optimized for strict auditability, high availability (99.99%+), multi-region active-active deployments, and data residency/compliance isolation.

Build Next-Gen Customer Onboarding & Integration Tooling

  • Pioneer self-service integration frameworks, developer toolkits, and onboarding accelerators that reduce customer time-to-value from weeks to hours.

  • Build interactive testing, simulation, and validation sandboxes allowing enterprise customers to simulate country-specific mandate flows and tax authority responses prior to going live.
  • Standardize modern API designs, webhooks, SDKs, and event-driven integration patterns across the entire ELR product suite.

Be a Hands-On Builder

  • Write production-grade foundational code, reference implementations, SDKs, and architectural spikes that engineering teams build upon.
  • Drive rigorous design and code reviews, championing architectural consistency, modularity, and operational resilience.
  • Proactively identify performance bottlenecks, systemic risks, and technical debt across distributed services, driving architectural remediations.

Lead with AI

  • Design and embed intelligent, AI-powered capabilities into ELR workflows—such as automated schema mapping, predictive error remediation, anomaly detection in high-volume invoice streams, and conversational onboarding assistants.
  • Establish architectural patterns and security standards for responsible, high-leverage AI integration across backend pipelines and developer tools.
  • Drive measurable efficiency gains by automating complex regulatory data extraction and customer integration testing with AI.

  • Mentor and grow senior engineers across global teams through technical coaching, architectural guidance, and hands-on pairing.
  • Establish engineering standards for API design, system observability, automated testing, documentation, and operational excellence.
  • Cultivate a culture of innovation, simplicity, and rapid iteration across global engineering layers.

What You'll Need to be Successful

Required Experience

  • 15+ years of hands-on software engineering experience, with extensive experience designing and operating large-scale distributed cloud systems.
  • Proven track record designing and delivering developer tools, integration platforms, self-service customer onboarding engines, or enterprise integration middleware.
  • Strong proficiency in modern backend languages and runtimes (such as Java, C#/.NET Core, Go, or Python).
  • Deep mastery of API design (REST, GraphQL, gRPC), event-driven architectures (Kafka, EventBridge, RabbitMQ), and microservices design patterns.
  • Experience with complex schema definitions, validation, and payload transformations (e.g., XML/XSD, JSON Schema, UBL, EDI).
  • Extensive experience with AWS (or other major cloud providers) and modern DevOps practices (Terraform, Docker, Kubernetes/ECS, CI/CD).
  • Demonstrated ability to navigate complex domain logic and regulatory requirements with clarity and robust software abstraction.

Strongly Preferred

  • Direct experience in E-Invoicing, Live Reporting, Peppol, EDI/B2B data exchange, or adjacent fintech/compliance/tax domains.
  • Hands-on experience building ERP connectors or middleware integration tooling for enterprise platforms (SAP, NetSuite, Workday, Dynamics 365, Oracle).
  • Experience architecting systems with strict data sovereignty, digital signing (PKI, HSM, X.509 certificates), and cryptographic verification requirements.
  • Experience designing or integrating generative AI and ML models into production data pipelines or developer tooling.
  • Clear builder mindset—passionate about code, architecture, and solving hard technical challenges as an individual contributor.

In your first 6–12 months, you will:

  • Establish a unified architectural roadmap for customer onboarding tooling and integration accelerators across the ELR ecosystem.
  • Deliver foundational platforms and tools that measurably decrease enterprise customer onboarding time and integration friction.
  • Partner with engineering leads across Platforms, Core Services, and Applications to modernize core ELR processing engines for global scale.

  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, Onboarding, Professional Services, and CX to strengthen compliance execution and the Premium Returns for Communications experience.
  • Mentor and coach junior analysts on complex jurisdictions, Premium Returns for Communications best practices, customer communication, and AI-enabled workflows.

What You'll Need to be Successful

Qualifications (Required)

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Tax AND 7+ years of hands-on practical experience in multi-jurisdiction indirect tax compliance – both are required; a degree alone or experience alone is not sufficient.

  • Strong analytical, research, and problem-solving skills; able to operate calmly and methodically under strict filing deadlines.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex tax and system topics in clear, simple language to non-experts.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines in a high-volume environment while maintaining quality.
  • Proven application of AI tools in a professional context to improve efficiency, accuracy, or customer experience (e.g., analysis, summarization, drafting, documentation) – this is a required capability, not a nice-to-have.

12-Month Success Signals

  • Maintain high accuracy with visible reductions in rework, variances, and notices relative to baseline.
  • Implement at least one documented AI-driven workflow or process improvement adopted by the broader team.

AI Bar Raiser Expectations

jobs.description:
What You'll Do

Role Summary

As Avalara scales its AI-first enterprise systems, workflows, and automation footprint, we must reimagine how work is automated, orchestrated, and continuously improved across every function. This role exists to establish and engineer an enterprise-grade AI automation and transformation ecosystem, with n8n as a core platform, enabling faster process transformation, intelligent workflow execution, and measurable gains in productivity, quality, and operational scale.

This is a high-impact individual contributor role responsible for elevating automation standards, reducing manual work and process friction, and enabling AI-powered transformation across the organization.

How This Role Elevates Avalara

This role strengthens Avalara's enterprise automation and transformation capability by establishing scalable, secure, and measurable AI orchestration standards across the organization.

This AI Automation Engineer will:

  • Improve operational efficiency and process quality by engineering resilient AI automation solutions and governed platform standards
  • Accelerate business transformation and reduce cycle time through reusable automation patterns, CI/CD enablement, and standardized development frameworks
  • Enhance employee and customer experience by removing manual bottlenecks, reducing process defects, and increasing AI workflow intelligence
  • Advance Avalara's AI-first execution model by embedding agentic automation, intelligent decisioning, and data-driven observability into enterprise workflows

Bar Raiser Expectations

As a Bar Raiser, this role is expected to elevate the capability and execution rigor of the entire automation and transformation function, not simply contribute as a senior engineer. This includes:

  • Holding high standards for quality, ownership, reliability, and accountability
  • Using metrics (automation adoption, cycle-time reduction, SLAs, SLOs, MTTR, cost per workflow) to guide platform and architectural decisions
  • Simplifying complex business processes into scalable, governed, and maintainable automations
  • Mentoring engineers and contractors to raise automation maturity and talent density
  • Challenging technical assumptions constructively and driving measurable improvement
  • Leaving every platform, process, and engineering practice stronger than it was before

This role does not only build automation, it transforms how work is engineered, automated, governed, and scaled across Avalara.

What Your Responsibilities Will Be

Enterprise AI Automation Leadership

  • Own the enterprise-wide AI automation and transformation strategy with n8n as a core orchestration platform
  • Architect scalable, secure, and resilient automation solutions that eliminate manual effort, improve process quality, and reduce operational friction
  • Design hybrid patterns leveraging n8n/Boomi, APIs, event-driven systems, and AI agents to improve reuse, enable intelligent decisioning, and reduce time-to-value

Platform Ownership (n8n)

  • Enable AI-powered workflow capabilities within n8n (e.g., agent orchestration, prompt management, model integrations, human-in-the-loop controls)
  • Implement workflow standards, logging, monitoring, and reliability guardrails to improve MTTR, uptime, and automation trust
  • Incorporate AI-assisted monitoring, anomaly detection, and intelligent alerting to proactively detect failures, drift, and degraded workflow performance
  • Ensure platform scalability, fault tolerance, and high availability for both deterministic and AI-driven workflows

Standards & Governance

  • Establish enterprise automation development standards and best practices
  • Define exception-handling frameworks, retry strategies, naming conventions, security protocols, and approval patterns that reduce production defects
  • Create reusable templates, accelerators, and automation design patterns, including AI agent templates and reusable prompt frameworks
  • Define governance for AI usage (model selection, cost controls, prompt/version management, data privacy, and auditability)
  • Introduce code review processes and quality gates that increase execution rigor, including AI workflow validation and evaluation standards

Technical Mentorship & Delivery Excellence

  • Operate as a player-coach — hands-on while mentoring engineers
  • Guide contractor and external implementation teams to ensure quality and standards adherence
  • Lead technical design sessions, workflow reviews, and post-incident reviews
  • Mentor teams on designing, building, and operationalizing AI agents and autonomous workflows within business processes
  • Promote best practices for prompt engineering, agent orchestration, human-in-the-loop workflows, and responsible AI automation
  • Elevate automation engineering capability across the organization, including AI fluency and adoption

12-Month Success Signals

Within the first 12 months, this role will have:

  • Enabled AI-native automation capabilities, including production-grade AI agents integrated into core workflows
  • Improved automation reliability and reduced workflow failure rates and/or MTTR
  • Standardized automation patterns, including AI-enabled orchestration patterns, adopted across new transformation initiatives
  • Implemented measurable observability, including AI performance, business impact, and cost metrics
  • Delivered AI-driven automation use cases that reduce manual effort, improve decision-making, or shorten process cycle time across multiple functions
  • Raised execution standards across the automation team through mentorship, technical leadership, and AI capability development

What You'll Need to be Successful

AI Expectations

As an AI-first company, Avalara expects this role to embed AI into how automation and transformation work is designed and executed.

This role will:

  • Design and implement AI-enabled workflows and transformation patterns that materially improve speed, automation, and scale
  • Use AI tools to optimize development productivity, workflow diagnostics, process analysis, and root-cause investigation
  • Identify high-value AI automation opportunities tied to efficiency, reliability, employee experience, or customer impact

  • Elevate AI capability across the automation team by sharing best practices and driving measurable adoption

  • B.S. in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field (required)
  • 10+ years of experience in enterprise automation, workflow engineering, integration engineering, or platform architecture
  • Deep hands-on expertise in n8n or Boomi, including building and orchestrating AI-enabled workflows, agents, and cross-functional business automations
  • Experience designing API-first and event-driven architectures, including integration of AI/ML services and agent-based systems
  • Strong understanding of REST, webhooks, OAuth, JWT, and API security, along with secure integration of AI services and model endpoints
  • Experience implementing CI/CD for automation or integration platforms, including deployment and versioning strategies for AI workflows, prompts, and models
  • Cloud experience (AWS, Azure, or GCP), including AI/ML services (e.g., Bedrock, Azure OpenAI) and scalable model integration patterns
  • Familiarity with LLMs, prompt engineering, AI agents, and orchestration frameworks, and how they apply to enterprise automation
  • Experience with observability and monitoring, including AI-specific considerations (latency, cost, accuracy, drift)
  • Proven ability to influence architecture and technical direction at scale, including driving adoption of AI-powered automation, process transformation, and intelligent orchestration patterns

Pay Range Details

The base pay range(s) below are provided in compliance with state specific laws. Pay ranges may be different in other locations.

Colorado $126,000-$201,600 (annually)

Washington $126,000-$222,800 (annually)

What You'll Do

As Head of Operations, you'll own onboarding, go-live and customer support for a portfolio that includes DAVO (automated sales tax for small businesses, set up through their point-of-sale system) and MyLodgeTax (lodging tax registration and filing for short-term rental hosts), along with the registration operations that get customers compliant in the first place.

This isn't a role about growing a support team in line with customer growth. It's about building an operation where most customers never need to contact us — because onboarding just works, problems are caught early, and the manual work is automated away. You'll lead the teams that serve customers today and work directly with Product and Engineering to make each of those teams more scalable every quarter.

Own the customer's first 90 days. Lead onboarding and go-live for every customer, from signup to their first successful filing. Define what a great activation looks like, measure it, and remove the friction that slows customers down or sends them to support.

Set service standards, staffing models and quality measures, and treat every recurring contact as a problem to eliminate rather than a ticket to close.

Automate registration operations. Lead the team that handles tax registrations for MyLodgeTax customers today, and partner with Product and Engineering to automate that work, so the team can focus on the exceptions that really need a person.

Turn customer friction into product fixes. Build the feedback loop between operations and the product team: which issues drive contacts, which onboarding steps lose customers, and which fixes would pay back fastest. Bring data, not anecdotes, to roadmap conversations.

ATR operates at the intersection of high-scale cloud services, information-dense domain content, and cutting-edge generative AI workflows. In this domain, precision is paramount: tax research demands authoritative, citation-backed accuracy where hallucination is unacceptable.

As a Software Architect, you will shape how ATR scales across microservices, data pipelines, domain knowledge graphs, and multi-agent AI architectures. You will be hands-on with reference implementations and proof-of-concepts while exercising high-order communication and influence—collaborating across engineering pods, negotiating API contracts and integration protocols with cross-functional platform teams, and establishing pragmatic architecture roadmaps.

How This Role Elevates Avalara:

Team:

  • Establishes robust platform patterns, domain-driven service boundaries, and clear technical direction across multiple engineering squads.

  • Raises the engineering bar through hands-on reference designs, rigorous architecture reviews, and mentorship of Staff engineers and Tech Leads.

  • Reduces accidental complexity and technical debt by standardizing microservice design, event-driven interfaces, and AI orchestration protocols.

Business:

  • Accelerates time-to-market for premier AI capabilities across Indirect, Direct, and Trade tax domains without compromising reliability, compliance, or cost efficiency.

  • Strengthens Avalara’s competitive moat by transforming vast, complex tax repositories into high-confidence, programmatic APIs and agentic research workflows.

Customer:

  • Delivers rapid, resilient, and citation-backed research experiences that tax professionals and automated systems can trust implicitly.

  • Translates advanced AI and retrieval architectures into verifiable, audit-proof answers with transparent provenance and sub-second performance.

What Your Responsibilities Will Be

Key Responsibilities:

End-to-End Architecture & Microservices Strategy

  • Own and evolve the target-state architecture for ATR across microservices, data ingestion, search/retrieval, and AI agent layers.

  • Architect high-throughput, low-latency, resilient distributed microservices utilizing modern cloud-native stacks (Go, PostgreSQL, vector stores, distributed streaming, and event-driven messaging).

  • Define clean service boundaries, gRPC/REST APIs, asynchronous workflows, and integration protocols across disparate domain subsystems.

AI-Native, Multi-Agent & Grounded Retrieval Systems

  • Lead the architecture for ATR’s AI-native capabilities, including advanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), vector search, semantic routing, and citation attribution pipelines designed for information-dense content.

  • Architect multi-turn, multi-agent systems and Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations where domain-specialized agents collaborate to decompose complex research queries and execute structured tax workflows.

  • Integrate continuous AI evaluation, observability, and guardrail frameworks (e.g., Arize or equivalent LLM eval platforms) to measure, benchmark, and systematically improve answer quality, grounding fidelity, and latency.

Cross-Team Collaboration & Technical Influence

  • Serve as the technical authority and primary architecture liaison across engineering pods, product management, security, SRE, and adjacent platform teams.

  • Negotiate integration protocols, contract schemas, and shared infrastructure boundaries with clarity and pragmatic engineering judgment.

  • Translate business strategy into phased architectural blueprints, RFCs, and delivery milestones aligned with organizational operating models (AIM30).

Hands-On Technical Leadership & Governance

  • Build proof-of-concepts (PoCs), reference implementations, and scaffolding for novel agentic workflows, caching strategies, and data access layers.

  • Partner with tax content engineering stakeholders to design ingestion and normalization pipelines for highly structured and unstructured legal/tax datasets.

  • Champion non-functional requirements (NFRs): multi-tenancy isolation, secrets management, role-based access control (RBAC), operational observability, disaster recovery, and cost-to-serve optimization.

 

12-Month Success Signals:

  • Verifiable Accuracy & Grounding: Citation fidelity and answer grounding metrics reach industry-leading accuracy benchmarks with automated evaluation pipelines actively catching regressions.

  • Architectural Cohesion: Service boundaries and API contracts across ATR’s core microservices and domain-specific agents are clearly defined, reducing cross-team delivery dependencies.

  • Multi-Agent & Workflow Maturity: A scalable multi-agent and workflow orchestration framework is established in production, enabling multi-turn research and tool-calling capabilities.

  • Engineering Velocity: Reusable service templates, reference implementations, and standardized evaluation patterns measurably reduce the onboarding and feature delivery time for engineering pods.

  • Operational Rigor: System reliability, P99 latency, and cost-per-query targets meet or exceed established SLA/SLO thresholds under growing enterprise workloads.

AI Expectations:

Avalara is an AI-first company, and ATR is a flagship AI product. Every senior technical leader is expected to demonstrate role-relevant AI leadership:

  • Architecting for Accuracy: Designing retrieval and agent architectures that prioritize grounding, transparency, and provenance over unvalidated generation.

  • Systematic Evaluation: Leveraging automated evals and LLM-as-a-judge pipelines to optimize prompts, context windows, chunking strategies, and model selection.

  • Engineering Productivity: Championing agentic development tools and AI-assisted workflows within engineering teams to accelerate code quality, testing, and architecture exploration.

  • Safety & Responsible AI: Implementing robust guardrails for prompt injection defense, data privacy, tenant isolation, and auditability.

What You'll Need to be Successful

What You'll Need to be Successful:

  • Education & Experience: B.S./M.S. in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or equivalent practical experience, with 10+ years of progressive software engineering and distributed systems experience.

  • Leadership Level: Proven track record as a Staff+ Engineer, Principal Engineer, or Software Architect (I6 equivalent) driving architecture for enterprise-grade SaaS platforms.

  • Distributed Microservices Mastery: Deep, hands-on expertise designing, building, and deploying microservices architectures in production using modern back-end languages (e.g., Go, Java, or C#) and relational databases (e.g., PostgreSQL).

  • Applied AI & Information-Dense Retrieval: Demonstrated experience building production-grade RAG and AI applications over dense, authoritative content domains. Strong understanding of embeddings, vector databases, hybrid lexical/semantic search, and chunking/re-ranking strategies.

  • Evaluation & Quality Benchmarking: Hands-on familiarity with LLM observability and evaluation frameworks (e.g., Arize, Ragas, Phoenix, TruLens, or LangSmith) to benchmark hallucination rates, retrieval precision, and answer relevance.

  • Exceptional Communication & Negotiation: High-order verbal and written communication skills with proven ability to author crisp architectural design records (ADRs/RFCs), align diverse stakeholders, and negotiate cross-team technical contracts.

  • Security & Cloud Resiliency: Thorough understanding of cloud-native design, container orchestration (Kubernetes), API gateways/service mesh, zero-trust security, and observability (metrics, tracing, structured logs).

Preferred/Nice-to-Have

  • Experience architecting multi-agent systems, agent coordination protocols, Model Context Protocol (MCP), or graph-based workflow engines (e.g., LangGraph, Temporal, or custom state machines).

  • Experience with domain-driven design for complex metadata, knowledge graphs, or regulatory/compliance document repositories.

  • Familiarity with enterprise search engines (Elasticsearch, OpenSearch) combined with dense retrieval vector stores (pgvector, Qdrant, Pinecone, Milvus).

Senior FDA Compliance Analyst

Reports to: Head of Third Party Services

Position Summary

The Senior FDA Compliance Analyst supports FDA regulatory compliance across the organization's multi-site fertility network. Reporting to the Head of Third Party Services, this position serves as a subject matter resource for FDA requirements related to third party reproduction and supports the development, implementation, and monitoring of consistent regulatory processes.

The Analyst plays a key role in transitioning the organization toward a centralized FDA compliance model, with a focus on regulatory oversight, policy development, staff education, auditing, inspection readiness, and new practice integration.

Core Responsibilities

FDA Regulatory Compliance

  • Serve as a subject matter resource for FDA requirements applicable to third party reproduction.
  • Monitor regulatory changes, assess operational impacts, and communicate updates to appropriate stakeholders.
  • Provide guidance on donor eligibility, screening, testing, documentation, quarantine, release, and recordkeeping.
  • Collaborate with internal stakeholders and external regulatory partners to address compliance questions and concerns.

Program Development & Standardization

  • Support the development and implementation of a centralized FDA compliance model across the network.
  • Assess existing workflows, identify regulatory and operational gaps, and recommend process improvements.
  • Develop and maintain standardized policies, consents, SOPs, work instructions, and documentation requirements.
  • Support consistent application of FDA requirements while accounting for appropriate practice-level differences.
  • Identify opportunities to optimize technology, workflows, and centralized support processes.

Auditing & Compliance Monitoring

  • Support the development and execution of an internal FDA audit program.
  • Conduct routine and targeted audits to identify compliance gaps, documentation deficiencies, and operational risks.
  • Prepare audit findings and recommendations and assist with corrective and preventive action plans.
  • Track corrective actions through resolution and monitor recurring issues.
  • Maintain compliance metrics and provide regular updates to the Head of Third Party Services.

FDA Inspection Readiness

  • Support ongoing FDA inspection readiness across applicable practices.
  • Conduct readiness assessments, mock inspections, and documentation reviews.
  • Serve as a key resource during FDA inspections, coordinating documentation, communication, and follow-up activities.
  • Assist with responses to regulatory observations and corrective actions.
  • Maintain inspection records and share lessons learned across the network.

Education & Training

  • Develop and deliver standardized FDA compliance education and training.
  • Support onboarding, ongoing education, and competency development for staff involved in FDA-regulated activities.
  • Provide targeted education in response to regulatory changes, audit findings, and identified knowledge gaps.
  • Serve as an ongoing resource for staff questions related to FDA requirements.

Integration & New Practice Support

  • Participate in FDA compliance assessments during acquisition due diligence and support transition planning for newly integrated practices.
  • Support FDA compliance assessments for new practice acquisitions and integrations.
  • Review current-state workflows, policies, documentation, and systems to identify gaps.
  • Assist with transition plans to align new practices with the organization's centralized FDA compliance model.
  • Coordinate implementation of required workflows, SOPs, tools, and training.
  • Provide go-live and post-implementation support and monitor adoption.

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor's degree in regulatory affairs, life sciences, healthcare administration, quality management, business administration, or a related field; equivalent relevant experience may be considered.
  • Experience in FDA-regulated reproductive medicine, tissue banking, third party reproduction, or a comparable regulatory environment.
  • Knowledge of FDA requirements related to reproductive tissue and donor eligibility.
  • Experience developing and maintaining regulatory policies, SOPs, and workflows.
  • Experience conducting compliance audits, supporting regulatory inspections, and tracking corrective actions.
  • Ability to interpret regulatory requirements and translate them into practical operational processes.
  • Ability to independently prioritize work, manage multiple projects simultaneously, and exercise sound judgment when evaluating regulatory and operational risks.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, communication, and project management skills.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively across multiple practices and departments.

Preferred

  • Experience with donor egg, donor sperm, embryo donation, gestational carrier, or other third party reproductive services.
  • Experience supporting FDA compliance across a multi-site healthcare organization.
  • Experience with centralized compliance programs, practice integrations, and regulatory process improvement.
  • Experience developing compliance education and supporting FDA inspections.

jobs.description:
This role is open to applicants living in the Philippines.

Operations Assistant VA

Keep Every Order Moving, From Vendor to Warehouse

Why This Role Matters
Before a lab can order from Filtrous, the product has to be on our shelves, and that starts with a purchase order placed well in advance. When that order goes out late, a vendor falls behind, or a shipment arrives wrong, our stock runs low and customers wait. As our Operations Assistant VA, you'll own the purchasing and vendor pipeline end-to-end, from the reorder sheet to the warehouse door. You'll make sure purchase orders go out on time, vendors stay on schedule, and shipments don't fall apart. In a business built on speed and reliability, your work keeps products in stock and our customers' labs running.

What You'll Do
• Turn the Reorder Sheet into Purchase Orders: Work from our reorder sheet to figure out what we need, build purchase orders in our ERP system with the purchasing team, and route them to leadership for approval.
• Source Product with Vendors: Find supplier options, request and compare quotes, and work through product specs and minimum order quantities before an order is placed.
• Confirm Every Order Detail: Send purchase orders to vendors, get the proforma invoice back, and work out adjustments like carton quantities and price changes. Verify barcodes with our operations team before anything is confirmed, and send vendors the full item package: photos, Certificate of Analysis (CoA), and packing list.
• Keep Payments and Production on Track: Send vendor invoices to our finance team for payment, share proof of payment with the vendor, and get a production timeline back. Follow up with every vendor at least weekly, every three days if they go quiet, and escalate if they stop responding. WeChat must be used during business hours for faster turnaround on vendor communication.
• Coordinate Shipping, Tariffs, and Customs: Work with our logistics team and freight partners on shipping and tariffs, consolidating across open purchase orders so we never ship a partial container. Handle customs declarations, declared values, and product classifications using information provided or approved by the company.
• Keep the Warehouse Ready for Every Delivery: Update our ERP system as soon as a delivery date is set and share it with the warehouse right away, then send reminders a week out, three days out, and the morning of delivery.
• Fix Problems and Track Every Order: If a shipment arrives incorrect or damaged, contact the vendor promptly and arrange a timely re-shipment at the vendor's cost. Keep a tracking sheet with each PO number, its exact status, and dates for everything, and other duties as assigned.

Problems You Will Solve
• Purchase orders go out late: Without one person working the reorder sheet and pushing orders through approval, purchase orders slip and stock runs low before replacements are on the way.
• Vendors drift off schedule: When no one follows up on a steady rhythm, suppliers go quiet, production timelines slide, and delays surface only when it is too late to recover.
• Order details slip through the cracks: When carton quantities, price changes, barcodes, and product documents are not checked before an order is confirmed, small mistakes turn into wrong labels, wrong quantities, and costly rework.
• Shipping costs more than it should: Partial containers, orders that are not consolidated, and incomplete customs paperwork add freight costs, tariff surprises, and delays at the border.
• Deliveries catch the warehouse off guard: Without accurate delivery dates and timely reminders, shipments show up unannounced, receiving gets rushed, and damaged or incorrect goods are not sent back to the vendor in time.

How Success is Measured
• Get purchase orders built, approved, and sent to vendors on time, every month
• Follow up on every open order at least weekly, with a confirmed production timeline
• Ship zero partial containers by consolidating open orders on every shipment
• Keep the tracking sheet and ERP current, and give the warehouse notice before every delivery

Why You'll Love It Here
At Filtrous, you won't be a back-office clerk pushing paperwork. You'll own a pipeline that keeps real laboratories stocked with the supplies they rely on every day. You'll work in a fast-paced, high-growth environment where your ideas for faster, smoother purchasing actually get implemented. You'll collaborate closely with our purchasing, finance, logistics, and warehouse teams, and your impact on on-time orders and in-stock products will be visible and celebrated. As we grow, so will your career, with opportunities to shape how Filtrous buys and ships from the ground up.

Who You Are
• Bachelor's degree in Business, Supply Chain Management, Operations, or a related field (required)
• Experience in purchasing, procurement, or supply chain coordination, working directly with vendors (required)
• Proficient with ERP and inventory systems (e.g., Acumatica, NetSuite, SAP) and spreadsheets (Excel or Google Sheets)
• Comfortable with international shipping basics: freight, tariffs, customs declarations, and product classifications
• Strong written English and the persistence to keep vendors responsive across time zones
• Highly organized with a process-driven mindset and commitment to follow-through

Bonus points if you have:

  • Background in the life sciences, biotechnology, or laboratory supplies industry
    • Experience importing from overseas suppliers, including container consolidation and vendor communication on WeChat

About Filtrous
Founded in 2017, Filtrous delivers speed, quality, and value to agile labs. We're a lab supplies distributor serving laboratories across a wide range of scientific and industrial sectors. Our secret? We combine uncompromising product quality with customer service that actually picks up the phone.

About Rosenblum Law and why this role exists

Rosenblum Law is a growth-focused consumer law firm with three practices: Estate Planning, Traffic Tickets (TrafficTickets.com), and Personal Injury. Our growth runs on technology: lead capture, call tracking, SMS and email nurture, paid acquisition, payments, and the project systems that keep cases moving.

That stack has grown tool by tool, with no single owner. Configuration lives in people's heads, integrations are stitched together with Zapier, and fixes happen reactively. We are hiring our first dedicated technology leader to own how our systems work and connect, make them reliable and documented, and turn them into a competitive advantage.

Role summary

Title

Head of Technology & Systems

Reports to

Chief Operating Officer

Works closely with

CEO, Chief Growth Officer, Managing Attorney, practice leads, sales and intake

Team

Individual contributor at start; may build a small team or manage contractors as the roadmap grows

Location: Remote

Type

Full-time

You will own how technology works and connects at the firm: the integrations, data flows, and architecture across every platform. Marketing platforms are run day to day by the growth team, and you'll support their maintenance and technical health. Half your time is hands-on: building automations, fixing integrations, configuring platforms, and supporting users. The other half is strategic: setting the architecture, choosing and retiring vendors, owning data and security, and building a roadmap leadership can fund and track.

The environment you'll own

You inherit a modern SaaS stack of roughly 15 platforms, with no on-premise infrastructure to speak of. The work is integration, data, automation, and governance.

Category

Platforms

What they do for us

CRM

FileMaker Pro

The firm's CRM: client and matter records, the system of record for client data

Marketing automation & lead nurture

ActiveCampaign, Loops

Email and automation journeys, lead and deal pipelines

Shared intake & communications

CallTrackingMetrics, Sakari

Call tracking and attribution, routing, queues, transcription, two-way texting

Acquisition & SEO

Meta Ads, firm websites incl. TrafficTickets.com

Paid social, search visibility, landing pages and lead forms

Work management

ClickUp

PMO, practice workflows, capacity planning

Collaboration

Google Workspace (Gmail, Drive, Calendar, Docs), Slack

Email, files, scheduling, internal communication

Payments & finance

Stripe, ACH payment workflows

Client payments; ACH validation and bank verification improvements in flight

Workforce

Hubstaff; payroll and contractor platforms (Gusto, Payoneer under review)

Time tracking, payroll, international contractor payments

Automation & AI

Zapier, Claude, AI dictation tools

Cross-system workflows, AI-assisted work

Who owns what: FileMaker Pro is the firm's CRM, and you will own it outright, including its configuration, data quality, and integrations. CallTrackingMetrics and Sakari are shared intake and communications systems used by marketing, sales, and intake, and you will own them outright. The marketing platforms (ActiveCampaign, Loops, Meta Ads, and the firm websites) are owned day to day by the growth team; you own their integrations and support their maintenance. You own all other platforms.

Known work already on the table: the CRM migration project; documenting the ActiveCampaign, CallTrackingMetrics, and Sakari configuration and integrations; restructuring the ClickUp workspace; fixing recurring ACH bounces with a validated payment form and bank verification; and evaluating contractor payment platforms.

Key responsibilities

Strategy and architecture

  • Own the firm's technology roadmap, tied to business goals for each practice, and report progress to leadership.
  • Define a target architecture: which system is the source of truth for leads, clients, matters, payments, and people, and how data flows between them.
  • Run vendor selection, contracts, renewals, and consolidation. Stay vendor-agnostic until requirements are clear, and retire tools that overlap.
  • Own the technology budget and track license spend against usage.
  • Set and enforce standards for security, access, data retention, and client confidentiality appropriate to a law firm.

Hands-on build and optimization

  • Administer and configure the firm's core operating systems: FileMaker Pro (CRM), CallTrackingMetrics and Sakari (shared intake and communications), ClickUp, Google Workspace, Slack, and Stripe.
  • Own the integrations between the marketing platforms (ActiveCampaign, Loops, Meta Ads, and the firm websites) and the firm's other systems, and support the growth team with platform maintenance: access, updates, troubleshooting, and vendor issues.
  • Design, build, and maintain integrations and automations (Zapier today; APIs and webhooks where they are more robust).
  • Own the integrations behind lead-to-client flow (forms to the FileMaker Pro CRM and ActiveCampaign, call and SMS data, routing, and handoff from intake to the practice teams), and partner with the growth team on nurture sequences and speed-to-lead.
  • Build reliable attribution so marketing spend in Meta and search ties to calls, signed clients, and revenue.
  • Ship payment and billing improvements, starting with ACH validation and bank verification.
  • Find practical uses for AI across intake, marketing, and operations, with guardrails.

Operations, support, and governance

  • Be the escalation point for system issues. Triage, fix, and find root causes rather than patching symptoms.
  • Own user lifecycle: onboarding and offboarding, accounts, permissions, and device setup.
  • Document every system's configuration, integrations, and owners, and keep that documentation current.
  • Monitor integrations and data quality; catch broken automations before clients or staff do.
  • Train staff and write simple how-to guides so the firm uses the tools it pays for.

Your first year

1. First 30 days: learn and stabilize. Meet every team, inventory every system, login, integration, and contract. Fix the top three pain points staff raise. Take over admin access for core platforms, and integration access for marketing platforms.

2. Days 31–60: document and decide. Finish documentation of each core system's configuration and integrations (starting with ActiveCampaign, CallTrackingMetrics, and Sakari). Deliver a current-state architecture map, a risk list, and a prioritized backlog.

3. Days 61–90: roadmap and first wins. Present a 12-month technology roadmap and budget to leadership. Ship two to three visible improvements, such as the ACH payment form or a speed-to-lead fix.

4. Months 4–12: build the platform. Deliver the roadmap: consolidated tools, reliable lead-to-revenue reporting, monitored integrations, security baseline in place, and staff trained on the systems they use.

Qualifications

Required

  • AI-first mindset (we are an AI-first organization). Hands-on experience using AI tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, or Copilot to automate work, build workflows, and change how teams operate, with a track record of rolling them out with practical guardrails. You will lead how the firm uses AI across every practice.
  • 7+ years in business systems, IT, or marketing/revenue operations, including 2+ years owning a multi-platform SaaS environment end to end.
  • Hands-on experience integrating and supporting marketing automation or CRM platforms (ActiveCampaign, HubSpot, Salesforce, or similar).
  • Proven integration skills: Zapier or Make, plus REST APIs, webhooks, and JSON.
  • Comfortable writing light scripts (JavaScript or Python).
  • Experience with call tracking, telephony, or SMS platforms and their attribution data.
  • Track record of documenting systems and running vendor evaluations with clear recommendations.
  • Working knowledge of SaaS security: SSO, MFA, role-based access, offboarding, data retention.
  • Clear communicator who can explain trade-offs to non-technical leaders and train front-line staff.

Preferred

  • FileMaker Pro development or administration experience.
  • Experience with Stripe, ACH, or bank verification providers.
  • Reporting and BI skills (SQL, Looker Studio, or similar) to build lead-to-revenue dashboards.
  • Has built or led a small team or managed outside contractors.

What success looks like

Targets are set with the COO in the first 90 days, once baselines exist.

Measure

Broken automations or integrations caught by monitoring before users report them

Support

Time to resolve system issues; repeat issues trending down

Documentation

Growth

Payments

ACH return rate; time from payment to service start

Spend

Security

MFA and SSO coverage; offboarding completed same day

Adoption

Staff satisfaction with tools; training completed for core systems

Compensation and how to apply

jobs.excerpt: Role Summary Revamp is looking for an Associate Principal Electrical Engineer for utility-scale battery energy storage system (BESS) projects, including standalone storage and PV-plus-storage facilities.
jobs.description:
Role Summary

Revamp is looking for an Associate Principal Electrical Engineer for utility-scale battery energy storage system (BESS) projects, including standalone storage and PV-plus-storage facilities. You will seal electrical design packages, own the technical direction of a program of BESS projects, and act as the PV/BESS group's main electrical point of contact for clients, EPC contractors, and authorities having jurisdiction. The storage projects you support will help turn renewable power generation into a source of dispatchable power, and your work will play a direct role in the energy transition. As an employee-owner, you will have a personal stake in the success of your projects and the organization as a whole.

Duties & Responsibilities

Core Technical & Functional Responsibilities

  • Serve as Engineer of Record for BESS and PV-plus-storage projects, sealing electrical drawings, calculations, and specifications in states where you hold licensure.
  • Direct BESS electrical design from conceptual layout through issued-for-construction, including DC block and PCS arrangements, MV collection, auxiliary power, grounding, and SCADA and communications interfaces.
  • Review and approve single-line and three-line diagrams, AC and DC cable sizing, grounding designs, and equipment specifications.
  • Establish design criteria for AC- and DC-coupled storage, augmentation strategies, and hybrid PV-plus-storage plants.
  • Evaluate battery enclosure, PCS, transformer, and switchgear submittals, resolving technical deviations with equipment manufacturers.
  • Coordinate BESS electrical studies, including short-circuit, arc flash, load flow, voltage drop, wire loss, auxiliary load, and ground grid analysis.
  • Integrate fire protection and hazard mitigation requirements, including NFPA 855 spacing and explosion control inputs, into the electrical design.
  • Resolve unusual technical conditions and design conflicts using expert judgment, seeking guidance only for program-level issues.

Project & Portfolio Execution

  • Oversee the technical and delivery performance of all BESS projects within an assigned program.
  • Approve scopes, budgets, and schedules for electrical design assignments, identifying risks or deviations early.
  • Prepare proposals and fee estimates for BESS electrical engineering services in collaboration with Business Development.
  • Lead and assign engineers and designers needed to complete deliverables across concurrent projects.
  • Lead and participate in BESS program reviews and client program meetings.
  • Mentor Engineer I–III and Senior Engineer staff in BESS design practice, code application, and Engineer of Record responsibilities.
  • Act as a supervisor of assigned staff, including performance feedback and development planning.

Quality, Standards & Compliance

  • Review complete BESS design packages for conformity, constructability, and quality assurance before sealing.
  • Ensure designs comply with the NEC (including Articles 480, 690, 691, 705, and 706), NFPA 855 and 70E, UL 9540 and 9540A, IEEE 1547 and 2800, and applicable utility and AHJ requirements.
  • Set and maintain the group's BESS electrical design standards, templates, and calculation tools.
  • Resolve AHJ, utility, and third-party review comments and maintain records of sealed documents.

Collaboration & Communication

  • Act as one of the PV/BESS group's main electrical points of contact for clients, EPC contractors, and AHJs across a program of BESS projects.
  • Coordinate with civil, structural, High Voltage, and Power Systems Engineering teams on layouts, substation interfaces, and interconnection requirements.
  • Lead design reviews and technical meetings, presenting recommendations and trade-offs to clients and internal stakeholders.
  • Negotiate technical scope and design changes with clients and contractors, documenting impacts on schedule and budget.

Program, Strategy & Innovation

  • Track BESS technology, code, and market developments, setting the group's design response to them.
  • Develop new techniques, tools, and improved processes for BESS electrical design and review.
  • Advise Revamp leadership as a technical specialist on energy storage design.
  • Represent Revamp in industry working groups and technical forums on energy storage.

Additional Responsibilities

  • Perform essential duties, including meeting deliverables and deadlines.
  • Occasionally perform additional related duties as assigned or directed.

Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering or similar applicable work experience.
  • 10+ years of electrical design experience on utility-scale power generation projects, with substantial experience specifically in solar PV or BESS design.
  • Active Professional Engineer (PE) license in electrical engineering, with the ability to obtain licensure in additional states.
  • Experience serving as Engineer of Record or lead electrical engineer for utility-scale BESS projects.
  • In-depth knowledge of the NEC, NFPA 855, UL 9540 and 9540A, and IEEE standards that apply to energy storage and interconnection.
  • Experience designing MV collection systems, grounding systems, and BESS auxiliary power systems.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage scopes, budgets, and schedules across concurrent projects and to lead and mentor engineering teams.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including presenting technical recommendations to clients and AHJs.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master’s degree in electrical engineering with a power systems focus.
  • PE licensure in multiple states or an active NCEES Record.
  • Proficiency with ETAP, SKM, EasyPower, CYMCAP, or comparable power analysis software, and with AutoCAD.
  • Experience with battery enclosure and PCS products from multiple manufacturers and with augmentation planning.
  • Experience with hybrid plant controls and SCADA integration for PV-plus-storage facilities.
  • Prior work in an engineering consulting, owner/developer, or EPC environment supporting utility-scale renewable projects.

Benefits for Full-Time Positions

· Participation in Revamp’s Employee Ownership ESOP program.

· Competitive compensation with bonus.

· Full benefits package offerings including 99% employer-paid health, vision, life, and dental insurance.

· Medical, dependent care, and commuter FSA.

· Monthly health and wellness stipend.

· Attractive vacation, sick, and holiday pay.

· Paid parental leave.

· 401(k) savings plan with 100% match up to 6%, vested immediately.

· Paid volunteer time off and charitable donation matching.

About Revamp

Founded in 2016, Revamp is the premier employee-owned engineering design firm dedicated to advancing large-scale renewable energy projects. Our team is united by a shared commitment to accelerating the global energy transition and creating a workplace where talented people can make a tangible impact in the fight against climate change.

As employee-owners, we take pride in building a culture of collaboration, innovation, and accountability where every individual’s contribution drives both company success and personal growth. Revamp engineers have supported the design of more than 10% of the utility-scale solar generation capacity in the US since 2020, contributing directly to the renewable energy transformation.

So much more than just an engineering firm; we are a diverse, international team of artists, singers, dancers, pastry chefs, outdoor enthusiasts, animal lovers, travelers and problem-solvers who bring curiosity and creativity to everything we do. For more information, visit www.revamp‑eng.com.

Disclaimers

Employment with Revamp Engineering Inc. may be subject to background checks that are permitted by applicable law and relevant to the position. Any such checks will be conducted in compliance with all legal requirements, including providing notice, obtaining consent where required, and allowing candidates to access and correct personal information as permitted by law.
