jobs.excerpt: The Managing Editor oversees all editorial, production, and publication operations for Architecture at Rice, the peer-reviewed imprint of the Rice School of Architecture.
jobs.description:
The Managing Editor oversees all editorial, production, and publication operations for Architecture at Rice, the peer-reviewed imprint of the Rice School of Architecture. Published since 1961 and newly relaunched, Architecture at Rice produces peer-reviewed book-length studies, thematic anthologies on architecture and the city, and two specialized series: Dossiers (focusing on pedagogy) and Pamphlets (focusing on research in progress). The imprint engages cultural, political, and environmental issues through established and emerging threads of design thinking, connecting local and global dialogues across art, architecture, and landscape.

Working in close collaboration with the Associate Dean, school faculty, and internationally recognized contributing scholars, the Managing Editor manages the full lifecycle of print and digital publications. Key responsibilities include managing peer-review workflows, developmental and structural editing, translation oversight, production coordination with external designers and printers, and developing strategic publication plans. The position ensures that Architecture at Rice maintains the highest standards of academic rigor, editorial precision, and public reach.

The ideal candidate is an accomplished scholarly editor and architectural historian with deep expertise in design theory, pedagogy, and academic book publishing. The candidate combines rigorous scholarly credentials with extensive hands-on experience directing complex editorial project lifecycles, managing peer-review processes, and executing high-level manuscript editing across academic presses and cultural platforms. Possessing sophisticated editorial precision and translation expertise, the ideal candidate moves effortlessly between complex theoretical concepts and refined prose. The candidate brings university-level teaching or research experience in architectural history and theory, enabling seamless collaboration with faculty, international scholars, graphic designers, external editors, and university leadership.

Special Instructions to Applicants

All interested applicants should attach a resume (or Curriculum Vitae) and a cover letter detailing their experience in scholarly, architectural, or academic editorial management in the Supporting Documents section of the application, preferably in PDF format to avoid formatting issues. Applicants should also submit a sample of published editorial work or a portfolio demonstrating scholarly manuscript-editing experience.

Workplace Location

This position is fully remote, permitting all tasks to be completed from any location within the United States. Working hours will align with Central Standard Time. Per Rice policy 440, work arrangements may be subject to change.

Hiring Range

This is a part-time position, and the salary will be commensurate with experience and qualifications. *Exempt (salaried) positions under FLSA are not eligible for overtime.

Minimum Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Art History, Architectural History, English, Architecture, Humanities, or a related field
  • Two years of professional editorial, publication-management, or content-development experience

Preferences

  • Ph.D. or master’s degree in Art History, Architectural History, Architecture, or a closely related academic discipline
  • Five or more years of distinguished editorial, translation, and publication-management experience across academic and cultural publishing contexts, including long-term affiliations with prestigious art and architecture publishers or peer-reviewed scholarly journals
  • Demonstrated university-level teaching or research experience in architectural history and theory
  • Proven record of managing and editing peer-reviewed monographs, essay anthologies, and design publications featuring established and emerging scholars
  • Experience managing translation workflows and editing translated scholarly texts across international cultural contexts

Required Skills & Knowledge

  • Demonstrated command of the principles, terminology, procedures, and best practices of academic editorial content, peer review, and scholarly publishing
  • Extensive experience planning and implementing complex editorial and book-publication projects from conception through publication
  • Superior developmental, structural, line-editing, and proofreading skills for complex scholarly texts
  • Demonstrated ability to synthesize and coordinate materials from multiple scholarly resources and contributors
  • Deep familiarity with architectural scholarship, design theory, and pedagogical frameworks
  • Proven ability to produce highly effective, print-ready work within fixed deadlines and budget constraints
  • Technical proficiency with layout software, word-processing systems, and Adobe Creative Suite
  • Demonstrated ability to apply ingenuity, discretion, and sound judgment in evaluating editorial content and managing external scholarly partnerships

Essential Functions

  • Manage the complete editorial, review, and publication workflow for all Architecture at Rice titles, including book-length studies, thematic anthologies, dossiers, and pamphlets
  • Coordinate the peer-review process for manuscript submissions, serving as the primary liaison among authors, external reviewers, and the Associate Dean for Research and Academic Affairs
  • Research, plan, write, and edit original and complex scholarly texts for both style and substance
  • Review content to be disseminated through print publications and digital imprint platforms
  • Direct prepress and production processes, overseeing the work of freelance copyeditors, indexers, translators, graphic designers, and printers
  • Develop and maintain imprint-specific style guides, editorial guidelines, and workflow standards
  • Advise and collaborate with faculty and contributing international scholars on manuscript development, editorial methods, and publication requirements
  • Establish publication schedules, conduct content-review sessions, and ensure all milestone deadlines are met

Additional Functions

  • Develop and direct Architecture at Rice publication strategy, editorial schedules, and imprint identity to advance Rice Architecture’s scholarship and public reach
  • Actively engage in, cultivate, and research design and editorial strategies that promote the imprint’s publication series
  • Build and maintain long-term professional relationships with graphic designers, print vendors, indexers, and distribution partners
  • Supervise the distribution, rights management, and digital archiving of all imprint publications
  • Perform all other duties as assigned related to the operation and advancement of the Architecture at Rice imprint.

jobs.description:
We're Hiring

Remote Academic Coach & Student Assistant (Part-Time, ~10 hours/week)

The steady partner who helps a high-achieving student master hard material and never miss a deadline.

About the Role

Seamless Assist is hiring a part-time Academic Coach & Student Assistant for a US-based family. You will work one-on-one, online, with their daughter, a motivated high-school student taking classes a year ahead of her grade, including several college-level Advanced Placement (AP) courses. This role reports to the student's parent.

Why This Role Exists

The student doesn't need to be taught from scratch. She is carrying a demanding, writing-heavy course load, and the pressure is in the volume: essays, problem sets, labs, tests and extracurricular deadlines all landing in the same week. This role exists to give her a sharp, organised partner who can keep up with advanced material, help her work through the hardest parts, and keep her schedule under control so nothing slips.

Her Current Classes

  • AP Microeconomics & Macroeconomics
  • AP Biology
  • AP English Language & Composition
  • AP US History
  • Pre-Calculus
  • Spanish 4
  • Journalism & News Production

You don't need to be an expert in every subject. You do need to be strong in several of them, especially writing-heavy courses (AP English Language, AP US History) and at least one of economics, biology or maths.

What You'll Actually Be Doing

Academic coaching (about 70% of your time)

  • Run live one-on-one video sessions to work through homework, problem sets, essays and test preparation.
  • Explain difficult concepts clearly and check that she can explain them back.
  • Review essays and written work for argument, structure, evidence and citations, including AP-style timed essays.
  • Build practice questions, review plans and study guides ahead of tests and the AP exams in May.
  • Learn how each course is taught and graded (syllabi, teacher rubrics, the College Board AP course frameworks) and coach to them.
  • Coach, never complete. Her work must always be her own, in line with her school's academic integrity rules.

Planning and student assistant support (about 30% of your time)

  • Run a weekly planning session: map every class's assignments, tests and deadlines into a shared calendar and task list.
  • Keep her schedule current across classes, activities and appointments, with study time blocked in.
  • Send short reminders before deadlines and confirm work was actually submitted.
  • Track grades and flag early when something starts to slip.
  • Send the parent a short weekly progress update.

Schedule

About 10 hours per week. Sessions fall on weekday afternoons and evenings, US Pacific Time (roughly 3:30–8:30 pm PT), plus one short weekend planning session. You must be reliably available in that window.

Who Will Succeed in This Role

This is a high-trust role with a bright, busy teenager. You will need real subject depth, patience, and the organisational discipline of a strong executive assistant.

  • You explain things clearly and can tell the difference between "I get it" and actually getting it.
  • You are a strong writer and can give specific, useful feedback on an argumentative essay.
  • You run your own life from a calendar and a task list, and you follow up without being asked.
  • You are warm, steady and encouraging, and you hold a high standard.

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree or higher, ideally in education, English, history, economics, biology, mathematics or a related field.
  • At least 2 years of tutoring or teaching high-school or first-year university students.
  • Strong command of the material in several of the subjects listed above.
  • Excellent written and spoken English. Your writing will be assessed during screening.
  • Uses AI tools in your daily work (for example Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini) to build study materials and plan faster, and can teach a student to use them responsibly and within school rules.
  • Able to work US Pacific Time afternoons and evenings, about 10 hours per week.
  • Reliable high-speed internet, a quiet workspace, a webcam and a backup power or internet plan.
  • Willing to complete a national police clearance or background check and provide two professional references before starting.

Nice to have

  • Experience with the US Advanced Placement (AP) programme, or strong AP, SAT, IB or A-Level results of your own.
  • Conversational or better Spanish.
  • Journalism, editing or newsroom experience.
  • Comfortable in Google Workspace (Calendar, Docs, Drive) and a task tool such as Notion or Todoist.

How We Work

Because this role involves working one-on-one with a teenager, clear safeguards apply. All sessions run on a family-owned video account and are recorded. All messages go through a group channel that includes a parent. There is no private messaging or social-media contact with the student. A background check and references are required before the first paid session.

Pay

Competitive hourly pay, paid monthly in USD. Pay varies by country.

How to Apply

Apply with your CV. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to a short AI-led video interview, a written subject task, an interview with the family and a paid trial session.

About Us

SentinelOne is a company at the intersection of AI and security, pioneering a new operating model for cybersecurity. Our AI-native platform unifies protection across endpoint, cloud, identity, data, and AI systems to deliver autonomous detection and response with clarity and speed. By combining real-time analytics, intelligent automation, and a unified data foundation, we reduce noise, simplify complexity, and empower security teams to focus on what truly matters.

Our teams are builders, problem-solvers, and innovators committed to shaping the future of security. If you are excited to solve hard problems alongside talented, mission-driven people, we invite you to help us build a safer future for humanity.

We’re looking for people who are relentlessly curious and committed to continuous learning. AI is reshaping every function across our business, and we enable every team member, regardless of role or level, to build fluency in AI tools and concepts. Those who thrive here actively seek out new solutions, experiment thoughtfully, and apply what they learn to drive better, faster, smarter outcomes.

As a Principal Architect, Strategic Partner Services, you will be tasked with serving as the principal-level technical authority and chief architect for our partner services relationship, setting the technical bar for partner-delivered solutions, advising on the most complex customer architectures, and resolving disagreements that cross product, security, implementation, and commercial boundaries. This partnership brings together SentinelOne's AI-powered security platform and our partners' expertise in managed detection and response, managed SIEM, and incident response, and your judgment will help ensure that what is sold, validated, deployed, and operated can succeed in the customer's environment. This is a hands-on technical governance role, not a general consulting or vendor-management position.

What Will You Do?

Primary responsibilities include:

  • Serve as SentinelOne's principal architecture advisor to the partner, defining design standards and decision rights for complex cross-platform services.
  • Review and approve high-risk solution designs spanning Endpoint, AI SIEM, data pipelines, automation, cloud, and AI security integrations.
  • Lead technical arbitration when SentinelOne, the partner, and customers disagree on scope, design suitability, security controls, or remediation paths.
  • Connect proof-of-value results and exit criteria to practical deployment designs, prerequisites, and acceptance standards.

  • Partner with Product and Engineering to turn recurring implementation or operability issues into prioritized fixes and platform improvements.
  • Coach senior partner architects and help define readiness criteria for advanced partner technical delivery capabilities.
  • Deliver measurable results, including fewer repeat escalations caused by design ambiguity or unsupported implementations; timely, effective resolution of complex technical disputes and critical customer escalations; adoption and effectiveness of architecture patterns, standards, and technical review gates; higher first-time technical acceptance and fewer avoidable implementation defects; and improved partner technical readiness and customer time to value.

What Skills and Knowledge Will You Bring?

Ideal candidates will have:

  • 12 or more years of experience in enterprise security architecture, cybersecurity consulting, platform engineering, or complex technical services.
  • Deep expertise in endpoint security and security operations, with working knowledge of SIEM, data ingestion, cloud, integrations, and response automation.
  • Proven authority in large-scale distributed deployments, complex migrations, and enterprise architecture design reviews.
  • Ability to troubleshoot ambiguous issues across product boundaries using logs, telemetry, APIs, and evidence-based root-cause analysis.
  • Experience making defensible technical decisions in customer- and executive-facing escalations.

Leidos is seeking an experienced Mid-Level Network Security Migration Engineer to support the Army Global Unified Network (AGUN) program.

This is an exciting opportunity to help modernize and secure the Army's global network infrastructure, ensuring reliable and protected communications for critical military operations worldwide.

In this remote role, you'll focus on firewall engineering, network security migrations, security policy management, and secure network connectivity. You'll work with network engineers, cybersecurity professionals, and migration teams to transition legacy security infrastructure into modern, secure enterprise network solutions.

We're looking for a hands-on Network Security Engineer with strong firewall experience, preferably Palo Alto, who can troubleshoot complex network security issues and support large-scale network migrations.


What You'll Do

  • Configure, manage, and troubleshoot enterprise firewalls, including Palo Alto Next-Generation Firewalls (NGFW).
  • Support firewall migrations, security policy conversions, and network security modernization.

  • Work independently on assigned technical tasks while collaborating with senior engineers on complex issues.

  • Understanding of LAN/WAN, TCP/IP, BGP, OSPF, IPSec, VPNs, and Layer 2/Layer 3 routing.

  • Experience troubleshooting firewall policy conflicts, network connectivity, and security performance issues.
  • Familiarity with Palo Alto Panorama, Cisco management platforms, or similar tools.
  • Experience with firewall patching, upgrades, configuration management, and lifecycle maintenance.

We are on the front line of recruitment, enabling organizations to hire smarter and onboard faster. At First Advantage (Nasdaq: FA), people are at the heart of everything we do. From our customers and partners to our greatest advantage — our team members.


Say hello to a rewarding career and come join a leading provider of mission-critical background screening solutions to some of the most recognized Fortune 100 and Global 500 brands.


About First Advantage

First Advantage (NASDAQ: FA) is a leading provider of global software and data in the HR technology industry. Enabled by proprietary technology and AI, First Advantage’s platforms, data, and APIs power comprehensive employment background screening, identity solutions, and verification services.


Headquartered in Atlanta, GA, we have an internationally distributed workforce of about 10,000 employees spanning 17 countries. With a strong emphasis on innovation, automation, and customer success, First Advantage empowers 80,000 organizations to modernize their hiring and onboarding processes on a global scale.


What You'll Do

The Corporate Staff Attorney reports directly to the SVP, Contract Management, and Associate General Counsel and prepares, reviews, and approves a wide range of business contracts for First Advantage. Representing First Advantage's interests, this attorney evaluates contractual risk, works with internal and external teams on contract negotiations, and resolves issues so that both parties can enter into mutually beneficial agreements. The attorney also helps ensure that activities, policies, business practices, and transactions comply with all relevant laws and regulations. The work is complex and has a steep learning curve because it combines commercial contracting with the regulatory framework that governs background screening. We are therefore seeking a candidate who can contribute quickly, and prior background screening industry experience is strongly preferred. Success in this role requires a highly organized individual with excellent attention to detail who can work independently, manage multiple projects, and meet competing deadlines simultaneously.


Responsibilities:

  • Prepare, review, and approve sales and procurement contracts for services, along with related legal documents, to protect the organization's legal and business interests.
  • Work with relevant stakeholders to revise contracts and modify standard terms and conditions to mutually benefit First Advantage and its customers.
  • Represent First Advantage in contract negotiations with external clients and partners; serve as an advocate for the company's business interests.
  • Assist in the revision of standard form contracts and the development of new form contracts that advance the organization's strategic interests in creating repetitive business transactions.
  • Provide analysis and counsel on existing policies and the development of new policies.
  • Apply the Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA), GDPR, and consumer protection requirements when drafting and negotiating contract terms and advise business partners on how those requirements affect First Advantage's agreements and practices.
  • Perform legal research assignments and manage special projects as needed.

What You Will Need to be Successful:

  • JD from an American Bar Association accredited law school.
  • Experience working in a multinational company, including collaborating with colleagues and customers across countries and cultures.
  • 3+ years of corporate contracting experience, with at least 2 years specifically involving sales/procurement of services, or equivalent
  • Prior experience in the background screening or consumer reporting industry strongly preferred, including working knowledge of FCRA, GDPR, and consumer protection laws
  • Active bar license in any of the 50 states
  • Training in and understanding of common business, technical, financial, and legal practices
  • Strong knowledge of contract management principles and guidelines
  • Analytical skills relative to contract information and related matters
  • Ability to evaluate risk, urgency, and prioritize tasks
  • Strong organizational ability and a demonstrated track record of managing urgent projects concurrently
  • Excellent attention to detail and the ability to complete tasks with a high degree of accuracy
  • Proven excellence in written and verbal communication and the ability to convey complex information
  • Demonstrated ability to formulate new ways of doing things in a resourceful way
  • Ability to develop and maintain executive-level relationships
  • Strong negotiation skills
  • Ability to communicate effectively across all levels of the company, while ensuring confidentiality and compliance with set processes and procedures

Why Join Us at First Advantage?

At First Advantage, team members are united around a noble purpose: helping organizations to safeguard their workplaces and manage risk. The company’s culture is shaped by its core values — Authenticity, Curiosity, Integrity, Teamwork, Customer-Inspired — empowering team members to bring their best ideas forward, collaborate across departments, and make a real impact.

  • Medical, Vision, Dental, and supplementary benefit plans, including paid Parental Leave and Bereavement.
  • 401k with an employer match and an Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP).
  • Competitive and flexible Paid Time Off (PTO) and 8 paid company holidays.
  • Volunteer Time Off Policy (VTOP) up to 10 hours a year.

JazzX AI is defining the future of enterprise work—by building AI-native digital workers that actually get the job done.
We believe enterprises don't scale expertise—they lose it. Knowledge stays trapped in individuals, judgment gets applied inconsistently, and the best talent spends time on work that should run itself. We're changing that.
JazzX AI transforms messy enterprise reality into institutional intelligence: governed digital workers that capture expert judgment, make every decision explainable, and continuously improve through real-world execution. We're starting with lending and due-diligence workflows—complex, regulated, high-stakes. From here, we're building the backbone for enterprise intelligence across industries.
This is early-stage, hard, and consequential work. If you want to be part of bringing AI systems to market that actually run in production, handle real complexity, and deliver real outcomes—not demos, not chatbots—JazzX AI is the place.
About SAIGroup :
SAIGroup a private investment firm that has committed $1B to build and scale next-generation, AI-powered enterprise software companies. SAIGroup’s portfolio serves 2,000+ global enterprise customers, generates nearly $800M in annual revenue, and employs 4,000+ people worldwide — providing JazzX AI with long-term capital, deep operating expertise, and access to real-world enterprise scale from day one.

About the role

JazzX AI builds an Enterprise General Intelligence (EGI) platform regulated businesses use to build, govern and run AI agents on their own policies and data. Our customers are in mortgage, commercial lending, healthcare, financial crimes and other regulated domains. We are hiring a Principal Outbound Product Manager / Product Marketing Manager to own how the platform goes to market: how it is positioned, packaged, priced, demonstrated and sold.

This is a senior role sitting between product, engineering, sales, customer success and partners. You will represent the market inside the product team and represent the product in the field. You should be as comfortable presenting to an enterprise’s executive team as you are walking an enterprise architect through an API, and you will work directly with customers from your first weeks.

Key Responsibilities

Positioning and messaging

  • Own positioning, messaging and the product narrative for the platform, tailored to each audience: developers and architects, risk and compliance leaders, business operators, and partners who build on or resell the platform.
  • Maintain a current view of the competitive landscape, including model providers, cloud AI platforms and workflow automation vendors,and turn it into clear differentiation and competitive guidance for the field.

Launches and field enablement

  • Lead go to market for platform releases: launch plans, messaging, content, and readiness across sales, solutions and delivery teams.
  • Build and maintain the core demos, pitch materials, reference architectures and objection handling guidance, and train the field to deliver them.
  • Join strategic customer and prospect conversations as the product expert on architecture, governance, security and business value.

Packaging and pricing

  • Define packaging and SKUs across platform licenses, builder seats and usage-based consumption, segmented by customer size and maturity.
  • Set pricing and discount guidance with Leadership and Sales, model deal economics and margin, and adjust based on win/loss data and customer usage.

Customer and market insight

  • Bring structured customer, win/loss and market feedback into the roadmap, and partner with product managers and engineering on prioritization.

These engagements are execution-heavy, data-driven workstreams with regulatory delivery timelines and require hands-on analytical expertise rather than policy or advisory support. This person will support Transaction Monitoring (TM) model validation, tuning, and optimization activities across four client engagements, including: TM Model Validation and Tuning, Threshold Calibration, and TM Rules Optimization.

This is a remote role in the USA.

Job Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree or international equivalent is required.
  • Demonstrated experience performing Transaction Monitoring model validation and/or tuning.
  • Hands-on experience with ATL / BTL testing.
  • Strong SQL and Python skills for transaction-level data analysis.
  • Experience analyzing alert volumes, thresholds, and false positives.
  • Experience working with bank-owned or bespoke TM systems.
  • Ability to work independently under regulatory delivery timelines.
  • Experience producing evidence-based analytical documentation.
  • Hands-on experience applying network / graph analytics for financial crime (e.g., NetworkX, Neo4j, Quantexa, or similar entity-resolution and graph tools).
  • Experience supporting banks or exchange houses preferred.
  • Exposure to UAE or comparable regulatory environments preferred.
  • Familiarity with model risk management expectations preferred.
  • Comfort engaging directly with clients on technical topics preferred.

Job Responsibilities:

  • Perform Transaction Monitoring model validations, including conceptual soundness assessments, data quality and data lineage testing, model implementation accuracy testing, and outcomes analysis (ATL / BTL testing).
  • Execute TM model tuning and optimization activities, including threshold calibration, alert volume analysis, false positive reduction, and rule effectiveness assessment.
  • Conduct transaction-level data analysis to validate model inputs and outputs and reconcile source data to alerts and cases.
  • Apply network and link analysis to transaction and customer data to identify connected parties, counterparty clusters, and fund-flow patterns indicative of layering, money mule activity, circular or round-tripping transactions, and other typologies that rule-based TM can miss.
  • Use network-derived insights (e.g., shared identifiers, counterparty concentration, centrality and community detection) to identify TM coverage gaps, support customer segmentation, and inform threshold and rule tuning decisions.
  • Support alert investigation and adjudication frameworks, including analysis of alert decisioning logic and investigation workflows.
  • Produce clear, defensible analytical outputs for model validation reports, regulatory submissions, and client walkthroughs.
  • Engage directly with client compliance teams to explain analytical findings and tuning decisions.

jobs.excerpt: The SVP, Head of Value Engineering turns the Sapiens AIP and SaaS proposition into a financial case a CEO, CFO or COO of an insurance carrier will sign.
jobs.description:
The SVP, Head of Value Engineering turns the Sapiens AIP and SaaS proposition into a financial case a CEO, CFO or COO of an insurance carrier will sign. The role owns the value methodology, the business case models and the people who build them, and it carries that case from first conversation through contract to proven realization.

The role adopts the lifecycle model used by Value Advisory teams in the Enterprise Software industry, adapted for insurance. The idea is to run value as one journey: benchmark and diagnose before the deal, build the business case, then track realization after go-live, supported by platforms for benchmarking, business cases and TCO. The team combines external benchmark data with a customer's own process data to size and prioritize opportunities.

  1. Discover: executive interviews and workshops; benchmark the carrier's KPIs against peers to find the value drivers.
  2. Quantify: build the ROI and TCO case, with the carrier's own numbers and agreed assumptions.
  3. Commit: anchor the case in the proposal, contract and program governance.
  4. Realize: with Customer Success, track delivery of benefits after go-live against the original case.
  5. Amplify: convert proven results into references, renewals and expansion.


Reports to: Chief Revenue Officer
Location: Europe or USA, with regular travel to clients and regional sales teams.
Team: Regional Value Engineers and Business Value Advisors, plus a small team for models, benchmarks and tooling.
Key Partners: Sales leadership, Industry Practice Heads, Product, Finance, Customer Success and Marketing

Job Responsibilities

Financial case for the C-level buyer
  • Convert the AIP and SaaS proposition into CFO-grade business cases: ROI, NPV, payback, TCO versus legacy and on-premise, and the shift from capex to opex.
  • Quantify value across expense ratio, speed to market, straight-through processing, claims and servicing efficiency, retention and growth, and risk and compliance.
  • Lead executive interviews and value workshops with CEOs, CFOs, COOs and CIOs of insurers; hold the case up under finance and procurement scrutiny.

Methodology, models and benchmarks
  • Own the Sapiens value framework, model library and assumptions governance, so every case is consistent, auditable and defensible.
  • Build an insurance benchmark and KPI baseline library by line of business and region, and decide the tooling for modeling and tracking.

Pursuit and deal support
  • Embed value engineering in qualification, proposal and negotiation for strategic pursuits; align pricing, packaging and commercial structure to the value case.
  • Partner with Industry Practice Heads, Presales and Sales leadership on pursuit strategy and executive sponsorship.

Value realization
  • With Customer Success and Delivery, define value milestones, track realized benefits post-go-live, and use the results to support renewal and expansion.
  • Convert proven outcomes into quantified references, case studies and analyst proof points.

Leadership and enablement
  • Build and lead a regional team of Value Engineers and Business Value Advisors; train the field on value-based selling and discovery.
  • Give Product and Finance structured feedback on value drivers, pricing and packaging.

Job Requirements

  • 15+ years in value advisory, strategy or management consulting, enterprise software sales or insurance technology, including 5+ years leading value engineering or business-case teams.
  • Proven record, building business cases and financial models that CFOs have accepted for multi-year SaaS and platform investments.
  • Strong finance acumen: ROI, NPV, TCO, cash-flow phasing, and subscription and cloud-transition economics.
  • Insurance domain knowledge across Life, Annuity and P&C operating models; credibility with insurer C-suites.
  • Experience with benchmarking, value-management tooling and post-sale value realization.
  • Executive presence and facilitation skills; able to influence Sales, Product and Finance without direct authority.
  • Bachelor's degree in business, finance or engineering required; MBA or equivalent preferred.

You: You're a natural relationship builder with an entrepreneurial spirit, a strategic mind, and a knack for turning conversations into opportunities. In this role, you'll be PLF's bridge to the business world: building relationships with companies, trade associations, and industry leaders, learning where government overreach is hurting them, and turning those insights into new cases, coalitions, and policy wins.

You’re equally comfortable with a corporate executive, a trade association leader, or a small business owner, and you’re energized by finding creative solutions to the challenges American businesses face. You’re more than a networker: you spot connections and opportunities others miss, build trust from scratch, and find common ground among people with different priorities. You know the best partnerships are mutually beneficial and long-term, so you make the first call, ask good questions, and follow through.

You want to develop strategies and own your projects, not execute someone else’s playbook. You don't wait for opportunities to come to you. You recognize where PLF can make a difference, develop strategies to engage the right people, and take ownership of turning ideas into results. You're comfortable operating independently, navigating ambiguity, and building something from the ground up. Above all, you’re motivated by impact, whether that’s identifying the next Supreme Court case, building industry support for a legal challenge, advancing state or federal policy reform, or introducing PLF to an entirely new audience.

Them: Government agencies, regulators, and lawmakers imposing barriers that keep Americans from building businesses, developing property, creating jobs, and pursuing opportunity. Burdensome permitting, property rights restrictions, occupational licensing, and unchecked administrative power affect businesses and industries across the country.

Us: We fight back. Pacific Legal Foundation is the nation's first and most successful public interest law firm dedicated to vindicating individual liberty, with 18 U.S. Supreme Court victories and more than 200 active cases nationwide. Our Private Sector Partnerships team connects PLF's mission and capabilities with the businesses, industries, and associations that have a stake in limiting government overreach.

Here's what you get to do in this roleReporting to the Private Sector Partnerships Principal on the Outreach Team, you'll expand PLF's engagement with businesses, trade associations, and industry leaders, working closely with our attorneys, policy experts, researchers, and communications, events, and development teams. One day you might help an industry association identify clients for a constitutional challenge; the next, you might build a coalition around state legislation or connect PLF attorneys with businesses affected by government overreach. Success isn't measured in business cards collected. It's measured in relationships built, opportunities uncovered, and results delivered.

Your specific responsibilities will include:

  • Build partnerships with corporations, trade associations, business leaders, and industry stakeholders whose priorities align with PLF's mission.
  • Help identify PLF's next cases by working with attorneys and industry contacts to uncover litigation opportunities and prospective clients.
  • Mobilize private sector support for strategic litigation, amicus briefs, and state and federal legislative reforms.
  • Take initiatives from concept to execution, from targeted outreach campaigns to speaking engagements, webinars, events, research collaborations, and media placements.
  • Represent PLF at industry conferences, legislative gatherings, and association meetings, positioning PLF as a trusted resource.
  • Connect prospective corporate supporters and industry partners with PLF's Development team.
  • Serve as a reliable point of contact for partners, and track outreach and outcomes in Salesforce.

Where you might be coming from

People who thrive in this role have traditionally come from public affairs, government relations, external affairs, strategic partnerships, and corporate partnerships. You might be a Government Relations Manager at a trade association, a Public Affairs or External Affairs Manager at a company, a Strategic Partnerships Manager at a nonprofit or think tank, or an Account Manager running corporate partnerships. Whatever your title, the people who succeed here bring two things: the skills to build relationships that produce real results, and a genuine commitment to PLF's mission of protecting individual liberty, property rights, and constitutional limits on government power.

What we're looking for:

  • 3+ years of experience in government affairs, external relations, public policy, trade associations, corporate affairs, business development, strategic partnerships, public affairs, or a related field.
  • A demonstrated ability to build strong relationships with business leaders, industry associations, policymakers, or other stakeholders.
  • An understanding of how regulation and public policy affect businesses and economic opportunity.
  • A strategic, entrepreneurial mindset and the ability to plan and execute independently.
  • Strong communication skills, a collaborative approach, and the confidence to engage senior stakeholders.
  • Exceptional follow-through and the ability to manage multiple projects and relationships at once.
  • Intellectual curiosity, sound judgment, and eagerness to learn new industries, policy issues, and legal concepts.
  • Genuine enthusiasm for PLF's mission of advancing individual liberty, protecting property rights, and restoring constitutional limits on government power.
  • Willingness to travel up to 30% of the year.

Bonus points for:

  • Existing relationships with corporations, trade associations, or business advocacy groups.
  • Experience with state legislatures, federal policymakers, or regulatory agencies, or with conferences such as ALEC, NCSL, or major trade association gatherings.
  • Experience with property rights, energy, permitting, housing, healthcare, occupational licensing, or administrative regulation.
  • A track record of turning relationships into tangible outcomes, such as legislative support, litigation referrals, or strategic partnerships.
  • Experience with Salesforce or a similar CRM.

You don't need a law degree or litigation background. We're looking for someone who asks good questions, learns quickly, and knows how to bring the right people together.

General Information

PLF has offices in Sacramento, CA, and Arlington, VA, with about half of our staff working remotely across the country. This position is open to both in-office and fully remote candidates, with no preference given based on location.

The salary range is $80,000–$100,000, depending on experience. This is a full-time, permanent position with medical and dental insurance, parental leave, employer-paid retirement savings, generous paid leave, flexible work arrangements, and opportunities for professional development and advancement.

How to apply

If you think you might be a good fit, submit the following application materials:

  • Your resume, including your experience in the liberty movement and relevant professional experience
  • A cover letter explaining why PLF is the place for you, why you want to fight for liberty, and what distinguishes you from typical applicants.

jobs.description:
Treat PeteDME’s MSK Integrated Care patients from home. Our program pairs knee and lumbar bracing with physical therapy and remote therapeutic monitoring, delivered through a network of in-home therapists. Remote visits and monitoring are paid per visit and per call.

How you join
Every therapist on the remote caseload starts with six in-person brace fittings on patients from your own current caseload, so you know the devices you will be coaching patients on. Each fitting is a paid clinical visit — intake, fitting, and follow-up — at a flat fee agreed in writing before your first patient. We give you a one-page screening tool to identify candidates among the patients you already see, and we handle the prescription, benefit verification, and the paperwork.

This is not a sales role. We do not ask you to refer; you treat patients you already see.

After six fittings
Teletherapy patient referrals from PeteDME begin: our patients, work from home, on your schedule, paid per visit and per call.

What you get
• Free specialized training and certification in orthopedic bracing.
• AI-generated SOAP notes — no new EMR to learn.
• Keep your current job. This is additional, independent-contractor work alongside it.
• Flat fees fixed in advance; no part of your pay depends on volume or on referrals.

Requirements

    • Active physical therapist or physical therapist assistant license in the state where you practice.
    • Currently working in home health or another in-home setting.
    • You evaluate and provide treatment.

How to apply

    Complete the short questionnaire. It asks about your license, your setting, and your caseload, and it asks you to acknowledge that teletherapy referrals begin after six fittings. A clinical onboarding specialist will reach out within one business day.

  • Design, implement, migrate, upgrade, troubleshoot, and integrate ArcGIS Enterprise deployments, while monitoring and optimizing performance.

Skills and Requirements of a successful candidate should have the following, but are not limited to:

  • Experience working with state government agencies (e.g., state DOTs, natural resource, or environmental agencies) and navigating public-sector IT, security, and procurement requirements preferred.

jobs.title: Client Support Analyst, EPIC Loan Systems
jobs.excerpt: We are excited to speak to you about this opportunity.
jobs.description:
We are excited to speak to you about this opportunity. If you are interested in joining our growing team, please apply to this link directly.

Who we are

At Aquila, we invest in category-defining B2B/B2G software companies globally, acting as a thought-partner, striving for the success of our companies in the long term. We are a well-managed, profitable company that operates like a startup with the financial backing of a parent company. For our people, this means limitless possibilities.

We are unapologetically unique, pivoting to respond to the needs of the multiple markets we operate in. We have ambitious goals, and we are looking for genuine contributors with integrity, energy, flexibility, and loyalty. We are investing in building future leaders who can take an idea and make things happen.

About EPIC Loan Systems

EPIC Loan Systems is a specialized financial technology company providing lending software solutions to businesses in the lending industry. EPIC has been part of Aquila since 2018, providing specialized lending software that helps clients manage their operations, supported by a team committed to solving problems and building lasting relationships.

Its core product is a Loan Management System that helps lenders manage their end-to-end lending operations, from loan processing and administration to reporting and data management.

The company focuses on simplifying complex lending processes, improving operational efficiency, and building long-term relationships with its clients. As part of Aquila and the broader Constellation Software group, EPIC combines the agility of a specialized software business with the support and resources of an established global organization.

Who we need

Reporting to the Client Support Lead, we are hiring a Client Support Analyst. As part of a small, collaborative team, you will play a key role in shaping the client experience, combining technical curiosity with thoughtful, responsive support. You will look beyond the immediate issue to uncover its root cause, collaborate directly with developers, and see challenges through to resolution. Your work will help clients feel heard, build confidence in the solutions we provide, and strengthen the relationships that set our service apart.

This is a fully remote role open to candidates across the Canada, with working hours of 8:30 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. Eastern Time.

What’s in it for you

Make a meaningful difference. You will go beyond resolving tickets to become a trusted partner to clients who rely on EPIC Loan Systems to manage their lending operations. You will build relationships, understand their challenges, and help them move forward with confidence. Your follow-through and problem-solving will directly impact their experience and their ability to use the software effectively.

Turn complex challenges into better solutions. You will have the opportunity to dig deeper, ask questions, and uncover what is really happening when something does not work as expected. Working closely with clients and developers, you will see issues through to resolution and contribute insights that can prevent recurring problems and improve the experience for other clients. You will have the satisfaction of knowing your work makes a difference beyond the individual issue.

Build your expertise. You will join a small team where your contributions are visible, your ideas are welcome, and you can take meaningful ownership of your work. You will develop specialized knowledge of lending technology, strengthen your technical and client relationship skills, and gain exposure to different parts of the business. As part of Aquila and the broader Constellation Software network, you will also have access to learning opportunities and potential career paths beyond client support.

As our new Client Support Analyst, you will

  • Build trusted client relationships. You will be a reliable point of contact for clients, responding to questions and concerns primarily through email, with phone and messaging support as needed. You will take the time to understand what clients are experiencing, communicate clearly and empathetically, and keep them informed as you work toward a resolution.

  • Investigate and resolve complex issues. You will look beyond the initial request to understand the underlying problem, reproduce issues, and identify possible causes. You will use your technical curiosity, available resources, and collaboration with colleagues to find practical solutions, escalating when needed while maintaining ownership of the client experience.

  • Connect clients with the people who can help. You will work closely with the development team and other internal partners to investigate technical challenges, share relevant information, and move issues toward resolution. You will translate client concerns into clear, actionable details and explain technical findings in language clients can understand.

  • Turn individual solutions into lasting improvements. You will accurately document investigations, resolutions, and client interactions, helping the team build knowledge and identify recurring issues. You will share observations and client feedback that can improve troubleshooting, support practices, and the overall client experience.

  • Take ownership in a collaborative team. You will manage and prioritize your support requests, follow through on commitments, and proactively communicate progress and potential roadblocks. You will contribute to a small team where sharing knowledge, asking for help, and supporting one another are essential to delivering consistent client service.

  • Support a reliable client experience. You will assist with scheduled software releases and occasional after-hours support to help clients navigate changes or unexpected issues. You will bring flexibility, attention to detail, and a commitment to keeping clients informed and supported.

You bring

  • The client support experience. You have experience supporting customers or clients, ideally in a software or technology environment. You know how to listen carefully, ask thoughtful questions, and guide people through challenges while creating a positive experience.

  • The investigative mindset. You enjoy figuring out how things work and getting to the root of a problem. You can assess information, test possible explanations, and work through unfamiliar challenges systematically rather than relying on quick assumptions.

  • The technical aptitude. You are comfortable learning new software, navigating digital tools, and troubleshooting technical issues. You can document findings clearly and communicate effectively with technical colleagues. Experience supporting SaaS platforms or financial technology is an asset, but you do not need to be a developer to succeed in this role.

  • The communication skills. You can explain complex information in clear, accessible language and adapt your approach to different audiences. You bring empathy and patience to challenging conversations and keep clients informed, even when an issue takes time to resolve.

  • The ownership and organization. You can manage multiple requests, assess priorities, and maintain accurate records of your work. You follow through on commitments, recognize when to escalate, and proactively communicate updates and potential roadblocks.

  • The collaborative approach. You are comfortable working independently in a remote environment while staying connected to your team. You welcome feedback, share knowledge, and ask for help when it leads to a better outcome for the client.

  • The flexibility. You can occasionally support scheduled evening software releases and participate in after-hours or weekend on-call coverage when required. You understand the importance of being available to help when clients need additional support.

Why join?

EPIC Loan Systems and Aquila are part of Constellation Software Inc., one of Canada's largest and most successful software companies and its most successful technology stock over the last 10 years [TSE: CSU].

Our entrepreneurial culture, lean environment, and people come together to form a dynamic organization where purpose drives our growth. This is a place where high performance and hard work are rewarded, where leaders are grown, and where the best ideas win. With the autonomy to be creative and curious, we collaborate and iterate to achieve real impact in the communities we support.

We spend our days asking questions and challenging the status quo, manipulating our structure, roles, and internal operations in order to stay ahead in a competitive landscape.

If you share our growth mindset, relationship-focused approach, and high moral fibre, you will thrive at Aquila.

Compensation

At EPIC Loan Systems and Aquila, we believe compensation should be transparent, fair, and reflective of both experience and impact.

Compensation is determined based on skills, experience, and the scope and complexity of the role. We value open conversations about compensation and are happy to discuss our approach at any stage of the hiring process.

Apply now.

Diversity and inclusion are not mere words on paper to us. We welcome and appreciate candidates with a range of backgrounds and experiences. If you have most of the qualifications we are seeking, and want to play an integral role in our success, apply to express your interest.

What you can expect from our interview process:

  • A virtual interview with a Talent Advisor to discuss your interest in joining the company and in the role. The conversation will be recorded using BrightHire, an AI-powered video interview tool. More details will be shared when you are invited to interview.

  • A virtual interview with the Client Support Lead and a team member to explore your approach to client relationships, technical troubleshooting, problem-solving, and managing competing priorities.

  • A final virtual interview with the General Manager to discuss your working style, collaboration, and alignment with the team’s approach to client service. You will have the opportunity to learn more about the role and ask questions.

Aquila and EPIC Loan Systems promote equal employment opportunities for all. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, colour, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, disability, national origin, veteran status, marital status or any other basis covered by appropriate law. All employment decisions are made based on qualifications, merit, and business needs. We welcome and encourage applications from people with disabilities and accommodations are available on request.

We are excited to speak to you about this opportunity. If you are interested in joining our growing team, please apply to this link directly.

Partner Marketing Manager

Remote, North America

As our Partner Marketing Manager, you’ll own marketing to, with, and through our partners, building on an established partner strategy. You’ll work closely with our partnerships and marketing teams to bring joint solutions to market, build relationships across our ecosystem, and help partner sellers understand where GrowthLoop fits and when to bring us into a customer conversation. This is a hands-on role: you’ll shape the plan and drive the details that deliver results.

What You'll Do

  • Own partner event marketing from planning through follow-up. Turn conferences and joint events into opportunities to reach the right buyers, deepen partner relationships, and create sales conversations.
  • Lead co-branded product launches and customer announcements, coordinating the joint story, partner quotes and approvals, content, and promotion.
  • Build marketing relationships with priority technology, cloud, and advisory partners. Develop joint campaigns that support shared sales priorities and give partners a reason to introduce GrowthLoop to their customers.
  • Help sellers at our strategic partners understand, trust, and recommend GrowthLoop through relevant content, enablement, and opportunities to engage with our team.
  • Bring key partner marketing opportunities into GrowthLoop’s broader quarterly marketing plan. Coordinate with partnerships, sales, marketing, and partner teams to deliver joint initiatives with clear owners, timelines, and goals.
  • Proactively involve strategic partners in our major marketing announcements by securing endorsements and/or social media amplification and coordinating with content and product marketing.
  • Work with content and product marketing to create partner-targeted content and sales materials, including solution one-pagers, decks, and joint customer stories.
  • Collaborate with content marketing on co-branded content, such as drafting guest blog posts and lead generation assets (eBooks, whitepapers).
  • Keep external partner listings and the partnerships sections of our website up to date.
  • Run partner campaigns in HubSpot, including audience lists, campaign setup, lead capture, routing, and reporting, so engagement turns into timely sales follow-up.
  • Work with sales to track partner engagement, event follow-up, and sales opportunities generated or supported by partner programs. Use the results to improve programs and decide where to focus next.
  • Regularly analyze and report on partner engagement and results of partner marketing initiatives.

What You Bring

  • 4–6 years of relevant partner marketing experience in enterprise B2B.
  • Experience running partner campaigns, joint launches, and event marketing, including lead capture and sales follow-up. You can explain what you owned and how you measured the results.
  • Strong relationship-building skills. You can earn a partner’s trust, find a shared opportunity, and get commitments, content, and approvals across the finish line.
  • Clear writing and messaging skills, with the ability to turn a joint solution into a story buyers and partner sellers understand. You’re comfortable creating content, collateral, and presentations.
  • Strong project management and follow-through. You can coordinate multiple teams, manage competing deadlines, and keep work moving when priorities change.
  • You’ve run partner marketing programs that led to customer introductions or sales conversations, and can explain what worked and how you measured it.
  • Hands-on experience with HubSpot or a similar marketing automation platform. You’re comfortable setting up campaigns, managing lists and workflows, and tracking results yourself.

About GrowthLoop

GrowthLoop built the first composable CDP, helping marketers leverage live, first-party data from their cloud warehouse to launch highly targeted campaigns. That composable foundation gave way to the Compound Marketing Engine, an evolution of the composable CDP that drives compound growth by using agentic AI to accelerate the marketing cycle.

Now, we’re building what comes next: an agentic system that uses causality data to find the actions that actually improve customer outcomes and gets smarter with every campaign cycle.

Founder-led, we’re partnering with the world’s most innovative brands to close the loop between people, data, and AI. Enterprise marketing teams at Google, Costco, Ford, and Whirlpool (to name a few) choose GrowthLoop to launch smarter, more personalized marketing programs that compound growth with every campaign.

About You

You’re a builder who enjoys turning a shared idea into something real, whether it’s a partner event, a joint launch, or a campaign that opens doors. You take ownership from planning through follow-up, bring clarity when priorities shift, and care about the details that make the work successful. You build trust by listening, communicating directly and kindly, and doing what you say you’ll do. You’re curious about our partners, our customers, and how to do the work better, including using new tools thoughtfully. You pitch in where needed, make the people around you better, and measure success by what the team and our partners achieve together.

What We Offer

The on-target earnings range for this role is USD $125,000–$135,000. Total compensation includes equity.

Final base salary decisions will be based on a variety of non-discriminatory factors unique to each candidate, such as the individual’s skill set, location, depth of experience, and qualifications.

Rewards

  • Opportunities for career progression and dynamic collaboration across teams
  • Equity incentives for employees making an impact

Flexible Work Style

Competitive Benefits

Learn and Grow

Description:

Purpose

Health Informatics (HI) is the specialty that integrates health care science, computer science, and information science to manage and communicate data, information,knowledgeand wisdom in clinical practice across the care continuum. Health informaticsfacilitatesthe integration of data, information,knowledgeand wisdom to support operations, in their decision-making and adoption of workflow in all roles and settings. This support is accomplished with information structures, information processes, and information technology.

The goal of informatics is to improve the health of populations, communities, families, and individuals byoptimizinginformation management and communication. Job Title: Provider Credentialing Specialist
Primary Location: 100% Remote

This position exists to support hands-on payer credentialing and provider enrollment, with a strong focus on behavioral health providers. The Credentialing Specialist will also play a key role in cleansing and validating credentialing data as the organization transitions to MD-Staff. We're looking for someone who has personally done the work, not just overseen or coordinated it. Contractors may be considered for permanent openings as opportunities arise.

What You Bring to the Role. (Ideal Experience)

  • 2+ years of direct, hands-on provider credentialing and/or payer enrollment experience.
  • Proven ability to independently manage payer enrollment end to end: preparing and submitting applications, tracking payer responses, resolving deficiencies, and maintaining provider participation records.
  • Experience credentialing and enrolling behavioral health providers (LCSWs, LPCs, psychologists, psychiatrists, etc.) and working within payer-specific requirements is strongly preferred.
  • Hands-on experience with Cactus and/or MD-Staff is strongly preferred; experience with both is ideal.
  • Experience with credentialing data cleansing, validation, reconciliation, and resolving duplicate or incomplete records, ideally as part of a system transition.
  • Working knowledge of initial credentialing, recredentialing, primary source verification, NPDB queries, CAQH profile maintenance and re-attestation, and Medicare/Medicaid revalidations.
  • Experience with CAQH and payer portals; strong computer and data-entry skills.
  • Strong attention to detail, organization, and the ability to manage a workload independently.
  • Clear, professional communication with providers, practices, payers, and internal teams, and a firm commitment to confidentiality.
  • High school diploma or GED required; associate degree preferred.
  • CPCS certification preferred.

  • Process and track initial payer credentialing, provider enrollment, recredentialing, and revalidation applications for participating providers.
  • Support behavioral health provider credentialing and enrollment, including collecting and reviewing payer-required documentation.
  • Prepare, assemble, review, and quality-check provider applications, following up with providers and payers to resolve missing or inconsistent information.
  • Conduct credential verifications and mandated queries in line with organizational policy and payer requirements.
  • Enter, maintain, and update provider information in credentialing databases, CAQH, and payer systems.

Workforce & Systems Integration Manager

Georgia Center for Opportunity (GCO) is an independent, non-partisan policy research organization that develops solutions leading to social and economic opportunity in the state of Georgia and beyond. Our vision is to make vibrant communities where everyone can achieve their potential.

Our mission is to empower families to flourish across generations. We advance solutions that increase opportunity and create durable pathways to prosperity for Georgia’s families. To achieve our mission, we research ways to help remove barriers to opportunity in each of these pathways, promote our solutions to policymakers and the public, and help effective and innovative social enterprises deliver results in their communities. Our ultimate goal is to see every Georgian who is willing to seize the opportunities presented to them living a life that can be characterized as truly flourishing.

GCO is poised for growth, with an office in Peachtree Corners and programs in Gwinnett County and Columbus, Georgia, GCO is a fast-paced, entrepreneurial, and highly collaborative environment. The Workforce & Systems Integration Manager must be a self-starter, an independent worker, and a team player in this fast-growing organization.

This role reports to the Vice President of Program Strategy & Impact. The Workforce and Systems Integration Manager develops and manages the external partnerships, workforce strategies, and community resource networks that help participants and graduates achieve lasting family stability and economic mobility. Serving as the bridge between program delivery and the broader workforce ecosystem, this role ensures participants have coordinated access to education, financial literacy, employment opportunities, and other critical resources that support long-term flourishing.

This role identifies systemic barriers that limit graduate success and works collaboratively to reduce friction, improve alignment, and strengthen outcomes. Working throughout Georgia across both program areas, the manager identifies, cultivates and maintains relationships with workforce organizations, educational institutions, employers, public agencies, and/or community partners to create seamless pathways from learning to career advancement, employment, and sustained family well-being.

The Workforce and Systems Integration Manager also coordinates with the Program Insight & Impact Manager to utilize participant feedback to inform improvements to both programs and external systems by cultivating strategically targeted partnerships and leveraging graduate outcome data to support advancement, retention, wage growth, and continued opportunity throughout the partner network.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and maintain relationships with workforce boards, educational institutions, vocational training providers, public agencies, and community organizations.
  • Build and steward workforce focused partnerships that create meaningful career pathways, advancement opportunities, and family-sustaining employment directly contributing to improved retention, wage growth, and family stability.
  • Collaborate with partners to understand workforce needs and translate those insights into program improvements.
  • Align external systems to reduce barriers and improve graduate access to opportunities across all program areas.
  • Communicate proactively to ensure graduates have coordinated access through these targeted partnerships to resources that promote economic mobility and family flourishing.
  • Support strategies that minimize the impact of benefits cliffs and other systemic barriers to advancement.
  • Collaborate with internal teams to ensure external partnerships strengthen program effectiveness and participant outcomes.
  • Represent the organization within workforce and community networks to advance the mission of economic mobility and family stability.

jobs.title: Ingénieure ou Ingénieur, Sécurité physique
jobs.excerpt: Vous vous joindrez à une équipe spécialisée qui conçoit des systèmes de sécurité électronique intégrés pour des projets complexes au Canada et aux États-Unis.
jobs.description:
Vous vous joindrez à une équipe spécialisée qui conçoit des systèmes de sécurité électronique intégrés pour des projets complexes au Canada et aux États-Unis. Le poste s’adresse à une ingénieure ou à un ingénieur comptant de 4 à 10 années d’expérience, capable de prendre en charge des volets techniques définis, de la définition des besoins jusqu’au soutien à la construction et à la mise en service.

Vous pourrez travailler à partir du bureau Stantec de votre choix, en télétravail à temps plein ou en combinant librement les journées au bureau et en télétravail, selon les modalités applicables au poste.

Des projets qui comptent

Vous travaillerez sur des projets où votre expertise servira à protéger les personnes, les biens et les infrastructures, notamment dans les secteurs suivants :

  • les installations gouvernementales fédérales, provinciales et municipales, la défense, les ambassades et les postes frontaliers;

  • la justice et la sécurité publique : palais de justice, établissements de détention et installations policières;

  • les infrastructures de transport, d’énergie (électricité et gaz naturel), d’eau et autres services essentiels, y compris les installations maritimes comme les ports et les écluses;

  • les centres de données, centres de contrôle, installations de radiotélédiffusion et environnements technologiques critiques;

  • les établissements de santé et d’enseignement ainsi que les installations de recherche et développement;

  • les installations industrielles, minières, aéronautiques et commerciales.

Votre rôle

Sous la direction d’un ingénieur principal ou du responsable de discipline, vous prendrez en charge des volets techniques définis et agirez comme interlocuteur technique auprès du client et des autres disciplines du projet. Selon votre niveau d’expérience et votre degré d’autonomie, vous pourrez aussi prendre en charge des mandats de plus petite envergure. Vous transformerez les objectifs de sécurité, les contraintes d’exploitation et les résultats d’évaluations des risques en solutions d’ingénierie cohérentes, réalisables et documentées.

Orientations techniques et conseils au client

  • Analyser les besoins fonctionnels et techniques à partir des exigences du client, des recommandations issues d’évaluations des risques et des menaces, des études de sécurité et des programmes fonctionnels et techniques.

  • Définir, avec l’ingénieur principal, les concepts de sécurité, les critères de performance, les stratégies d’intégration et les limites de portée entre les disciplines.

  • Préparer les options, les risques, les coûts et les compromis techniques à présenter aux décideurs, et formuler des recommandations claires.

Conception de systèmes de sécurité intégrés

  • Concevoir, planifier et documenter des solutions de contrôle d’accès, de détection d’intrusion, de vidéosurveillance, d’intercommunication, de gestion des clés, de gestion des visiteurs et d’autres applications spécialisées.

  • Développer les interfaces entre les sous-systèmes de sécurité, les systèmes de bâtiment, les réseaux de télécommunications et les outils d’exploitation.

  • Intégrer, lorsque requis, les contrôles de véhicules et de piétons, les solutions biométriques et les technologies émergentes en fonction du besoin réel et du contexte d’utilisation.

  • Effectuer des relevés de sites existants, valider les contraintes et établir des concepts adaptés aux opérations, aux infrastructures et aux étapes de réalisation.

Espaces opérationnels et infrastructures associées

  • Concevoir, en collaboration avec les autres disciplines, les centres de contrôle des opérations, postes de garde, salles d’équipements et postes de travail en tenant compte de l’ergonomie, des flux opérationnels, de la continuité des opérations et de la maintenabilité.

  • Coordonner les besoins en câblage, télécommunications, alimentation normale et de secours, locaux techniques, interfaces de portes et résilience des systèmes, avec l’appui de nos équipes internes spécialisées en infrastructures de télécommunications, électricité, structure, mécanique et architecture.

Documents d’ingénierie et assurance qualité

  • Préparer et réviser les rapports de conception, schémas de zonage, diagrammes fonctionnels, schémas-blocs, plans, devis, cahiers des charges, estimations budgétaires et documents d’appel d’offres.

  • Coordonner le travail de production avec les collègues et les techniciens, et veiller à la qualité, à la cohérence et à la traçabilité des livrables.

  • Produire les documents d’ingénierie et, lorsque requis, les signer et les sceller pour les volets dont vous avez la responsabilité, conformément aux règles de l’Ordre des ingénieurs du Québec et aux exigences applicables au projet.

  • Appliquer les codes, normes, exigences réglementaires et critères propres à la clientèle.

Appels d’offres, construction et mise en service

  • Soutenir les clients durant les appels d’offres, analyser les soumissions et les écarts techniques, et formuler des recommandations.

  • Répondre aux demandes d’information, examiner les dessins d’atelier et soutenir l’équipe de surveillance pendant la construction.

  • Réaliser des inspections et des essais fonctionnels, participer aux activités de mise en service et assurer le suivi de la résolution des déficiences, selon la portée du mandat.

  • Maintenir des relations de travail efficaces avec les clients, les équipes de projet, les entrepreneurs et les fournisseurs

jobs.description:
Team Associate I

Office of Student Affairs

Non Exempt, Contingent II, Full Time, Pay Grade 007

Job location: Remote

JOB SUMMARY

Under direct supervision, performs the full range of multi-functional clerical/operational duties as part of an institutionally defined self-directed team. Work involves a broad variety of specialized tasks and methods consistent with a clearly defined team-based work environment and continuous quality improvement objectives. Participates in providing guidance and instruction to Team Assistants.


PRIMARY DUTIES

  • Receives and directs incoming calls and visitors. Responds to general inquiries requiring research or interpretation of relevant departmental policies and procedures. Makes referrals to other team members or teams as appropriate.
  • Maintains manual and automated record-keeping and filing systems. Codes, sorts, processes, and files the full range of team documents and materials. Assembles, enters, edits, and retrieves data and records.
  • Operates office equipment such as multi-line telephones, personal computers, typewriters, facsimile machines, and photocopiers.
  • Prepares worksheets, tables, correspondence, and standard reports. Participates in the preparation and review of statistical and other reports for completeness and accuracy.
  • Identifies and resolves clerical process problems impacting productivity and quality. Participates in developing new or revised processes.
  • Assists in planning and coordinating team clerical work. Coordinates work flow of assigned clerical tasks or function.

Note: The intent of this list of primary duties is to provide a representative summary of the major duties and responsibilities of this job. Incumbents perform other related duties assigned. Specific duties and responsibilities may vary based upon departmental needs.

ADDITIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Conduct calls to students using the Five 9 telephony system and dialer and follow standard operating procedures for each call.
  • Respond to student and staff emails collaboratively and with excellent internal and external customer service.
  • Provide excellent customer service in speaking with students and identifying any challenges that the student had that prevented them from finishing their program.
  • Encourage and motivate students to overcome challenges to finish their program and reach their goals.
  • Coordinate the warm transfer and hand off, of students to a Success Coach, Financial Solutions Advisor, or other department to work with the student to resolve issues or enroll into a course.
  • Verify and capture student information and document completely in the CRM. Submit cases for any needed resolution or issue.
  • Provide support and resolution to enrollment inquiries made by phone or through email, cases, in person, chat and other established means of communication.
  • Other duties as assigned to support University wide initiatives such as training, attending meetings and presenting ideas to colleagues or guests will also be required.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Education: High School Diploma or GED.

Experience: Three years in clerical work.


REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE/SKILLS/ABILITIES

  • General knowledge of team office practices, procedures, and equipment; of grammar, spelling, and punctuation.
  • Skill in independently performing a broad range of team clerical and operational tasks including computer data entry, basic arithmetic calculations and compilation of statistical data; completion of standard forms, creation and maintenance of paper and computer files, preparation of standard reports and data summaries, and responding to requests for general information.
  • Skill in effective telephone usage.
  • Ability to work effectively in a self-directed team-based work environment; to understand and apply team quality and performance standards.
  • Ability to plan and independently perform specialized clerical tasks; operate all team office equipment; to communicate both orally and in writing; to follow oral and written procedures and processes; to establish and maintain effective work relationships both within and outside the team; to operate personal computers and software; to understand and interpret department policies and procedures; to provide guidance and instruction to Team Assistants.

All submissions should include a cover letter and resume.
