jobs.title: Lead Data Architect – Data & Analytics Platforms
jobs.excerpt: Purpose of the role: The Role •This is Capita's senior technical authority for enterprise data platforms.
jobs.description:
Purpose of the role:

The Role
•This is Capita's senior technical authority for enterprise data platforms. It is emphatically not an advisory architect role: you will set the architecture, make the difficult technical decisions, and then get hands-on with engineers to make it work.
•You will own our enterprise data platform architecture, particularly across Databricks and Snowflake, and lead the platform engineering capability around it, combining deep technical architecture capability, platform ownership and engineering leadership in one role.
•You will act as the senior technical decision-maker for data, with the authority to challenge or veto inappropriate designs through our integration/data design authority, bringing consistency to security and platform decisions across the estate.
•There is no management layer above you dedicated to this domain. You will operate as the senior technical authority for data and analytics, with a direct line to the Director of AI and Technology Engineering for decisions that cross domain boundaries.
Who We're Looking For
We need someone who can operate at both ends of the spectrum:
Enterprise authority → architecture → detailed design → engineering implementation
You might spend one morning explaining Capita's data platform strategy to a client or challenging a proposed architecture at design authority, and the afternoon sitting with engineers working through why a Databricks pipeline, Snowflake model, security design or integration pattern isn't working. That combination of technical depth and authority is what this role is about.

Job title:

Lead Data Architect – Data & Analytics Platforms

Job Description:

What you'll be doing:


Mandate & Scope:

You own, directly:

  • Enterprise data platform architecture across Databricks and Snowflake — design patterns, data modelling, pipeline architecture, security models, governance, and cost/performance optimisation
  • Leadership of the data platform engineering capability, including technical direction, engineering standards and the quality of what the team builds
  • Reference architectures, reusable patterns, standards and guardrails that allow delivery teams to self-serve
  • Data decisions at the integration/data design authority, including the authority to challenge or veto designs that are inappropriate, insecure or inconsistent with platform standards
  • Architectural input into presales, bids and client proposals, ensuring proposed solutions are technically sound and deliverable
  • Delivery accountability for data platform workstreams; you are responsible for designs actually shipping, not just for producing them

You coordinate on, jointly:

  • How data, AI, integration and other enterprise platforms fit together into coherent solutions across the Engineering Studio and AI Catalyst ecosystem
  • Integration points with other platforms (integration and APIs, identity and security, networking, cloud infrastructure, CI/CD, application and AI platforms) owned by other technical leads
  • Shared infrastructure costs and cross-platform dependencies
  • Any design decision where a change on your platform has a material impact on another

Escalation: where you and another platform owner can't reach agreement on a shared decision, it comes to the Director of AI and Technology Engineering to resolve. You're expected to flag these early rather than let them stall.

Delivery

This role carries explicit delivery accountability, not just design authority. You will:

  • Own the technical roadmap and translate it into a deliverable plan
  • Be accountable for data platform workstreams landing on time and to spec, not just for the quality of the designs
  • Identify and manage delivery risk on your workstreams and escalate early when scope, resourcing, or dependencies threaten delivery

Key Responsibilities:

Architecture and technical authority

  • Design and evolve our enterprise data platform architecture across Databricks and Snowflake, including lakehouse/warehouse structure, ingestion, transformation, governance, security and consumption layers
  • Design complex enterprise data architectures and data models, and explain both the detail and the rationale behind them to engineers, architects and stakeholders

jobs.title: 2027 Summer Associate (1L)
jobs.excerpt: 2027 Summer Associate Program (1L) Remote-first · Opportunity to work out of our New York or San Francisco office · 10-week program The practice of law is being redefined in the AI era, and we’re looking for first-year law students who want to learn it from the firm doing the redefining.
jobs.description:
2027 Summer Associate Program (1L)

Remote-first · Opportunity to work out of our New York or San Francisco office · 10-week program

The practice of law is being redefined in the AI era, and we’re looking for first-year law students who want to learn it from the firm doing the redefining. As a Summer Associate at General Legal, you won’t just watch how attorneys work. You’ll contribute to live client matters alongside seasoned attorneys, master the AI-native workflows that are reshaping how legal work gets done, and build the judgment that no tool can replace. If you want to start your career at the forefront of where the profession is headed, we’d like to meet you.

About General Legal

General Legal is an AI-native law firm built to deliver high-quality legal work faster and more predictably than traditional firms. We combine experienced, U.S.-barred attorneys with AI-native workflows to handle drafting, review, and negotiation end to end, without billable hours or a bloated process.

We operate like a startup because we are one. That means modern tooling, outcome-based pricing, remote-friendly work, and meaningful ownership for the people doing the work. By using AI to handle the routine parts of legal work, we give our attorneys the space to focus on judgment, negotiation, and advising over 600 clients on what actually matters.

We’re building a modern law firm where great lawyers can do their best work, and help reshape how legal services are delivered.

Our Values

General Legal is one team with one set of values:

  • Make Clients the Heroes. Our clients’ legal needs are urgent to them, so they’re urgent to us. We deliver fast, reliable, and exceptional outcomes, and every client deadline is our deadline.
  • Continuously Compound. We use technology to do more with less, so everyone’s work goes further, faster, and better.
  • Kind and Candid. We operate as one team without egos, sharing knowledge, giving credit generously, and celebrating wins.
  • Failure is data. We communicate openly, set clear expectations, give direct feedback, and own our mistakes.

About the Program

Our 10-week Summer Associate Program gives a small class of law students who have completed their first year of law school a realistic view of practicing at General Legal. You’ll work on active client matters for high-growth technology companies and the investors who back them, with every assignment supervised by a licensed attorney.

You’ll also learn how our attorneys use AI-native workflows to move faster and more consistently than a traditional firm, and you’ll get to know the people behind that work: attorneys across our practices, plus the product, engineering, and client teams who build the platform with them.

By the end of the summer, you’ll know what it’s like to be an attorney here, and we’ll know what it’s like to work with you.

Every summer associate works under the supervision of experienced attorneys, receives regular feedback on substantive assignments, and has formal midpoint and end-of-summer reviews.

What You’ll Do

  • Work on live client matters under the supervision of licensed attorneys in our transactional practice, including drafting, reviewing, and redlining commercial agreements, supporting due diligence, researching legal issues, and preparing work product for attorney review before anything reaches a client.
  • Learn from attorneys directly. Join client calls and internal working sessions where appropriate, see how negotiations are run, and get timely feedback on substantive assignments.
  • Leverage AI tools as a genuine force multiplier. Use the firm’s AI legal technology daily to raise the quality of your work and compress timelines, and share what you learn about where the tools help and where they don’t.
  • Build your skills through training. Join the attorney-led trainings at our Weekly Attorney Call, plus summer-specific workshops on drafting, negotiation, and client communication.
  • Build relationships across the firm. Meet attorneys through weekly one-on-ones, small-group practice spotlights on recent deals and matters, and a mid-summer cohort meetup in our New York or San Francisco office.
  • Contribute beyond your lane. Work on a capstone project, on your own or with a fellow summer associate, that improves a real GL playbook, template, or workflow, with an opportunity to present your work to the firm at the end of the summer.

What We’re Looking For

Background & Experience

  • First-year J.D. candidate in good standing at an ABA-accredited law school, with an expected graduation date of May/June 2029
  • Strong academic record and excellent legal research and writing skills
  • Interest in transactional practice, technology, startups, or the business of law
  • Meaningful prior work experience, leadership, or extracurricular involvement

How You Work

  • You are fast and good, and working hard to improve
  • You’re already experimenting with AI tools, and you use them critically: to sharpen your analysis and accelerate your learning, not to replace your own thinking
  • You produce clean, careful work product and check your own work before you hand it off
  • You communicate directly: clear questions, clear recommendations, no filler
  • You take initiative and ask for feedback, and you know when to loop people in
  • You build relationships and earn trust with non-lawyers, including business and product people

Bonus Points

  • You’ve worked at a startup, or in product, engineering, finance, or another business role
  • You’ve built or improved a process, tool, or template from scratch
  • You have a practice area or industry you’d love to go deep on

The Structure

This is a remote-first program running from early June through early/mid-August 2027. The summer starts with a virtual (or in-person, depending on your location) kickoff week of orientation, training, and introductions to the team. We otherwise trust you to do your best work from wherever you do your best work, and you’re welcome to work out of our New York or San Francisco office or meet staff in Washington D.C., if you’re nearby.

Program Arc. After kickoff, you’ll spend the summer in two practice blocks, working on a range of transactional matters with different attorneys based on your interests and attorney capacity. Along the way, you’ll have a midpoint review, shadow client calls, take part in a mock negotiation, and join a cohort meetup. The summer wraps up with capstone presentations and final reviews.

Hours & Responsiveness. Responsiveness is core to how we serve clients. You’ll set your core working hours with your supervising attorney at the start of the summer. During those hours, you’re expected to be available and responsive to your supervising attorney and the teams you’re working with: acknowledging assignments promptly, communicating realistic timelines, and flagging questions, blockers, or changes in availability early.

Compensation

  • $30 - $35 per hour, paid semi-monthly

Why This Program

Most summer programs show you what a firm looks like. Ours shows you what the practice of law is becoming. You’ll get real client work, direct feedback, and attorneys who want to teach, at a firm that’s principled about quality, always looking for a better way, and genuinely excited about where the tools are going.

If you want to start your legal career learning how to do great work, not just a lot of it, we want you to apply.

How to Apply

Send us your resume and a cover letter by March 1, 2027. In your cover letter, tell us what kind of legal work you’re most interested in and why General Legal caught your interest. Interviews will take place on a rolling basis from January through May 2027. We read every application.

General Legal is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

The Opportunity

As a Workforce Planning Analyst supporting Backoffice operations, you'll turn workload trends into reliable forecasts, staffing analyses, and practical recommendations that help teams meet service commitments efficiently. In your first year, you'll strengthen capacity visibility, flag emerging workload or coverage risks early, and support data-informed decisions with Operations, Workforce Management, and Finance.

As a member of the Client Partnerships organization, the Client Partnerships Manager will lead the development and execution of strategic account plans, drive solution adoption, monitor client health and strengthen relationships with operational and executive stakeholders. The role is accountable for supporting client retention, identifying growth opportunities and ensuring clients recognize the business and operational value of their partnership with DataSpring.

This position operates at the intersection of client strategy, value realization and execution. The Client Partnerships Manager works closely with Product, Sales, Implementation, Operations, Analytics, Marketing, Finance and other internal partners to align resources around client priorities, address risks and create a consistent, high-quality client experience.

The ideal candidate is a proactive, commercially minded healthcare professional who can manage multiple client relationships, translate complex information into clear recommendations and move comfortably between strategic discussions and day-to-day execution.

The Client Partnerships Manager is a full-time, remote, exempt position and reports to the Director, Client Partnerships. This position will require the ability to travel up to 30% of the time.

Responsibilities

Client Strategy and Relationship Management

  • Serve as the primary relationship owner and strategic partner for an assigned portfolio of healthcare clients.
  • Develop a comprehensive understanding of each client’s organization, business objectives, operating environment, stakeholders and use of DataSpring solutions.
  • Build trusted relationships across executive, operational, technical and procurement stakeholders.
  • Create and maintain strategic account plans that document client priorities, relationship strategies, solution adoption, risks, opportunities and measurable success outcomes.

Retention and Client Growth

Portfolio and Organizational Contribution

  • Contribute to the development of Client Partnerships playbooks, processes, reporting and best practices.

Qualifications & Experience

jobs.title: Human Centered Design Engineer
jobs.excerpt: Company Overview Voted #1 EHR by PC Mag, WRS Health delivers a fully integrated cloud based EMR and practice management solutions to its clients.
jobs.description:
Company Overview

Voted #1 EHR by PC Mag, WRS Health delivers a fully integrated cloud based EMR and practice management solutions to its clients. We bring solutions to physicians by providing constant enhancement of our products and services including EHR, practice management, marketing, patient coordination and billing.

Job Overview

We are seeking a Human-Centered Design (HCD) Engineer to bridge the gap between user needs and technical execution. You will lead qualitative research, map user journeys, build interactive prototypes, and run usability tests to ensure our products are intuitive, accessible, and impactful for the physicians, clinical staff, billers, front-desk teams, and patients who rely on them every day. In a clinical setting, a confusing screen costs a provider time, adds to burnout, and can affect patient safety, so this role carries real weight. You will thrive here if you love sitting with users in their actual workflows, can turn messy observations into clear direction, and can defend design decisions with evidence.

Key Responsibilities

User Research

  • Conduct contextual inquiries, interviews, field observations, and surveys with physicians, clinical staff, billers, and patients to uncover explicit and latent needs.
  • Partner with account managers and support teams to surface usability pain points from client feedback and support tickets.

Synthesis & Strategy

  • Translate research into personas, journey maps, service blueprints, and system workflows across clinical, operational, and billing processes.
  • Present insights to product and executive leadership to shape roadmap priorities.

Ideation & Prototyping

  • Facilitate cross-functional design workshops and build low- to high-fidelity wireframes and interactive prototypes in Figma, Sketch, or Adobe XD.
  • Design AI-powered features (AI charting, AI agents) that keep clinicians in control and make AI output easy to review and correct.

Usability Testing

  • Plan, moderate, and analyze formative and summative usability tests to iterate on designs before and during development.
  • Evaluate safety-critical workflows such as medication management and e-prescribing, and support ONC Safety-Enhanced Design testing.

Collaboration & Governance

  • Partner with product managers, business analysts, and engineers in Agile/Scrum teams to maintain design integrity from concept through release.
  • Uphold accessibility standards (WCAG, Section 508) and HIPAA-safe research practices across all products.

Leadership

  • Build and scale WRS Health's HCD practice, including research operations, templates, and standards.
  • Mentor designers and researchers, and coach teammates on human-centered methods.

Qualifications

Required

  • Education: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Human-Centered Design, Human-Factors Engineering, Interaction Design, Cognitive Psychology, or a related field.
  • Experience: 3 to 6+ years of professional experience in HCD, UX design, or user research, including enterprise or regulated-industry experience.
  • Technical Skills: Proficiency in prototyping software (Figma, Sketch, or Adobe XD), qualitative research methodologies, usability testing frameworks, and Agile/Scrum delivery flows.
  • Accessibility: Working knowledge of Section 508 and WCAG standards and how to apply them in practice.
  • Core Competencies: Strong empathy, verbal storytelling, analytical problem-solving, and the ability to defend design decisions with data.
  • A portfolio or case studies demonstrating end-to-end research, synthesis, prototyping, and measurable impact.

Preferred

  • Experience designing for EHR, practice management, revenue cycle, telehealth, or other health IT products.
  • Familiarity with clinical workflows and terminology across ambulatory specialties.
  • Knowledge of ONC Safety-Enhanced Design (user-centered design and summative testing) requirements, NISTIR 7804, or ISO 9241-210.
  • Experience designing AI-assisted or automation features, including human-in-the-loop review patterns.
  • Prior experience leading or mentoring designers/researchers, or building a design function from the ground up.
  • Experience with remote research and unmoderated testing tools and product analytics platforms.
  • Clinical background or prior work in a medical practice setting.

A Day in the Life

Your days move between the field, the whiteboard, and the prototype. You might start by joining the product team's stand-up to flag a research insight affecting an upcoming sprint, then sit in (virtually or on-site) with a specialty practice to watch how the front desk, medical assistants, and physicians actually work, noting the workarounds they've built and where the screens slow them down. Later, you could be synthesizing those observations into an updated journey map, facilitating a workshop with product managers, engineers, and billing specialists to sketch solutions, or moderating a usability test of a new AI charting feature to see how a clinician reviews and trusts AI-drafted notes. Before the day ends, you refine prototypes in Figma based on what you learned, check designs against accessibility standards, share prioritized recommendations with product leadership, and make time to coach the designers and researchers on your team.

Success Metrics

  • Measurable usability gains: Improved task success rates, time-on-task, error rates, and System Usability Scale (SUS) scores for redesigned workflows, including fewer clicks and less documentation time for key clinical tasks.
  • Research-driven roadmap: Consistent monthly contact with users across specialties, with a clear, visible share of roadmap items originating from or validated by HCD research.
  • Fewer usability issues post-release: Decline in usability-related support tickets, rework, and post-launch design defects.
  • Accessibility and certification compliance: New and updated features meet WCAG 2.1/2.2 AA and Section 508 standards at release, and ONC Safety-Enhanced Design documentation is completed on time.
  • Adoption and satisfaction: Higher feature adoption (including AI features) and improved client satisfaction or NPS for redesigned areas.

Job Details

  • Job Type: Full-time | Independent Contractor
  • Location: Remote
  • Hours: Must be available during standard US business hours (9:00 AM – 5:00 PM EST or 8:30 AM – 4:30 PM EST)

Compensation will be based on location, experience, and qualifications.

This job description outlines the general responsibilities of the role and is not exhaustive. Additional duties may be assigned as needed to support business operations.

WRS Health is an equal opportunity employer.

Vālenz Health® is the destination for employers, brokers, payers, and providers to reduce costs, improve quality, and elevate the healthcare experience. About This Opportunity:
As a Stop Loss Claim Analyst (aka Stop Loss Claim Auditor), you’ll review and audit stop loss reimbursement requests to ensure accurate and timely payments in accordance with plan documents, stop loss policies, contractual requirements, and established procedures. You’ll evaluate supporting claim and eligibility documentation, perform aggregate claim calculations within your delegated authority, and help ensure reimbursement requests meet applicable requirements. You’ll also support plan document reviews, payment integrity initiatives, reporting, and high-cost claim monitoring to promote accuracy, consistency, and compliance throughout the stop loss reimbursement process.


Things You’ll Do Here:

  • Review and audits stop loss reimbursement requests to ensure accurate and timely payment in accordance with plan documents, stop loss policies, contractual requirements, and established procedures.
  • Evaluate supporting claim and eligibility documentation, performs aggregate claim calculations within delegated authority, and supports plan-document review, payment integrity, reporting, and high-cost claim monitoring.
  • Retrieve, log, organize, and review stop loss claim submissions and supporting documentation within established turnaround standards.
  • Audit initial and supplemental reimbursement requests for eligibility, covered expenses, contract terms, deductible application, and other applicable plan and policy provisions.
  • Perform preliminary calculations and audits for aggregate accommodations and final year-end aggregate claim submissions, including review of contract terms, aggregate factors and deductibles, enrollment and premium information, paid claim data, and supporting documentation.
  • Identifie discrepancies, exceptions, ambiguous contract language, and matters outside delegated authority and escalates them to appropriate Claims, Compliance, Underwriting, or leadership resources.
  • Obtain and evaluate supporting documentation, including eligibility records, extension-of-benefits information, FMLA and COBRA documentation, precertification information, accident or subrogation records, UB-04s, itemized bills, and other required materials.
  • Maintain complete and accurate documentation of audit activity, information requests, calculations, determinations, and supporting records within applicable claim systems.
  • Review plan documents, Summary Plan Descriptions, amendments, and related materials using established checklists and approved automated or AI-assisted tools.
  • Validate automated or AI-assisted review outputs before use in claim or plan-document decisions and escalates material discrepancies or uncertainties for additional review.
  • Identify potential eligibility, coordination, cost-containment, payment-integrity, or reimbursement issues and coordinates with appropriate internal and external partners.
  • Support high-cost claim monitoring, reserve and notification review, and related reporting by evaluating available clinical and financial information.
  • Communicate with TPAs, brokers, carriers, auditors, vendors, and internal partners regarding missing documentation, claim status, audit findings, and related questions within established authority.
  • Support claims quality reviews, reporting, research, procedure documentation, and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Provide backup support for claims intake and workflow activities as business needs require.
  • Perform duties in accordance with established procedures, contractual requirements, delegated authority, confidentiality standards, and applicable regulatory requirements.
Accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential duties.

What You’ll Bring to the Team:
  • 3+ years of experience in healthcare claims, stop loss claims, medical claim auditing, TPA operations, or a related field.
  • Working knowledge of self-funded medical plans, employer stop loss terminology, reimbursement processes, contracts, and operational workflows.
  • Demonstrated ability to interpret plan documents, stop loss policies, eligibility information, and claim documentation.
  • Strong analytical and mathematical skills with the ability to perform detailed claim audits and reimbursement calculations accurately.
  • Strong attention to detail with demonstrated ability to maintain complete, accurate, and audit-ready documentation.
  • Ability to independently review claims within established procedures and delegated authority and appropriately escalate exceptions or high-risk matters.
  • Strong organizational and time-management skills with the ability to manage multiple claims, deadlines, and documentation requirements.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to work effectively with TPAs, carriers, brokers, vendors, and internal partners.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel and Word, and the ability to learn stop loss administration, underwriting, and reporting systems.
  • Ability to use approved automated and AI-assisted tools responsibly while maintaining appropriate human review and validation of outputs.
  • Ability to handle confidential financial, claim, and member information with discretion.

A plus if you have…
  • Bachelor’s degree in Healthcare Administration, Accounting, Finance, Insurance, Business, or a related field.
  • Experience auditing complex or high-dollar medical claims.
  • Experience reviewing Summary Plan Descriptions, plan documents, stop loss contracts, or amendments.
  • Experience with aggregate accommodation and year-end aggregate claim calculations.
  • Experience with self-funded employers, stop loss carriers, TPAs, managing general underwriters, or related healthcare financing organizations.
  • Experience identifying payment-integrity, cost-containment, subrogation, coordination-of-benefits, or eligibility issues.
  • Experience with stop loss claims administration, underwriting, or reporting platforms.


Where You’ll Work: This is a fully remote position, and we’ll provide all the necessary equipment!

Why You'll Love Working Here

Our mission is to advance healthcare through technology and expertise to optimize cost, quality, access, and utilization for all.   • Technical risks are identified early and managed before they affect confidence or outcomes. 
  • Customers reach value faster after deployment or major use case activation. 
  • You are recognised by customers and account teams as a trusted, practical technical advisor.

  • Fluency in Bahasa Indonesia, and proficiency in English, both written and spoken.
  • Familiarity with customer success platforms, health scoring, adoption analytics, and renewal governance is advantageous. 

 

Why This Role Matters 

This is an opportunity to sit at the centre of customer value, technical strategy, and retention, helping customers turn powerful cybersecurity technology into sustained operational impact.

Help Secure and Modernize the U.S. Army's Global Network!

Leidos is seeking a motivated Junior Network Security Integration Engineer to support the Army Global Unified Network (AGUN) program.

This is an exciting opportunity to build your network security engineering skills while helping modernize and protect the Army's global enterprise network.

In this remote role, you'll focus on firewall integration, secure network connectivity, security policy configuration, and network modernization. You'll work alongside experienced engineers and cybersecurity professionals to integrate modern security technologies into the Army's enterprise network.

We're looking for someone with hands-on firewall experience, strong networking fundamentals, and the ability to configure, integrate, and troubleshoot enterprise security solutions.


.What You'll Do

  • Support the engineering and integration of site-specific firewalls and network security solutions.
  • Perform network device discovery, validate management connectivity, and identify migration dependencies.
  • Configure and troubleshoot Next-Generation Firewalls (NGFW), preferably Palo Alto Networks.
  • Assist with firewall security policies, access control lists (ACLs), NAT, security zones, and network segmentation.
  • Review legacy firewall configurations and help integrate security policies into modernized network environments.
  • Support Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) and secure remote access solutions.
  • Troubleshoot firewall policy conflicts, VPN connectivity, routing, and network security issues.

  • Support vulnerability remediation, security assessments, and network hardening activities.

  • Participate in technical reviews, readiness assessments, and security validation activities.
  • Coordinate with engineering and operations teams to ensure successful integration and operational handoff.
  • Work independently on assigned technical tasks while collaborating with senior engineers on complex issues.

What We're Looking For

  • Active DoD Secret security clearance and U.S. citizenship.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, IT, Cybersecurity, Network Engineering, or a related field with 2–4 years of relevant experience, or approximately 3 years of relevant experience without a degree.
  • DoD 8570/8140 IAT Level II certification (such as Security+) and an approved Computing Environment (CE) certification.
  • Hands-on experience with enterprise firewall configuration, integration, management, and troubleshooting, preferably Palo Alto Networks.
  • Knowledge of firewall security policies, ACLs, NAT, security zones, and network segmentation.
  • Experience supporting network security integrations, firewall migrations, or enterprise network modernization.
  • Understanding of LAN/WAN, TCP/IP, BGP, OSPF, IPSec, VPNs, and Layer 2/Layer 3 routing.
  • Familiarity with Zero Trust principles and secure remote access technologies.
  • Experience troubleshooting firewall policy conflicts, network connectivity, and security performance issues.
  • Familiarity with Palo Alto Panorama, Cisco management platforms, or similar tools.
  • Experience with firewall patching, upgrades, configuration management, and lifecycle maintenance.
  • Knowledge of DoD STIGs, network security hardening, and cybersecurity compliance.
  • Experience creating technical documentation, firewall configuration records, and network security diagrams.
  • Strong troubleshooting, communication, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to work independently and collaborate with geographically dispersed engineering teams.
  • Flexibility to work nonstandard shifts when needed for migration activities.
  • Willingness to travel up to 10%.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting U.S. Army, DISA, or other DoD enterprise networks.
  • Palo Alto Networks security certification (such as PCNSE or a current equivalent), CCNA, or CCNP.
  • Experience with large-scale firewall migrations, security policy conversions, and enterprise network transformation.
  • Hands-on experience with Palo Alto NGFW, Panorama, and GlobalProtect.
  • Experience with Cisco Secure Firewall, Juniper SRX, or other enterprise firewall platforms.
  • Experience with ZTNA solutions such as AppGate.
  • Knowledge of SD-WAN, MPLS, and enterprise network segmentation.
  • Experience with firewall rule optimization and security configuration validation.
  • Familiarity with virtualized firewalls, cloud security, and hybrid networks.

  • Familiarity with vulnerability management, RMF, and security compliance processes.
  • Experience supporting large, geographically dispersed enterprise networks.

Why Join Leidos?

At Leidos, you'll have the opportunity to develop your network security expertise while supporting a mission that directly impacts the U.S. Army's global communications.

You'll work alongside experienced engineers, gain exposure to advanced firewall and network security technologies, and contribute to modernizing critical military infrastructure.

If you're a cleared Network Security Engineer with hands-on firewall experience who wants to grow your skills and support a mission that matters, we'd like to hear from you!

Join Leidos and help secure the future of the Army's global network. Apply today!

jobs.excerpt: 📋 Tasks and responsibilities Join a collaborative development team working on a SCADA system used by dispatchers around the clock to balance a power perimeter across Belgium, France, Germany and the Netherlands.
jobs.description:
📋 Tasks and responsibilities

Join a collaborative development team working on a SCADA system used by dispatchers around the clock to balance a power perimeter across Belgium, France, Germany and the Netherlands. The platform is being expanded to cover a wider geographical area and to integrate additional smaller, flexible assets.

The team develops tools for the real-time control of power plants, the integration of flexibility assets and compliance with European grid codes in support of the energy transition. These tools are used to:

  • Monitor production assets and the available capacity of power plants.
  • Exchange information between TSOs and the real-time SCADA system, or Supervisory Control And Data Acquisition system.
  • Calculate real-time setpoints for power plants based on the production plan, real-time acquisition and other inputs such as FCR, aFRR and mFRR, helping to keep the power perimeter in balance.

FCR stands for Frequency Containment Reserve, aFRR for Automatic Frequency Restoration Reserve and mFRR for Manual Frequency Restoration Reserve. Similar balancing mechanisms are used in other countries.

As part of the development team, you will:

  • Develop and maintain the Hitachi Energy MicroSCADA X SYS600 platform, including custom logic and algorithms for real-time automated decision-making.
  • Write and maintain back-end logic in SCIL, the native language of the SCADA platform.
  • Design and develop clear, responsive web interfaces for dispatchers using HTML5, CSS3 and JavaScript or TypeScript within the MicroSCADA framework.
  • Work with Git and contribute to the further development of the SCADA landscape through ongoing projects.
  • Apply architectural design and software craftsmanship principles such as SOLID, DRY, KISS and YAGNI to create scalable, clean, maintainable and resilient code.
  • Collaborate in an Agile environment with analysts, dispatchers and technical teams.
  • Use AI-assisted engineering tools such as GitHub Copilot to reduce repetitive work, generate tests, document code and understand unfamiliar parts of the code base, including during incident investigations. You remain responsible for the design and quality of the resulting work.
  • After a full onboarding, take part in a shared, compensated on-call rotation that is mostly remote, helping to ensure system availability and grid stability. Critical incidents are handled with support from the team.

Previous SCIL knowledge is not required. You will receive training and coaching from the team, and the skills you develop can be applied beyond this specific platform.

📝 Your profile

  • You have relevant experience in an industrial OT environment.
  • You are fluent in spoken and written English. This is essential for the role.
  • You care about building reliable software and systems.

💼 Offer

You will be part of a growing Belgian SME where initiative and personal development are encouraged. We will provide you with an enjoyable work environment with fun colleagues. We will work out a career plan with you, with attention and a budget for extra education/certification. You can count on an attractive salary, supplemented with extra-legal benefits, including a company car.

(Freelance is also possible)

jobs.excerpt: Summary/ObjectiveQellus is looking for a curious, thoughtful problem-solver who enjoys giving ideas structure and helping a team turn them into something useful and lasting.
jobs.description:
Summary/Objective
Qellus is looking for a curious, thoughtful problem-solver who enjoys giving ideas structure and helping a team turn them into something useful and lasting. As part of an innovative Agile product team, you will bring a natural inclination for organization, quality and follow-through to the development of new solutions and methods.
You will be part of a product team that designs, builds and maintains Qellus’s knowledge core: a governed, connected foundation of business process and information models, reference architecture, shared definitions and relationships. It connects how a business works, the capabilities it needs, and the enterprise systems that support it. You will help keep this knowledge coherent, trustworthy and reusable. Your work will include creating and maintaining these models, investigating gaps and inconsistencies, and applying standards that help the foundation evolve sustainably. You will also contribute to the solutions and methods built on it.
You will work collaboratively with architectural and technical colleagues, contribute your own observations and ideas, and progressively take ownership as your understanding grows. Mentorship and practical experience will support your development in our models, methods and tools.

What Success Looks LikeEarly success means helping turn a defined enterprise process into a standard, reusable, and governed product that the team can use to work more efficiently and generate customer value more quickly. It is important that the product be built on foundational standards so that the product can be scaled to other areas without each new process starting from scratch. As the foundation grows, those practices help the team reuse, sustain and scale its solutions and methods.
Over time, you’ll take increasing ownership of the core and agreed aspects of the work built on it. Your judgment, investigation and follow-through make established work less dependent on repeated direction. Colleagues can rely on you to protect quality, improve how the work is done and help innovations become dependable, reusable practices that create value.

The role is fully internally focused for a minimum of six months. Architectural direction and specialist support will guide work as its scope develops.

Essential Functions

  • Build out and maintain the core’s connected models and reference architecture within the team's established metamodel and architectural direction, investigating definitions and relationships so the foundation remains coherent and reusable.
  • Investigate proposed reference architecture, definitions, relationships and gaps, applying enterprise architecture principles and established frameworks alongside evidence to make sound recommendations and improvements.
  • Collaborate on solutions and methods that apply the core, helping turn approved backlog items into repeatable practices that deliver value.
  • Apply and improve governance and quality practices so the team can innovate on a trustworthy foundation.
  • Use AI-assisted workflows thoughtfully, combining exploration with careful judgment about the quality and usefulness of their outputs.
  • Help colleagues understand and use the foundation, share learning and follow improvements through to practical adoption.

Skills, Education and Experience

Required Skills, Education, and Experience
  • Skills
    • Purposeful curiosity. You enjoy exploring unfamiliar subjects, ask why things work as they do, and investigate relationships and consequences before settling on an answer.
    • A natural instinct for structure. You see patterns, clarify definitions and recognize when something does not fit. You understand how standards and frameworks help good ideas become dependable, reusable practices.
    • Creativity with practical judgment. You see possibilities and suggest better approaches while considering their implications. You know when to investigate further, involve another perspective or move a useful piece of work forward.
    • Discipline and completion. You organize your work, pay attention to meaningful detail, document decisions and follow through. You find satisfaction in making an improvement last as well as getting it started.
    • Ownership. You take responsibility for outcomes, including investigating problems, seeking help when needed and staying involved through resolution.
    • Humble confidence. You question assumptions respectfully, explain your reasoning, acknowledge uncertainty and learn from others. You can contribute a concern before you have a complete solution.
    • Collaborative energy. You share knowledge, welcome different expertise and help the team succeed. You connect the quality of your work to its usefulness for colleagues and, ultimately, customers.
  • Education
    • Bachelor's degree in MIS, Computer Science, Data Science, Information Technology or related field, or equivalent experience.
  • Experience
    • 3-5+ years of experience in the fields of data science, architecture or data process
    • Demonstrated ability to create and maintain simple business process and information models within established standards.
    • Relevant professional experience working with structured information, business processes, models, quality or governance. We are interested in examples of how you applied standards thoughtfully, investigated an inconsistency, improved a practice or made information more useful to others.
    • Demonstrated ability to reason about relationships and downstream effects, communicate findings clearly and use everyday digital tools carefully.
    • Experience maintaining or improving an existing framework can demonstrate this foundation.
    • We will support your learning of our tools and specific metamodel along with the domain and workflow knowledge needed for the role.
Preferred Skills, Education and Experience
  • Experience with enterprise systems or information management systems, such as SAP or OpenText; enterprise architecture tools such as Signavio or LeanIX; or work involving structured models, process relationships and AI-assisted knowledge workflows can be helpful.
  • Exposure to process modeling with BPMN or to frameworks such as APQC or TOGAF.
  • Prior experience with these platforms or frameworks is helpful rather than required; curiosity about learning and applying them is important.
What we ValueAt Qellus, how you work matters as much as what you deliver. We're looking for someone who reflects our core values day to day:
  • Own The Outcome - Do what it takes to get it done. Own our commitments.
  • Focus on Customer Success - Earn the role of trusted advisor, committed to continuous improvement and tangible results for our Customers.
  • Problem Solver - Actively focus our skills and experience to creatively seek out effective solutions. View challenges as opportunities to innovate and improve.
  • Humbly Confident - Self-assured and modest. Always prepared and ready to make a difference, without arrogance.
  • The Qellus Principle - Work together as a collective team, sharing our unique talents to create something truly amazing. We push each other to be our best and achieve things that wouldn't be possible alone.

AI Disclaimer

We understand that candidates may use AI and other tools to prepare application materials. Candidates should be prepared to discuss and substantiate the experience, skills, technical knowledge, and accomplishments represented in their application. Our selection process may include position-specific questions, technical discussions, practical exercises, and other assessments to evaluate demonstrated capabilities. Misrepresentation of qualifications, experience, or individual contributions may result in disqualification from consideration.

Turnitin is seeking a forward-thinking global HR executive to lead People Operations and its continued transformation. Reporting to the Chief People Experience Officer, this role oversees Global People Shared Services, Benefits, HR Systems and Analytics, and Employee Relations operations, including our external ER partnership. The role will also lead the planned integration of global Payroll operations from Finance.

We are looking for a leader who can design organizations, build capability and create leverage through effective structures, systems, technology and people. This includes challenging legacy ways of working, testing hypotheses, making fact-based investment decisions and using AI and automation to simplify work and improve productivity.

Our environment is global, remote-first and evolving. Success requires someone who can lead through ambiguity, constructively challenge assumptions, make decisions with imperfect information and translate complex problems into practical solutions.

This leader must bring deep operational expertise, sound employee relations judgment, proven HR technology transformation experience and the ability to develop a strong leadership bench. The expectation is not simply to maintain operations, but to build a more scalable, resilient and accountable People Experience function. This leader will also serve as a trusted adviser to the CPXO and senior leadership, bringing independent judgment, sound business acumen and practical solutions to complex operational, organizational and employee matters. They will anticipate risks, offer constructive challenge and help translate business priorities into effective People practices.

What You Will Do

Global People Shared Services & Operational Excellence

  • Lead global People Shared Services across employee lifecycle operations, onboarding, offboarding, leaves, immigration coordination and employee support.
  • Lead the design and continuous improvement of the People Shared Services (PSS) delivery model, establishing clear ownership, decision rights, escalation protocols and accountability within PSS, while partnering with PBPs, COEs and external providers to ensure effective handoffs, coordination and service delivery.
  • Evaluate organizational structure, staffing, spans of control and work allocation to improve service effectiveness, productivity and management capacity.
  • Build scalable operations through standardization, self-service, documented procedures, cross-training and succession coverage.
  • Establish performance measures that identify service gaps, recurring issues, operational risk and opportunities to redirect work to more effective delivery channels.

Employee Relations, Governance & Risk

  • Lead the global Employee Relations operating model, including governance, quality and performance of external ER partners.
  • Bring strong judgment and practical expertise to complex employee matters, including investigations, performance, restructuring, separations and employment risk.
  • Establish clear decision rights, case ownership, service standards and escalation protocols in partnership with Legal and People Business Partners.
  • Evaluate the effectiveness and economics of the ER delivery model, building internal expertise and alternatives to external providers where appropriate.
  • Anticipate emerging employee risks and operational vulnerabilities, ensuring appropriate intervention before matters escalate unnecessarily.
  • Establish effective ER case management, tracking and reporting, including case volumes, themes, resolution timelines, outcomes and recurring risks to inform continuous improvement.
  • Strengthen the operational management of employee separations and HR offboarding, ensuring clear ownership, timely coordination, consistent documentation and effective partnership across PSS, PBPs, Legal and external providers.

HR Technology, AI & Digital Transformation

  • Lead HRIS modernization, including strategy, selection, implementation, integration, adoption and ongoing optimization.
  • Reimagine the People service model using AI, automation and integrated systems to reduce administrative work, improve self-service and create capacity for higher-value activities.
  • Expand AI-enabled employee and manager support, knowledge management, case routing, workflow automation and workforce analytics.
  • Establish reliable People data, reporting and governance, including appropriate security, privacy and responsible AI controls.
  • Develop fact-based business cases, test hypotheses through pilots and measure productivity, adoption, service improvements and return on investment.
  • Challenge technology investments that automate inefficient processes without first addressing underlying organizational or workflow issues.

Global Benefits & Payroll Transformation

  • Lead global Benefits operations, including administration, enrollment, vendor performance, financial stewardship and employee experience.
  • Design and implement an integration plan for global Payroll operations from Finance, including organizational structure, resourcing, systems, controls and transition readiness.
  • Partner with Finance, Legal and IT to strengthen Payroll governance, compliance, accuracy and integration with People systems.
  • Evaluate opportunities to standardize, simplify and automate Benefits and Payroll processes while protecting service continuity and financial controls.
  • Build sustainable functional leadership and operational coverage across both areas.

People Leadership, Organizational Design & Enterprise Partnership

  • Assess capabilities and capacity against future operating requirements, making evidence-based recommendations to build, buy, automate, or redesign work.
  • Lead effectively in a Remote-First environment, establishing strong operating rhythms, communication, collaboration and accountability across countries and time zones.
  • Partner with the CPXO, PXLT, Finance, Legal and IT on business-critical decisions, operational risks and transformation priorities.
  • Bring forward well-supported recommendations, welcome constructive challenge and adapt plans when new evidence warrants a different approach.
  • Maintain operational performance while implementing organizational change, balancing speed, employee experience, risk and financial discipline.
  • 15+ years of progressive global HR leadership experience, including senior accountability for HR Operations, Shared Services or organizational transformation.
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience required. Advanced degree or relevant HR or Employment Legal qualification / JD preferred.
  • Strong understanding of global Benefits, Payroll operations, HR compliance and employee lifecycle services.
  • Trusted advisor to C-suite (including Chief People Experience Officer) and senior business leaders, demonstrating strong business acumen and balancing of business objectives and priorities.
  • Demonstrated organizational design expertise, including restructuring teams, developing management capacity, establishing decision rights and improving spans of control and operational leverage.
  • Deep Employee Relations expertise, with sound judgment in complex matters, employment risk, external provider oversight and development of internal ER capability.
  • Proven leadership of significant HRIS implementations or transformations, including systems integration, process redesign, automation and adoption.
  • Demonstrated experience applying AI, automation or intelligent technologies to improve employee self-service, knowledge management, case management, workflow execution, analytics or operational productivity.
  • Strong financial and analytical acumen, including building fact-based business cases, testing assumptions, evaluating service delivery alternatives and demonstrating measurable returns.
  • Proven ability to build strong leadership teams, develop successors, address capability gaps and reduce operational dependency on individual employees or external providers.
  • Experience leading global, multidisciplinary teams in Remote-First, distributed or complex matrixed environments.
  • Demonstrated resilience through organizational change, competing priorities and constructive challenge, with the ability to maintain delivery while improving how work gets done.
  • Strong executive communication, sound judgment and the ability to influence stakeholders while remaining open to alternative perspectives.

The expected annual base salary range for this position is: $245,402/year to $283,445/year. This position is bonus eligible / commission-based.

Actual compensation will be provided in writing at the time of offer, if extended, and is determined by work location and a range of other relevant factors, including but not limited to: experience, skills, degrees, licensures, certifications, and other job-related factors. Leidos is seeking an experienced Mid-Level Network Security Vulnerability Remediation Engineer to support the Army Global Unified Network (AGUN) program.

This is an exciting opportunity to help secure and modernize the Army's global network infrastructure, protecting critical military communications and supporting mission readiness worldwide.

In this remote role, you'll focus on identifying, analyzing, and remediating firewall vulnerabilities across a complex enterprise network. You'll work closely with network engineers, cybersecurity professionals, and mission partners to implement security patches, configuration updates, and risk mitigation solutions.

We're looking for a hands-on Network Security Engineer with strong firewall experience, preferably Palo Alto, who can develop, test, and implement vulnerability fixes while maintaining network security and performance.


What You'll Do

  • Analyze and remediate firewall vulnerabilities and cybersecurity risks across enterprise network environments.
  • Evaluate vulnerability findings, vendor security advisories, software updates, and patches.
  • Develop, test, and implement firewall security patches, configuration changes, and mitigation solutions.
  • Execute approved firewall changes and vendor updates through established ASI and change-management processes.
  • Configure and maintain firewall security policies, access control lists (ACLs), NAT, security zones, and network segmentation.
  • Troubleshoot firewall connectivity, policy conflicts, performance issues, and security-related incidents.
  • Perform firewall upgrades, patching, configuration management, and lifecycle maintenance.
  • Collaborate with Information Assurance teams and the AGUN Cybersecurity Service Provider (CSSP) to address security risks and maintain compliance.
  • Implement and validate DoD Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs) and network security hardening requirements.
  • Support vulnerability assessments, remediation planning, and corrective-action activities.
  • Develop vulnerability assessments, patch/upgrade analyses, mitigation configurations, testing results, and production release plans.
  • Document remediation activities, ASI execution results, configuration changes, and ticket closure evidence.
  • Maintain firewall configuration records, network diagrams, and technical procedures.
  • Work independently on assigned engineering tasks while collaborating with senior engineers on complex technical issues.

What We're Looking For

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, IT, Cybersecurity, Network Engineering, or a related field with 4–8 years of relevant experience, or approximately 8–12 years of experience without a degree.
  • DoD 8570/8140 IAT Level II certification (such as Security+) and an approved Computing Environment (CE) certification.
  • Hands-on experience with enterprise firewall configuration, management, troubleshooting, patching, and vulnerability remediation.
  • Experience with Next-Generation Firewalls (NGFW), preferably Palo Alto Networks.
  • Strong understanding of firewall security policies, ACLs, NAT, security zones, and network segmentation.
  • Experience supporting firewall migrations, security policy changes, or enterprise network modernization.
  • Knowledge of LAN/WAN, TCP/IP, BGP, OSPF, IPSec, VPNs, and Layer 2/Layer 3 routing.
  • Familiarity with Zero Trust principles and secure remote access technologies.
  • Experience troubleshooting firewall policy conflicts, network connectivity, and security performance issues.
  • Familiarity with Palo Alto Panorama, Cisco management platforms, or equivalent tools.
  • Experience implementing DoD STIGs, network security hardening, and cybersecurity compliance requirements.
  • Experience developing technical documentation, firewall configuration records, and network security diagrams.

jobs.description:
Customer Implementation Manager

This role sits at the intersection of project management, healthcare operations, customer success, and deployment execution. Implementation Managers are responsible not only for getting Canopy installed, but for ensuring each customer is operationally ready, clinically prepared, technically stable, and demonstrating healthy early adoption before transitioning into long-term Customer Success.

You will serve as the primary customer lead during implementation, managing multiple workstreams across large health systems and coordinating stakeholders spanning Clinical Operations, Security, IT, HR, Communications, Training, Facilities, and executive leadership.

Before services begin, you will own the path to readiness: defining the implementation plan, driving customer deliverables, assessing workflows, helping determine the right program design, coordinating site walkthroughs and installations, and ensuring technical and operational dependencies are completed.

After go-live, your responsibility continues through stabilization. You will use customer sentiment, adoption data, system stability, and infrastructure health to determine whether the program is operating as designed and intervene when it is not. The Implementation Manager remains accountable until the customer meets defined stabilization criteria and is ready for a structured handoff to Customer Success.

Success in this role means delivering more than an on-time implementation. It means launching a healthy, adopted, sustainable program that customers trust and that creates the foundation for long-term value and expansion.

About Canopy

Canopy is committed to creating safer and more supportive environments for those on the front lines of care. Our mission is to help hospitals ensure that healthcare workers feel safe, appreciated, and empowered every day to deliver the highest quality of care.

We develop and deploy critical safety technology, including our wearable duress system and Real-Time Location System (RTLS) portfolio, delivered as a comprehensive service to enterprise healthcare systems across the United States.

Join our collaborative, mission-focused team and use your implementation expertise to make a real difference in the lives of those who care for others.

Key Responsibilities

Own the customer from kickoff through stabilization

  • Be the primary customer lead from kickoff through stabilization. Build confidence and trust with our partners and our team.
  • Run multiple complex healthcare implementations at once, with clear ownership of commitments, dependencies, risks, decisions and next steps.
  • Build strong, trusted relationships with customer project leads, clinical leaders, security teams, IT partners, executives and other stakeholders.

Plan and drive implementation readiness

  • Create, coordinate and execute project plans using Canopy's implementation playbook and best practices.
  • Set clear expectations with customers and internal teams on responsibilities, timelines, readiness requirements and success criteria.
  • Assess current workflows and help decide the right program design for each site.
  • Partner with clinical and security leaders to design alert and response workflows that fit how each unit actually works.
  • Partner with clinical leaders to build unit-level adoption plans and train clinical champions before go-live.

Lead complex healthcare deployments

  • Own every phase of the implementation: kickoff, technical configuration, installation, clinician training and go-live.
  • Coordinate site walkthroughs, hardware orders and delivery, and device installations with Canopy teams and the customer's IT, Security, Clinical, Facilities, HR, Communications/Training and executive stakeholders.
  • Hold both Canopy and customer workstreams accountable for progress toward the agreed services start or go-live date.
  • Identify and manage project risks and issues, build contingency plans, and escalate at the first sign of risk.

Protect implementation quality

  • Treat implementation quality gates as real decision points. Make sure gate requirements are met and documented, and recommend holding a phase or go-live when readiness criteria aren't met. At Canopy, a quality implementation beats a fast one.

Own post-go-live stabilization

  • Keep ownership of the customer after go-live until the site meets the defined stabilization exit criteria.
  • Assess program health with both quantitative and qualitative information:
    • Wear rate and badge use
    • Accidental alert rates
    • Alert activity and response
    • Customer and end-user sentiment
    • System, gateway and device health
    • Training or adoption gaps
  • Spot unhealthy trends early and use the Canopy stabilization playbook to step in. That can mean workflow changes, more training, re-engaging champions, fixing infrastructure, escalating technical issues, or bringing in leadership.
  • Coordinate fixes across the customer and Canopy teams when adoption, infrastructure, workflow or system performance falls short.
  • On a regular cadence, report health, risks, adoption metrics, time-to-value and ROI milestones to customer leadership and Canopy stakeholders, with clear next steps.

Deliver a strong Customer Success handoff

  • Work closely with the Customer Success Manager throughout the implementation so the transition feels seamless to the customer.
  • Identify early champions, executive sponsors, expansion opportunities and risks that may shape the long-term relationship.
  • Transition ownership only after the defined exit criteria are met. Document the handoff: customer goals, stakeholder relationships, implementation history, program design, health metrics, adoption trends, open risks, technical considerations and agreed next steps.

Improve the implementation practice

  • Share field feedback with Product and Engineering to improve the product and service delivery.
  • Help keep improving IM templates, playbooks and tools.

Required Qualifications

  • 5+ years in customer-facing implementation, deployment, onboarding, customer success, or consulting roles, with a track record of leading complex projects from start to finish.
  • Experience leading cross-functional implementations involving clinical, IT, security, HR, and executive stakeholders.
  • Experience in healthcare, medtech, or another regulated operational environment.
  • Experience managing hardware logistics or field-based installations.
  • Demonstrated ownership of post-launch outcomes: driving adoption, tracking performance metrics, and stepping in when results fall short.
  • Comfort working with data: you can read and interpret adoption and performance metrics, spot trends, and concisely report clearly to executive audiences.
  • Sound judgment on quality and readiness, including the confidence to recommend delaying a milestone and explain why.
  • Excellent organizational and communication skills.
  • Ability to travel to customer sites for key milestones (up to 50%).

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with workplace safety, duress, nurse call, or RTLS technology.
  • Change management or training/education experience with frontline clinical staff.
  • PMP or similar implementation-focused credential.
  • Proficiency with GuideCX, Salesforce, Google Workspace, Microsoft Teams, and AI tools such as Claude.
  • Experience in a startup or high-growth company with a flexible, generalist culture.

Location & Travel

  • Travel: up to 50% during active projects related to on-site kickoffs, walkthroughs, installs, go-lives and hypercare, and clinical training.

jobs.excerpt: We’re looking for a Senior Platform Engineer to join our tech team and help build the future of neuro-contextual advertising at global scale.
jobs.description:
We’re looking for a Senior Platform Engineer to join our tech team and help build the future of neuro-contextual advertising at global scale.

Who We Are

At Seedtag, our mission is to transform advertising by proving that effectiveness and user privacy can truly coexist.

As the leading Neuro-Contextual Advertising Company, we combine Artificial Intelligence, Natural Language Processing, Computer Vision, and neuroscience to understand not only what content is about, but how it makes people feel and what they intend to do next.

Our proprietary AI, Liz, enables brands to connect with audiences across the open web and Connected TV without cookies or user tracking. Founded in 2014 by two ex-Googlers, Seedtag has grown to 500+ Seedtaggers in 17 countries, backed by €250M in funding, and operates today as a global ad-tech leader.

If you enjoy solving complex engineering challenges and building AI-driven systems at scale, you’ll feel right at home here.

Your Challenge

As a Senior Platform Engineer, you will:

  • Collaborate with engineering teams at Seedtag to set direction and build platforms that enhance customer experience, while providing necessary operational support.

  • Contribute to the professional growth and performance optimization of the Platform Engineering (SRE) team by offering helpful feedback and guidance.

  • Foster and cultivate trust within the SRE team, empowering them to implement solid engineering practices and principles.

  • Ensure reliability, security and compliance of Seedtag's cloud foundations, aligned with the Google Cloud Architecture Framework and NIST/ISO controls (logging, vulnerability and secrets management, hardening, backup and restore).

  • Design, build and operate the internal developer platform (GKE, networking, IAM, CI/CD, GitOps) so product teams can ship autonomously under a "you build it, you run it" model.

  • Share knowledge, review peers' work and raise the bar on engineering practices in the team.

  • Take part in the Platform on-call rotation, lead incident response and write blameless postmortems, turning recurring issues into automation and lasting fixes.

  • Partner with engineering teams to understand their needs and communicate roadmap, trade-offs and progress transparently.

  • Operate and evolve our streaming and data infrastructure (Redpanda and self-hosted databases), including migrations, upgrades and the discontinuation of legacy components.

  • Own the observability stack (VictoriaMetrics, Grafana, alerting, PagerDuty), tackling scalability problems such as high-cardinality metrics, and define SLIs/SLOs and a service maturity model with engineering teams.

  • Drive cost efficiency (FinOps): capacity planning, node and instance right-sizing, quota management and cost anomaly detection.

  • Reduce toil and enable self-service: replace tickets with tools, golden paths and reusable CI/CD workflows, and keep documentation and runbooks fresh.

  • Apply AI to platform operations: build and operate agents and automations (e.g. cost anomaly detection, PR review, incident triage), define MCP integrations, and contribute to AI governance with Security.

Our Core Values

Outcome over Output
We measure success by impact and value, not by volume of features or lines of code.

Failure Is Allowed, Learning Is a Must
Experimentation is key to innovation. We test early, iterate often, and learn fast.

We Are All Scouts
We take ownership and leave things better than we found them.

We Are Data-Driven
Data informs our decisions and helps us continuously improve our systems and results.

Tech Stack

Our stack includes:

  • Languages & Automation: Python, Go

  • Cloud & Infrastructure: GCP, Kubernetes (GKE), Terraform, Terraform Cloud

  • CI/CD & GitOps: GitHub Actions, ArgoCD

  • Observability: VictoriaMetrics, Grafana, PagerDuty

  • Streaming & Data: Redpanda, Kafka, MongoDB, Redis

  • Security & Networking: IAM, VPC, Cloudflare, secrets management

  • AI & Automation: LLM-based agents, MCP integrations

What You’ll Need to Succeed

  • Technical Experience: Minimum of 4 years of experience in SRE/DevOps/Platform/Cloud Engineering roles, preferably in large-scale, high-traffic product companies, with proven technical proficiency and the ability to engage in deep technical conversations with the team.

  • Collaboration and Prioritization: Service-oriented mindset: understands stakeholders' problems, communicates clearly and prioritizes across several concurrent projects in a fast-paced environment. Experience with Kanban or Scrum.

  • Automation and Programming: Strong scripting/programming skills (Python, Go or similar) to automate operations and build internal tooling (operators, agents, CI/CD workflows).

  • Cloud Services: Deep hands-on knowledge of Google Cloud Platform (GCP) or an equivalent hyperscaler (VPC and peering/PSC, IAM, GKE, CloudSQL, GCS), including networking and migrations between projects or organizations.

  • Incident Management and On-call Responsibilities: Proven on-call and incident management experience, with strong problem-solving skills under pressure and a track record of root-cause analysis and blameless postmortems.

  • Kubernetes: Solid production experience with Kubernetes, ideally GKE: cluster lifecycle and upgrades, autoscaling and node pool tuning, and workload identity.

  • Infrastructure as Code and GitOps: Strong Terraform experience (Terraform Cloud a plus), GitOps (ArgoCD) and CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, self-hosted runners).

  • Observability: Experience with Prometheus-compatible stacks (VictoriaMetrics, Grafana), alerting design and SLI/SLO practices. Understanding of cardinality and scaling issues is a plus.

  • Security: Working knowledge of cloud security practices: secrets management, vulnerability and CVE remediation, hardening and least privilege.

  • Other tools and engines: Streaming platforms (Kafka/Redpanda), or other stateful systems (MongoDB, Redis, Elasticsearch, Aerospike); Cloudflare (CDN, load balancing); compliance frameworks (NIST CSF, SOC 2, ISO 27001); FinOps and capacity planning; hands-on experience building or operating LLM-based agents or automations (e.g. ADK, MCP) and using AI tools in daily engineering work; service maturity / internal developer platform approach.

  • People-Centric Approach: Focus on understanding stakeholders problems and providing the best way to solve team.

  • Agile Methodologies: Experience working with agile development methodologies like Kanban or Scrum, promoting transparency and collaboration within the team.

  • Planning and Execution: Strong skills in roadmap planning, execution, and measuring engineering excellence through key metrics and KPIs.

  • Priority Management: Proven ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment, managing multiple priorities and concurrent projects effectively.

  • Cloud Services: Experience with Google Cloud Platform (GCP) or other cloud services, including technologies like Terraform and Ansible, for designing and managing scalable infrastructures.

  • Incident Management and On-call Responsibilities: Previous experience in incident management and on-call responsibilities is needed. The candidate must demonstrate strong problem-solving skills under pressure and quick responsiveness to critical situations.

Why Join Seedtag?

  • A key moment of growth with real ownership and global impact.

  • Flexible work model with 100% remote or hybrid options.
    (Remote contracts available in Spain, Italy, UK, Belgium, Netherlands, France, and Germany.)

  • Continuous learning through a learning platform and optional language classes.

  • A supportive, trust-based culture that values well-being.

  • Team activities, offsites, and opportunities to connect beyond work.

Additional Perks

  • Home office setup budget up to €1,000

  • Paid trips to our HQ in Madrid

  • MacBook Pro M3

Ready to Join the Seedtag Adventure?

At Seedtag, we create an environment where everyone can thrive. If you need accommodations during the hiring process, let us know and we’ll ensure a positive experience.

Send us your CV and let’s build the future of neuro-contextual advertising together.
