jobs.excerpt: SALARY: $20. 37POSITION TITLE: Kansas City Regional Recruitment CoordinatorDEPARTMENT: Admissions RecruitmentJOB DESCRIPTION: EMPLOYMENT TERMS: Full-time, 12-month PRIMARY DUTY: The Kansas City Regional Recruitment Coordinator must have a passion for Northwest Missouri State University, be highly motivated, and goal-oriented to attract, recruit, and retain prospective students to meet the enrollment goals at Northwest.
jobs.description:
SALARY:

$20.37

POSITION TITLE:

Kansas City Regional Recruitment Coordinator

DEPARTMENT:

Admissions Recruitment

JOB DESCRIPTION:

EMPLOYMENT TERMS: Full-time, 12-month


PRIMARY DUTY:

The Kansas City Regional Recruitment Coordinator must have a passion for Northwest Missouri State University, be highly motivated, and goal-oriented to attract, recruit, and retain prospective students to meet the enrollment goals at Northwest. The desired candidate will reside in the KC metro area. Recruitment Coordinators must represent and promote Northwest Missouri State University accurately and persuasively to prospective students, parents, guidance counselors, educators and other publics within the assigned territory. Additionally, the Recruitment Coordinator assists the Admissions-Recruitment team with the administration of all campus recruitment activities.


ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

  • Responsible for the coordination of recruitment and yield in Kansas City metro area.
  • This remote position will be based within the recruiting territory to attend off-campus recruitment activities (including but not limited to counselor luncheons, high school visits, college fairs, regional conferences, award presentations, and more).
  • Travels to Maryville for on-campus events and training as necessary.
  • Collaborate and work closely with Great Jobs KC-KC Scholars partnership to build and maintain positive relationships with Great Jobs KC Advocates, partner high schools, and high school counselors.
  • Assist with recruitment activities and college fairs at area community colleges to promote Northwest to prospective transfer students.
  • Responsible for the coordination and management of all virtual recruitment activities including but not limited to large group, small group, and personalized sessions with their assigned territory.
  • Create and maintain positive relationships with prospective students, parents, guidance counselors, educators, and other publics within assigned territory by providing information on academics, value, scholarships, housing, student life, and general university activities
  • Analyze student data to select which recruitment strategies and information is most effective for each prospective student.
  • Utilize data management to target select populations for all armchair recruitment activities.
  • Actively conduct armchair recruitment that occurs during all stages of the recruitment funnel. Includes contact via emails, personal notes, phone calls, texting, and social media.
  • Review, update, and utilize computer-based lead tracking systems to aid in prospective student recruitment
  • Utilize value-added and relationship-based techniques when working with prospective students, parents, guidance counselors, educators, and other publics
  • Create and achieve territorial goals and objectives based on trend data, historical reporting, and evaluation of prospect and admitted database information
  • Analyze, read, and report feedback to Admissions-Recruitment leadership with on-going competitive environment.
  • Assist with the coordination of Summer Orientation and Registration, Advantage week, and General Registration
  • Survey residents of assigned territory to assess needs of prospective students, parents, guidance counselors, educators, and other publics
  • Serve as a liaison between various internal departments in resolution of prospective students, parents, guidance counselors, educators, and other publics concerns and issues
  • Performs other duties as assigned

QUALIFICATIONS:

Education: Undergraduate Degree


Certification/License: Driver’s license


Experience: 1-2 years of experience in the field or a related area


Skills: Extensive knowledge of colleges and universities; ability to communicate effectively with people from diverse backgrounds as well as cultivate awareness of cultural diversity; strong organizational skills; strong public speaking skills; ability to load, unload, and set up exhibits. Proficiency in Microsoft Office programs and high comfort level with technology and the ability to analyze and present data effectively.


WORKING CONDITIONS:

This position will work in a remote office environment with a work schedule determined based on service needs, which will likely include early morning, night, and/or weekend hours.


TYPICAL PHYSICAL DEMANDS: Ability to lift up to 20 pounds


COMMUNITY:

Northwest Missouri State University located in Maryville, Missouri, a community of 12,000 with a diverse economy and a strong industrial base. Maryville is located 45 miles north of St. Joseph, Missouri, 90 miles north of Kansas City, Missouri, and 110 miles southeast of Omaha, Nebraska. For more information visit the city’s website at .


UNIVERSITY:

With an enrollment of more than 8,500 students, Northwest is a coeducational, primarily residential four-year university that offers a broad range of undergraduate and selected graduate programs on its Maryville campus and through Northwest Online.

Founded in 1905, Northwest boasts a high retention rate and a graduation rate in the 95th percentile among its peers. Additionally, results of the Ruffalo Noel Levitz Student Satisfaction Inventory show Northwest students are more satisfied than students at national peers, and 78 percent of Northwest students report they would repeat their university experience, compared to 75 percent of students surveyed nationally at their respective institutions.

Furthermore, the University is a national model for student success and career placement with 93 percent of bachelor’s degree earners and 98 percent of master’s degree earners securing employment or continuing their education within six months of completing a degree at Northwest, according to the most recent data.

Northwest places a high emphasis on profession-based learning to help graduates get a jumpstart on their careers while maintaining competitive tuition rates and generous financial assistance to help minimize the financial barriers students may face when pursuing a college degree.

Students have opportunities to build their résumés with experiences on campus in nearly every area of study, including the Horace Mann Laboratory School, National Public Radio affiliate KXCV, the R.T. Wright Farm, Mozingo Outdoor Education Recreation Area, a partnership with the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency or Knacktive, a student-driven integrated digital marketing communications agency. In conjunction with its emergency and disaster management program, Northwest organizes and hosts Missouri Hope, an annual mass casualty training exercise that attracts first responders and emergency workers from throughout the nation and provides hands-on training in preparation for a natural disaster.

The University’s vibrant and diverse learning community also offers more than 150 student organizations, and textbooks and a laptop are included in tuition, saving students an estimated $6,900 over four years. Northwest offers 1,200 student employment positions, allowing students to build professional skills through its internationally benchmarked student employment program.

For more information about Northwest and its performance, visit www.nwmissouri.edu/aboutus/facts/.

jobs.description:
“In 36 months, agentic AI systems will be an operating reality across major institutions. We intend to be central to it.” — Dr. Jim Rebesco, Cofounder and CEO, Striveworks

The government’s demand for AI is growing far faster than the systems required to support it. Fewer than 15% of federal AI programs have reached sustained production, despite billions of dollars invested. The models perform in testing, but they degrade in the real world. And when performance drops, trust goes with it.

Striveworks was built to solve that problem.

What you’ll build

Since 2018, we have delivered the most trusted AI systems operating in real-world use cases—providing a layer of assurance underneath hundreds of deployed models that monitors performance, manages drift, and sustains systems long after they leave the lab.

As a Senior Machine Learning Engineer–Maritime Systems, you will be a core contributor to both customer-driven projects and the enduring products of the company. Working directly with customers, data scientists, software engineers, and DevOps engineers, you’ll define requirements and orchestrate complex data engineering pipelines. You’ll also develop machine learning models and custom analytics applied to image, video, text, geospatial, time series, and structured data. Your work will inform the future of Chariot, our proprietary AI operations platform, and it will extend to the field, with mission-critical deployments, direct customer contact, and insights that shape what we build next.

What it’s like here

We lead with trust, treat each other with respect, and use candor consistently, kindly, and constructively. We care deeply about our work, and we find genuine satisfaction in doing it well. Above all, we take ownership—because we feel the weight of collective results personally. We are looking for people who share these values and are eager to put them into practice.

What we’re looking for

  • A BS degree in computer science, machine learning, or a related discipline and 6+ years of relevant experience
  • Demonstrated experience delivering data-centric systems
  • Proficiency in programming languages and libraries common to machine learning; excellence in Python is essential, as is knowledge of TensorFlow, PyTorch, and/or scikit-learn
  • Proficiency in software engineering fundamentals to include algorithms, data structures, design patterns, and at least one systems programming language
  • Proficiency with modern software engineering tools and processes
  • US citizenship with eligibility and willingness to obtain a Secret US security clearance

The following isn’t required, but we’d love to see it:

  • Active Secret (or above) US security clearance, a recently expired clearance, or a past clearance

This position offers a fully remote work environment, or you can work hybrid/on site at our office in northwest Austin, TX. This role requires travel up to 20% of the time.

Compensation

The anticipated base pay range for this position is $160,000–$200,000/year. Striveworks’ total compensation package includes a competitive base salary, equity grants, and cash bonuses.

Benefits include:

  • Voluntary life, long-term disability, accident, and hospital indemnity insurance

Company Description

Candidly was founded in 2016 to flip the script on what it means to plan, borrow, repay, and save for college. Today, we’re the category leader with the market’s most comprehensive AI-driven student debt and savings optimization platform. We partner with hundreds of top employers, financial institutions, and retirement record keepers, positioning Candidly to serve more than 35 million Americans.

We’re already achieving incredible results — to date, we’ve helped our users get on track to eliminate more than $1.8B in student debt and pay off their loans 175,000 years quicker — and we’re seeking movers, shakers, innovators, and problem solvers to help take our mission even further.

Candidly is a high-growth, Series B startup, funded by leading investors including Altos Ventures, Aflac, Salesforce Ventures, UBS, Equal Opportunity Ventures, Impact Engine, Rethink Impact, Unum, and Cercano Management. Our fully remote, international team of 70 (and counting) includes alumni from Google, UBS, Twitter, Plaid, Prudential, LendingTree, Morgan Stanley, Deutsche Bank, and more.

Job Description

Candidly is looking for a full-time Senior Product Designer to lead design for Cait, our AI-native financial guidance product. Employers offer Cait as a benefit. Employees use it to understand their benefits, debt, savings, and retirement, and to see the dollar effect of each decision. Cait is a conversation, not a set of pages, so you will design in use cases, states, and recovery paths, not only in screens. You will work with product managers and engineers who build with AI tools, and you will deliver specs and coded prototypes that they can build from. You will also help make the Cait brand clear and distinct in a form that partners can theme with their own colors. This role reports to the VP of Product and Design.

Standard Job Description

The CNC Machining Capability Project Engineer is the technical person for evaluating, selecting, and developing external machining suppliers for complex CNC milling and turning operations (3 to 5 axis). In addition to deep technical expertise, this role requires strong business acumen—the ability to translate capability data into strategic sourcing decisions that drive cost savings, revenue protection, and market competitiveness.

This role partners closely with Supply Chain, Strategic Sourcing, Supplier Quality, and Operations to evaluate machining capabilities, resolve technical issues, reduce cost and risk, and ensure suppliers can meet quality, delivery, and performance requirements.

This position bridges the gap between engineering intent and supplier execution, providing hands-on machining expertise to support supplier selection, development, and ongoing performance

Focus Areas:

Supplier Technical Evaluation & Selection

  • Lead technical assessments of machining suppliers, including:
    • CNC milling/turning (3–5 axis)
    • Complex tolerances & GD&T
    • Materials (aluminum, titanium, steel, Inconel, composites, etc.)
  • Support RFQ/RFP reviews by:
    • Review drawings for machining types
    • Match suppliers to drawing requirements, quality requirements, volume and program needs
    • Manufacturability concerns
    • Process assumptions
    • Cycle times and cost drivers
    • Support PO Kickoffs and drawing reviews with the supplier
  • Participate in source selection decisions as the machining technical authority

Basic Qualifications

10 + years of engineering experience with at least 4 years leading large, multi‑disciplinary projects (≥ $5 M budget, 10+ team members).

Expert in CAD/CAE, GD&T, BOM management, and PLM/ERP tools; strong command of Earned Value, risk registers, and schedule control.

Proven leadership and communication skills – able to mentor teams, influence senior stakeholders, and produce clear technical and executive reports.

Familiarity with applicable industry standards and regulations (AS9100, ISO 9001, ITAR/EAR, etc.) and capable of driving root‑cause analysis and continuous‑improvement initiatives.

Desired Skills

Bachelor’s (or higher) degree in a relevant engineering discipline or equivalent experience and certifications; PMP/PRINCE2 or advanced degree preferred.

Advanced CNC & CAD/CAM expertise – Proficient with 3‑, 4‑ and 5‑axis machining, tooling selection, cutting‑parameter optimization, and multi‑axis CAM software (e.g., Mastercam, Siemens NX, HyperMILL).

Process planning, fixturing & quality control – Develop detailed setup sheets, design work‑holding, program CMM/laser inspections, apply GD&T, and follow ISO/AS9100 quality procedures.

Project‑management & continuous‑improvement – Use Earned‑Value, risk registers, and schedule tools (MS Project/Primavera); drive root‑cause analysis, Lean/Six‑Sigma projects to cut cycle time, scrap and tool wear.

Cross‑functional communication & documentation – Translate engineering requirements into clear machining documentation, status reports, and presentations for designers, suppliers, customers, and senior leadership.

jobs.description:
About Acquia

Acquia empowers the world’s most ambitious brands to create digital customer experiences that matter. With open source Drupal at its core, the Acquia Digital Experience Platform (DXP) enables marketers, developers, and IT operations teams at thousands of global organizations to rapidly compose and deploy digital products and services that engage customers, enhance conversions, and help businesses stand out.

Headquartered in Boston, MA, Acquia is a Great Place to Work-CertifiedTM company, is listed as one of the world’s top software companies by The Software Report, and is positioned as a market leader by the analyst community. We are Acquia. We are building for the future and we want you to be a part of it!

Career Exploration at Acquia

Our recruitment process is designed to empower you in making the most informed decisions. Acquia is committed to providing an inclusive, transparent, efficient, and educational interview experience that cultivates exploration into career opportunities at Acquia

You will discover the opportunity to grow your career here and learn from a global team that empowers you to exceed boundaries and achieve the extraordinary.

The Mission

Acquia is in the middle of its biggest platform transformation in a decade, and the economics of that transformation need an owner. As Senior Product Manager, that’s you.

This is not an accounting role. Finance closes the books, runs the monthly close, and owns the numbers. What you own is the story on top of them: what platform costs are doing and why, where margin is moving and what it means, what investment cases actually say when the assumptions are pressure-tested. You are the financial voice inside the product organization, the person PMs bring their business cases to before they go up, and the person leadership turns to when they need to understand what’s happening with the platform’s economics.

You also own the platform economics story, the ongoing performance narrative that keeps leadership aligned on how the business is performing and where the opportunities and risks are. That means driving the executive check-ins and reviews, in partnership with the Cloud PM group, that keep platform economics visible and actionable at the right level.

The role is also expanding into new territory. AI is restructuring what cloud platforms cost to build and run, faster than most organizations are ready for. You will build the frameworks, internal and external reporting, chargeback models, CapEx planning, that give Acquia visibility and control over AI-driven costs as they grow. And you will own the strategic vendor relationships where Acquia needs someone who can hold both the financial negotiation and the product judgment at the same time.

The Profile

  • The Margin Owner: You are the ongoing source of truth for how the platform portfolio performs economically. You track actuals, understand what’s driving them, and run the leadership rhythm, executive check-ins and cross-functional reviews with the Cloud PM group, that keeps margin performance visible and actionable at the right altitude. When something moves, you know why, and you know what to do about it.
  • The Platform Economist: You read cost trends, consumption patterns, and margin signals the way other PMs read usage data: as a window into what’s working, what’s at risk, and where the platform needs to change. Platform cost efficiency, customer-level economics, cost trending across the portfolio, these are your inputs. Your output is clarity, in language engineers, PMs, and executives can all act on.
  • The Financial Advocate: Every PM on the team builds business cases. You make those cases better. You review assumptions before they become commitments, model the cost implications of a feature before it goes into the roadmap, and make sure significant investment decisions are economically grounded, not just technically compelling. This is not a gatekeeper role. It’s a force multiplier.
  • The AI Cost Pioneer: AI is changing what it costs to build and run a cloud platform faster than most finance teams are tracking it. You are building the frameworks, internal reporting, external customer visibility, chargeback models, CapEx planning, that let Acquia understand and manage AI-driven costs proactively, not reactively. This is early work with real impact, and you are the person defining what it looks like.
  • The Vendor Strategist: You own the financial and product dimensions of Acquia’s key strategic vendor relationships, cloud infrastructure, cost intelligence tooling, and OEM partnerships. You bring the financial rigor and product judgment that Acquia needs in the room on renewals, negotiations, and procurement decisions, and you manage those relationships as long-term strategic assets, not just contracts to renew.
  • The Context Architect: You thrive in an Agentic PDLC environment. You build and maintain the economic context, margin models, cost benchmarks, vendor frameworks, that lets the team’s agentic workflows scale financial analysis and reporting without requiring your involvement in every step.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own Gross Margin Reporting and Executive Engagement. Track and report on gross margin performance for the platform portfolio on an ongoing basis, in partnership with the Cloud PM group. Understand what’s driving the numbers, surface the risks and opportunities that matter, and run the executive check-ins and leadership reviews that keep platform economics visible and actionable at the right level.
  • Own the Platform Cost Narrative. Work from Finance’s data to build the product-side view of what the platform costs to run and why. Track platform cost efficiency, customer-level economics, and cost trends across the portfolio, and turn those signals into product priorities, investment sequencing, and recommendations leadership can act on.
  • Be the Financial Advocate for Every PM on the Team. Review business cases before they go up. Model feature and product costs. Help PMs pressure-test their assumptions so significant investment decisions are economically grounded, not just technically compelling.
  • Build the AI Cost Frameworks. Own AI cost reporting for internal and external audiences. Build the chargeback models that let Acquia track AI cost at the product and customer level. Develop CapEx frameworks that let the organization plan AI infrastructure investment with clarity, and advocate for AI cost best practices across the business.
  • Partner on Strategic Vendor Relationships. Serve as the financial and product voice in Acquia’s key vendor relationships across cloud infrastructure, cost intelligence tooling, and OEM partnerships. Contribute to renewals, negotiations, and procurement approvals with both financial precision and product judgment, and help ensure those relationships are managed as strategic assets, not just recurring line items.
  • Manage Third-Party Tool Economics. Own expense reporting, expense modeling, and contract management across the third-party tool portfolio. Maintain and evolve the platform’s cost intelligence infrastructure, including ongoing tool administration, dashboard development, and design partnership with key vendors.
  • Contribute to Platform Investment Planning. Feed into hosting forecasts and reservation planning, making sure platform infrastructure commitments are sized and sequenced against the product roadmap, not just current-state usage.
  • Agentic Collaboration. Build and maintain the shared economic context structures, margin models, cost frameworks, vendor intelligence, AI cost dashboards, that let the team’s agentic workflows scale financial analysis and reporting without manual overhead.

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience in a role that required both financial modeling and strategic product or business judgment, ideally at the intersection of PM and FP&A in a SaaS or managed cloud platform business — finance-fluent, not just finance-adjacent
  • A track record of building financial models from scratch: cost models, gross margin analysis, business cases, consumption forecasts — not updating someone else’s
  • Demonstrated experience owning executive reporting cadences and driving leadership reviews with your own recommendations, not just contributing the numbers
  • Hands-on cloud economics depth: consumption-based cost modeling, reserved capacity planning, or gross margin analysis in a cloud infrastructure or SaaS business — you’ve done the work, not observed it
  • Hands-on experience with FinOps tooling (CloudZero, Apptio, Cloudability, or equivalent) — not passing familiarity
  • Experience contributing to vendor negotiations and renewals where both financial outcomes and product strategy were on the table, not just one or the other
  • Enough PM craft to work as a peer to PMs, not just a finance partner to them — experience writing requirements, running discovery, or owning a roadmap area
  • Comfortable presenting financial narratives to VP-level or above, with accountability for the recommendations, not just the deck
  • Demonstrated interest in AI-assisted analysis and agentic workflows, and the drive to build those into how this role operates from day one

We are an organization that embraces innovation and the potential of AI to enhance our processes and improve our work. We are always looking for individuals who are open to learning new technologies and collaborating with AI tools to achieve our goals.

Acquia is proud to provide best-in-class benefits to help our employees and their families maintain a healthy body and mind. Core Benefits include: competitive healthcare coverage, wellness programs, take it when you need it time off, parental leave, recognition programs, and much more!

Final compensation will be commensurate with your experience and will be determined by a variety of factors, including city of residence, relevant skillset, and job-related knowledge.

Acquia is an equal opportunity (EEO) employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, protected veterans status or any other protected status or characteristic under federal, state or local law unrelated to the ability to perform the job.

We are seeking an AI-Native candidate who treats AI not as an external tool, but as a fundamental extension of their cognitive workflow. The ideal candidate possesses an orchestration mindset—the ability to skillfully prompt, manage, and direct AI to navigate complexity—and maintains a high degree of AI fluency.

You should be characterized by radical adaptability and a "builder" mentality, showing a restless drive to transform traditional work processes into agentic workflows. Beyond technical proficiency, we value intellectual humility: the willingness to constantly unlearn old methods in favor of more efficient, AI-augmented processes. You don't just use AI to do your job; you use it to redefine what your job can achieve.

Pay Range
$160,000—$170,000 USD

jobs.excerpt: At Ensono, our purpose is to be a relentless ally, disrupting the status quo and enabling our clients to Do Great Things.
jobs.description:
At Ensono, our purpose is to be a relentless ally, disrupting the status quo and enabling our clients to Do Great Things. As a trusted technology adviser and managed services provider, we help clients navigate continuous change and embrace innovation. We deliver world-class transformational services across hybrid cloud, infrastructure, mainframe, data, IdAM, and cloud-native solutions, simplifying complex business challenges and creating new pathways to success. Headquartered in the USA and backed by private equity, Ensono has a strong track record in the UK and Europe, with growth plans built on trusted partnerships and deep industry expertise.

About the Role

We are looking for an experienced Senior FinOps Engineer to join our growing SRE and Cloud Services team and help deliver a consistent, outcome-focused FinOps-as-a-Service capability. This is a foundational role in building and scaling our FinOps-as-a-Service offering across enterprise clients. You will combine hands-on cloud cost engineering, governance, reporting and stakeholder engagement to improve cost visibility, accountability and value from cloud investment. Working within each client’s environment and toolchain, you will partner with engineering, SRE, finance and business stakeholders to prioritise achievable outcomes, deliver recommendations and implementation-as-code, and maintain clear client approval for production changes and commercial commitments.

Key Responsibilities

Optimise

  • Create and maintain an opportunity register that records each optimisation opportunity, estimated value, implementation effort, status and realised benefit;
  • Perform rightsizing analysis of compute, database and storage resources using observed utilisation, performance and service requirements;
  • Model Reserved Instance and Savings Plan coverage and utilisation, presenting evidence-based recommendations while recognising that commitment purchases remain the client’s decision;
  • Participate in architecture and solution reviews, providing cost models, options and trade-offs for proposed cloud services;
  • Identify idle, orphaned and unattached resources and recommend safe, prioritised remediation;
  • Submit optimisation changes, including storage lifecycle and tiering controls, as pull requests to client Infrastructure-as-Code repositories with cost analysis; validate in non-production where available and promote only following client approval.

Govern

  • Define and maintain an Infrastructure-as-Code-aligned tagging taxonomy and supporting policies; monitor tagging compliance and manage remediation exceptions;
  • Develop reusable policy-as-code modules and cost gates for client delivery pipelines;
  • Establish anomaly detection and route alerts into agreed incident workflows; triage anomalies, coordinate investigation and record dispositions;
  • Own budget tracking, forecasting and variance analysis, including billing reconciliation and agreed baselines;
  • Apply proportionate financial governance controls that respect client approval, risk and change-management requirements.

Enable

  • Build and maintain cost, allocation and unit-economics dashboards using agreed business measures;
  • Deliver showback and chargeback reporting, with clear attribution of cost and consumption;
  • Participate in sprint and planning ceremonies, jointly prioritising work within available capacity, surfacing trade-offs and agreeing delivery and reporting cadence;
  • Create and maintain a joint FinOps roadmap, tracking priorities, dependencies, outcomes and progress;
  • Provide knowledge transfer and present the current cost position, optimisation activity, realised savings and roadmap progress to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Engage

  • Lead operational onboarding by establishing access to the client environment, billing and cost APIs or exports, and delivery toolchain; assess the current cost position, utilisation, commitment coverage and tagging quality; agree priorities and cadence; and establish initial reporting;
  • Work inside client toolchains and governance processes, collaborating through pull requests and evidence-based cost analysis rather than making unilateral production changes;
  • Own agreed monthly reporting covering cost and usage variance, allocation, unit economics, optimisation activity and realised savings, budget and forecast variance, anomaly dispositions, tagging compliance and billing reconciliation, plus quarterly commitment coverage and utilisation reviews;
  • Act as a trusted adviser and coordinate with Ensono SRE and other services. Deliver recommendations and implementation-as-code within scope, make client approval and prioritisation explicit, and communicate that savings depend on client decisions, implementation and usage.

What You Will Bring to Ensono

Must-Have

  • Demonstrable senior-level experience delivering an operational FinOps or cloud economics service, including onboarding new client environments and establishing repeatable delivery;
  • Strong hands-on experience with Microsoft Azure billing and cost management, including cost exports or APIs, Azure Cost Management, Azure Advisor and Azure Monitor;
  • Experience delivering Infrastructure-as-Code changes through client repositories and CI/CD pipelines, including pull requests, cost analysis, peer review and non-production validation;
  • Strong understanding of cloud pricing, Reserved Instances, Savings Plans, and commitment coverage and utilisation modelling;
  • Experience maintaining opportunity registers, estimating value and effort, and tracking realised benefits without over-stating or guaranteeing savings;
  • Strong capability in budgeting, forecasting, variance analysis, allocation, showback or chargeback, and billing reconciliation;
  • Experience with tagging compliance, policy-as-code, cost gates, anomaly detection and operational triage;
  • Ability to create clear cost and unit-economics dashboards and present service performance to technical, financial and business stakeholders;
  • Proven client-facing communication and consultancy skills, with the ability to manage prioritised outcomes within proportional capacity and surface delivery trade-offs.

Nice-to-Have

  • Experience with AWS cost management (Cost Explorer, Trusted Advisor, Compute Optimizer);
  • Experience with GCP billing and cost optimisation;
  • FinOps Foundation certification (FinOps Certified Practitioner or FinOps Certified Professional);
  • Experience with FinOps platforms such as CloudHealth, Apptio Cloudability, Kubecost or native cloud cost tools;
  • Familiarity with Kubernetes cost management and container rightsizing;
  • Understanding of unit economics and the ability to report cost against business measures;
  • Experience building dashboards and reporting using tools such as Power BI, Grafana or Looker;
  • Cloud certifications (Azure, AWS or GCP) at associate level or above.

What We Can Offer You

We are a people-first business, which means people are at the heart of everything we do here. We offer our associates a safe environment where learning, knowledge sharing, and open communication is encouraged.

We believe that great work deserves great rewards. In return for your ideas, commitment and ambition, we'll give you a very competitive base salary and a range of benefits as soon as you join. On top of your highly competitive base salary, we offer:

The VP, Consulting leads Domaine’s Consulting practice and holds a seat on the Craft Leadership team. This role owns consulting as a commercial function as well as an advisory one. It is how Domaine moves from being chosen for a platform build to being chosen for the business outcomes.

This role does not receive a brief and execute it. It takes in a conversation with a prospect or existing client, specific or vague, and discerns the goals, the real needs, the gaps, the path, and the teams and skills required to get there. It then builds the plan and the trust to see it funded. It works in lockstep with Client Partners, Creative, Sales and Engineering, and brings commercial instinct to every recommendation: what should change, why it will grow the client’s business, what it will cost, and what it will return.

Help evolve accounts from single-threaded delivery to multi-service relationships.
  • Provide the strategic input and human judgment layer on client health and monthly intelligence reporting, on top of AI-generated analysis.
  • Ensure consulting hours are named, scoped, and priced into retainers and new builds rather than absorbed into the account.
  • Join pursuits for strategic accounts, bringing senior transformational thinking into the room alongside Sales and Client Partners.

Practice Leadership and Partner Advisory

  • Fluent in every discipline they lead. Our interpreters serve clients across numerous industries, including health care, 911, first responders, education, government agencies, and all walks of business.

As an interpreter, you will receive training that is the best in the industry. We’ll ensure that you learn new skills while further developing your skillset. We provide numerous opportunities for advancement. You’ll be in a certified ASTM and ISO environment. You'll also be supported by a Senior Language Specialist, as well as our Interpreter and Technology Help Desks.

Join our team now!

Job Description

Work at Home Bilingual Jinyu-English Phone Interpreter


Job Title: JinyuInterpreter

Location: Work at Home position in United States

Position: Phone Interpreter

Status: Independent Contractor

Pay: $0.75 - $0.90 per minute


We Offer:

  • Employee Referral Program.
  • Advancement opportunities within the organization.
  • Interpreter support.
  • An inclusive and diverse work environment.
  • **This is an independent contractor position and therefore not eligible for employee benefits.**

Position Overview:


The Jinyu Telephone Interpreter is responsible for handling calls on demand, and renders the meaning of conversations between Jinyuand English speakers. The interpreter breaks the communication barrier in a wide range of industries that LanguageLine Solutions serves: Healthcare, Government, Insurance, Financial, Utilities, Travel & Hospitality, General Business, Law Enforcement, Court, and 911.


The interpreter processes information quickly, concisely and recognizes sensitive cultural differences. The interpreter is professional and courteous at all times and uses appropriate terminology and understands common industry procedures and practices. The interpreting sessions may involve simple or complex, technical or non-technical subjects.


This position does not involve written translation however translators and other skilled linguists are encouraged to apply. The Interpreters translate verbally.


**This is a remote position. The Interpreter works from his/her home-office. It is essential to ensure a quiet & secure environment.**


Essential Job Functions

  • Respond to the interpreting sessions promptly and conduct interpretation in a friendly and professional manner.
  • Render correct concepts and meanings according to the conventions of established interpretation protocol, avoiding omissions or additions.
  • Speak clearly in both languages using proper pronunciation, enunciation and polite expressions.
  • Maintain a professional demeanor throughout the interpreting sessions at all times.
  • Remain calm during interpreting sessions in the event that one of the primary speakers is incoherent or upset, especially in emergency situations such as 911 calls.
  • Maintain punctuality and availability during work hours.
  • Follow client instructions, in compliance with protocol to ensure client expectations are met with the Limited English-speaking Person (LEP), avoiding interaction with the LEP without client’s permission.
  • Understand protocol and terminology for various industries including, but not limited to, Medical, Insurance, Finance and Law.
  • Demonstrate commitment to cultural sensitivity and working in a diverse environment.
  • **Some calls may be highly emotional and/or stressful in nature. The interpreter may need to remain on a call for extended periods without breaks due to the nature of the call or may, at times experience high call volumes. The interpreter must have the ability to provide the required, company standards of service within this dynamic environment. **

Qualifications

  • Fluency inJinyu and English and skilled in the associated cultural dynamics.
  • Ability to provide cultural competency and assess regional and accent differences to find ways of communicating with the LEP.
  • Excellent listening, retention and note-taking skills to maintain a high level of accuracy during interpretation.
  • Ability to concentrate, stay detached from the conversation, remain neutral and objective at all times, and remain on calls that involve sensitive subjects such as end of life conversations, pregnancy termination, vaccinations, and matters concerning sexual orientation and/or gender expression.
  • Education or work experience in language-related fields such as teaching, language assessment, translation or interpretation preferred.
  • Must be able to adapt to any LLS technology enhancements that improve service delivery and meet client demands.
  • Must be at least 18 years of age.
  • Legally authorized to work in the United States
  • Applicants for employment in the US must have work authorization that does not now or in the future require sponsorship of a visa for employment authorization in the United States and with LanguageLine Solutions (i.e., H1-B visa, F-1 visa (OPT), TN visa or any other non-immigrant status).
  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • Candidates who are currently employed by a client of LanguageLine Solutions or an affiliated LanguageLine Solutions business may not be eligible for consideration.
  • Ability to read and write the requested languages - highly preferred.

**Based on your location, a post-offer, a pre-employment background check and/or drug screen may be required**


Technical Requirements:

  • Dedicated personal device for business purposes.
    • Desktop / Laptop Computers with any of the following Operating Systems: Windows, MacOS, or ChromeOS.
    • Tablets (iPadOS or Android) are acceptable.
    • Smartphones (iOS or Android) are also acceptable.
  • Restricted brands:
    • Kaspersky products.
    • Huawei hardware.
  • High speed Internet connection for work related electronic communication. This internet connection should provide download speeds of no less than 5 Mbps, upload speeds of 3 Mbps, Ping value of no more than 300 ms, Jitter value of no more than 30 ms.
  • Must have access to a quiet space free from background noise or distraction.

Physical Requirements:

  • Must be able to operate a keyboard and mouse and remain in a stationary position in front of a computer the majority of the workday.
  • Must be able to operate company provided software and systems to perform all aspects of the job.
  • Must have sufficient manual dexterity to type or write.
  • Able to lift up to 26 lbs.
  • May be exposed to moderate noise levels; i.e. computer, audio, telephone.

jobs.excerpt: The MA in Clinical Counseling Program (Online) Alliant’s MACC is CACREP-accredited, one of the most respected credentials in the field and the recognized training standard by the Institute of Medicine and the Veterans Administration.
jobs.description:
The MA in Clinical Counseling Program (Online) Alliant’s MACC is CACREP-accredited, one of the most respected credentials in the field and the recognized training standard by the Institute of Medicine and the Veterans Administration. As the required educational training for counseling licensure in most states, it can provide more flexibility to practice wherever a student’s career takes them. Students prepared to work across a wide range of community and healthcare settings equipped with the skills to assess, diagnose, and treat mental health conditions and to meet clients with both clinical precision and genuine compassion.

Application Description:
Applicants to this position will be considered for a candidate pool encompassing one or more of the subject areas outlined in the job description. This pool will be used to identify qualified candidates for potential appointments during the 2026–2027 academic year.

Salary Range: $40 - $46 hourly (based on course requirements & level of education). This is a temporary, non-benefits eligible role.

Minimum Requirements:

  • Education: Doctoral degree in Counselor Education from an accredited college or university.
  • Experience: Appropriate experience in the areas(s) of specialization and expertise

Specific Courses: Spring 2027

COU67320-Sexuality and Sex Therapy:

This course is designed for counseling and human service professionals whose work will bring them into contact with clients experiencing problems and concerns with their sexuality. The course is designed to develop: (a) students’ knowledge base related to human sexuality; (b) an understanding of the varied sexuality issues which may be encountered in professional counseling practice; (c) students’ skills in assessment and intervention skills with sexuality issues; (d) awareness of dynamics of sexuality that intersect with larger societal systems of privilege and oppression based on gender, sexual orientation, race, class, abilities, national origin, and religion; (e) understanding of the social justice advocacy competencies as they intersect with sexuality issues; and (f) increased awareness of one’s personal perceptions, attitudes and affect related to sexuality issues. Course participants will become more effective in identifying, assessing and intervening with human sexuality related counseling issues.

COU67370: Couple and Family Counseling:

This course explores theories, interventions and research related to couple and family relationship issues. Couple and family systems theory therapies and practices are considered relative to assessment, diagnosis, and treatment issues. There is an emphasis on developing familiarity with couple and family therapy theories and critical thinking. Students will also be encouraged to consider the role that contextual factors play, such as ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, religion, privilege, and oppression. The course challenges students to examine and better understand their beliefs, values and assumptions about couples, marriage, as well as biases for working with diverse, couples, families and relationships.

COU66380 Grief and Loss in Counseling (Elective):

This course addresses theories and counseling techniques related to death and dying, grief and loss including: multicultural and international issues in death, grief and loss. Didactic, discussion, and experiential learning. The Master of Arts in Clinical Counseling (MACC) program is organized to enable students to build sequentially on knowledge and skills. This is an elective course in the Clinical Counseling curriculum and serves as an introduction to death and dying and grief and loss theories and techniques. This course recognizes the 2016 competencies determined by the Council for Accreditation of Counseling and Related Educational Programs (CACREP) for Clinical Mental Health Counseling and will introduce the Social Justice Advocacy Competencies of the American Counseling Association.

COU67350 Psychopathology Diagnosis and Treatment Planning:

Introduction to the assessment, diagnosis, etiology, prevention and treatment of mental disorders and differential diagnosis using the DSM-5-TR and related information. Provides a framework for understanding the range of personality and behavioral disorders, systematic treatment planning, interviewing, incorporation of resilience and cultural competence, and short-and long-term interventions.

COU67390 Counseling Research Methods and Program Evaluation:

The applied research methods evaluation course is intended to provide basic understanding of quantitative and qualitative research methods; use of research to inform evidence-based practice; statistical analysis; ethical/legal considerations; needs assessment, program evaluation; presenting research pertinent to professional counseling.

COU67550 Play Therapy and Expressive Arts in Clinical Counseling (Elective):

This course addresses theories and counseling techniques related to the therapeutic role of play and expressive arts in clinical counseling. The course includes didactic, discussion, and experiential learning. The Master of Arts in Clinical Counseling (MACC) program is organized to enable students to build sequentially on knowledge and skills. This is an elective course in the Clinical Counseling curriculum and serves as an introduction to play therapy and creative art theories and techniques. This course recognizes the 2016 competencies determined by the Council for Accreditation of Counseling and Related Educational Programs (CACREP) for Clinical Mental Health Counseling and will introduce the Social Justice Advocacy Competencies of the American Counseling Association.

COU67240 Multicultural Counseling and Techniques:

Multicultural counseling theories and techniques, including counselor’s roles in developing racial, ethnic, socioeconomic status, gender, sexual orientation, ability, religious/spiritual and international awareness and identity development. Experientially examines intentional and unintentional oppression and privilege, promotes social justice advocacy, and develops competencies in addressing biases.

NOTE: THIS COURSE NCLUDES A THREE-DAY RESIDENCY.

COU67130: Counseling Skills and Techniques (with Lab):

This course will aid students in the acquisition of` knowledge, skills, and professional dispositions, associated with counseling micro skills via role play and mock sessions. Students will learn about suicide prevention, crisis intervention, trauma-informed, and community-based care. Ethical and diversity issues are considered, as well as counselor self-care. NOTE: THIS COURSE INCLUDES A THREE-DAY RESIDENCY

COU67380 Assessment in Clinical Counseling:

This course provides students with an introduction to psychological testing; from its theoretical foundation, to applications in understanding human performance, including an understanding of the relevance and potential biases inherent to assessment with multicultural populations. Beginning with traditional psychometric theories of reliability and validity, students will be introduced to several major psychological tests.

jobs.description:
Build the Linux platform beneath the product — from BSP and bootloader to kernel, hardware integration, and long-term maintainability.

Before You Apply

This is a full-time employment opportunity. We are not considering B2B, freelance, consulting, or independent-contractor arrangements for this position.

This is a low-level Embedded Linux platform-engineering role. We are looking for engineers with hands-on experience in Yocto, BSP integration, Linux kernel, Device Tree, bootloaders, board bring-up, and hardware/software integration.

This is not primarily a Linux application-development or userspace C/C++ role.

About L4B Software

L4B Software is an embedded software and platform-engineering company headquartered in Munich, Germany, with an engineering presence in Pune, India.

We design, customize, integrate, secure, and maintain operating-system platforms based on Embedded Linux and Android/AOSP, tailored to the hardware, product architecture, security requirements, and lifecycle needs of our customers.

Our engineering capabilities span:

Customized Embedded Linux | Android/AOSP | BSP & Platform Integration | Product Cybersecurity | DevOps | System Validation

We support long-lifecycle and technically demanding products across medical technology, automotive, industrial systems, and other embedded environments.

About the Role

We are looking for a Senior Embedded Linux / Yocto BSP Engineer to develop and maintain customized Linux operating-system platforms for embedded products.

You will work across Yocto, BSP integration, Linux kernel, Device Tree, bootloaders, hardware enablement, and low-level system debugging.

This role goes beyond board bring-up. You will help turn vendor BSPs and low-level Linux components into reliable, reproducible, secure, and maintainable operating-system platforms designed for long product lifecycles.

What You'll Do

  • Develop and maintain Yocto-based Embedded Linux distributions.
  • Create and maintain Yocto recipes, layers, machine configurations, and platform customizations.
  • Integrate and maintain vendor BSPs and SoC platform components.
  • Perform board bring-up and hardware enablement.
  • Configure, integrate, debug, and maintain Linux kernels.
  • Develop and troubleshoot Device Tree configurations.
  • Work with bootloaders such as U-Boot.
  • Integrate and debug device drivers and hardware/software interfaces.
  • Investigate complex boot, kernel, BSP, and hardware-integration issues.
  • Support Secure Boot, platform hardening, OTA/update, and other platform-security activities.
  • Improve build reproducibility, maintain patches, and support platform releases across long product lifecycles.
  • Integrate platform builds with CI/CD infrastructure and collaborate with Product Cybersecurity, DevOps, and Validation teams.

What You Bring

  • Strong professional experience in Embedded Linux platform/BSP development.
  • Strong hands-on experience with Yocto Project and BitBake.
  • Experience creating and maintaining Yocto recipes and layers.
  • Strong BSP integration experience.
  • Linux kernel configuration, integration, and debugging experience.
  • Hands-on Device Tree experience.
  • Experience with bootloaders such as U-Boot.
  • Board bring-up and hardware-enablement experience.
  • Strong C/C++ knowledge for low-level embedded development and debugging.
  • Experience debugging problems across bootloader, kernel, BSP, drivers, and hardware boundaries.
  • Strong Linux command-line and system-debugging skills.
  • Experience with Git and software configuration management.

Technical Experience We Value

Relevant experience across several of the following would be particularly valuable:

ARM64 | Yocto / OpenEmbedded / BitBake | U-Boot | Linux Kernel | Device Tree | BSP Bring-Up | Device Drivers | Qualcomm / NXP / TI / Renesas | Secure Boot | TPM / TEE | OTA & Update Systems | PREEMPT_RT | Linux Security Hardening | Python / Shell Scripting | CI/CD

Experience building platforms for regulated, safety-critical, security-sensitive, or long-lifecycle products is an advantage.

What This Role Is Not

This is not primarily:

  • Linux application or userspace development
  • General C/C++ application development
  • Cloud/backend engineering
  • DevOps engineering
  • Android application development

You should be comfortable working close to the hardware and operating system, where debugging may require moving between the bootloader, BSP, kernel, Device Tree, drivers, and physical target.

Why Join L4B?

At L4B, you'll work on the operating-system platform itself, not simply applications running on top of it.

You'll work alongside engineers across Embedded Linux, Android/AOSP, Product Cybersecurity, DevOps, and Validation to build customized platforms that must remain reliable and maintainable throughout demanding product lifecycles.

We hire for technical depth, relevant hands-on experience, problem-solving ability, and engineering ownership. You don't need to match every technology listed above, but you should have strong Embedded Linux/Yocto foundations and be comfortable solving problems across system boundaries.

Bucharest, Romania | Remote | Full-Time Employment
No B2B, freelance, consulting, or independent-contractor arrangements.

If you enjoy turning BSPs, kernels, bootloaders, and hardware into a reliable Linux platform, we'd like to talk.

Principal Embedded Product Security Architect

About L4B Software

L4B Software specializes in embedded software engineering, platform development and product cybersecurity. We work with Embedded Linux, Android/AOSP, board support packages (BSPs) and real-time embedded systems to develop reliable, secure and maintainable software platforms.

Our engineering work supports industries including medical devices, consumer electronics and other connected embedded products where security must be integrated throughout the product lifecycle.

About the Role

We are looking for a Principal Embedded Product Security Architect with strong hands-on experience securing embedded devices and connected products, particularly in consumer electronics or medical-device environments.

This is a hands-on engineering position, not a general IT cybersecurity, SOC, network security or compliance-only role.

You will work directly with embedded software, platform and product-engineering teams to design, implement, test and maintain security mechanisms across device hardware, bootloaders, operating systems, firmware and software-update infrastructure.

We seek principal-level engineers who have personally owned end-to-end security architecture and delivered substantial hands-on security implementation into production embedded products, from threat identification and security decisions through release, monitoring, and lifecycle maintenance.

Cross-Platform Security Ownership — Android/AOSP and Regulated Embedded Linux

  • Serve as the accountable technical security architect for an Android/AOSP-based mobile device platform, and a managed embedded Linux platform for regulated medical devices; own security decisions, risk acceptance recommendations, architectural reviews, implementation direction and release security readiness across both programs.
  • For the AOSP-based mobile platform, establish and review an end-to-end Android platform security architecture covering verified/secure boot, hardware-backed key protection and attestation, Android KeyMint/StrongBox where supported, SELinux policy, system-service and HAL trust boundaries, device identity, production provisioning, secure OTA/rollback protection and vulnerability response.
  • For the regulated embedded Linux platform, own platform-level security architecture and secure Linux baselines; lead threat and risk analysis, security hardening, boot integrity, secure communication and updates, SBOM/CVE monitoring, remediation, long-term security maintenance, and security verification. Deliver platform-level cybersecurity evidence supporting IEC 62304 and ISO 14971 activities and applicable FDA cybersecurity expectations, working within L4B's ISO 13485 quality management system. The medical device manufacturer retains responsibility for device-level risk acceptance and regulatory approval.
  • Select threat modeling and risk assessment approaches based on the product and applicable requirements (e.g., STRIDE, TARA or other suitable methods); translate identified threats into prioritized architectural controls and documented engineering decisions.
  • Remain hands-on: demonstrate prior personal implementation of meaningful embedded security controls and be capable of reviewing and debugging code, boot/security flows, platform configuration and verification evidence, while guiding AOSP, Linux, firmware and QA engineers.
  • Own product security from early architecture through integration, release, production maintenance and security incident/vulnerability response. Do not treat penetration testing, governance or compliance work alone as a substitute for security architecture and implementation ownership.

Key Responsibilities

1. Embedded Product Security Architecture

  • Design and implement security architectures for Embedded Linux, Android/AOSP and other embedded platforms.
  • Perform device-level threat modeling, attack-surface analysis and security risk assessments.
  • Identify threats involving physical device access, debug interfaces, firmware extraction, communication interfaces and software vulnerabilities.
  • Translate security requirements into practical technical controls and engineering tasks.
  • Collaborate with hardware, BSP, platform and application engineers to implement security by design.

2. Secure Boot, Device Identity and Cryptography

  • Implement and validate Secure Boot, Verified Boot and chain-of-trust mechanisms.
  • Work with hardware-backed security technologies such as TPM, HSM, secure elements, ARM TrustZone and OP-TEE, as applicable.
  • Design secure device identity, key provisioning, key storage and key lifecycle mechanisms.
  • Implement cryptographic signing, integrity verification and secure firmware authentication.
  • Support secure manufacturing provisioning and device lifecycle security.

3. Embedded Linux and Android Platform Hardening

  • Implement security controls within Embedded Linux and, where applicable, Android/AOSP platforms.
  • Harden bootloaders, Linux kernels, operating-system configurations and device services.
  • Work with Linux security mechanisms such as SELinux, AppArmor, dm-verity, dm-crypt and filesystem protection.
  • Reduce attack surfaces by securing services, ports, permissions, interfaces and debug capabilities.
  • Collaborate with Yocto/BSP engineers to integrate security controls into production firmware images.

4. Secure Firmware Updates and Product Lifecycle Security

  • Design and implement secure firmware and OTA update mechanisms.
  • Ensure firmware authenticity, integrity, rollback protection and secure recovery.
  • Support secure update architectures for connected and field-deployed products.
  • Investigate product vulnerabilities and contribute to remediation across supported software versions.
  • Help establish security maintenance practices for products throughout their operational lifecycle.

5. Vulnerability Management and Security Verification

  • Perform vulnerability analysis across embedded firmware, operating systems, libraries and third-party components.
  • Work with CVE databases, software composition analysis and SBOM generation.
  • Assess vulnerability exploitability and product-specific security impact.
  • Support static analysis, dynamic analysis, firmware analysis and penetration-testing activities.
  • Develop or integrate security verification into CI/CD pipelines.
  • Document security findings, remediation actions and verification evidence.

6. Product Security and Engineering Collaboration

  • Work closely with Embedded Linux, Android/AOSP, BSP, hardware, DevSecOps, QA and product-engineering teams.
  • Participate in security design reviews and technical risk assessments.
  • Support security requirements, verification and traceability for regulated or security-sensitive products.
  • Contribute to product-security documentation and technical security decisions.
  • Independently investigate and resolve complex embedded security issues.

Required Qualifications and Experience

  • Minimum 10 years of professional embedded or platform software engineering experience, with substantial hands-on work in Embedded Linux, Android/AOSP, firmware, bootloaders or similar low-level systems.
  • At least 5 years of direct, hands-on embedded product cybersecurity experience designing, implementing and validating security controls in connected devices or other shipped embedded products.
  • At least 3 years of demonstrable technical leadership or ownership of product-security architecture, including threat modeling/risk assessment, security requirements, design decisions, implementation oversight and verification through release.
  • Mandatory evidence: explain at least one real embedded product where the candidate was accountable for end-to-end cybersecurity decisions and personally implemented meaningful security controls. General IT security, compliance-only, penetration testing or advisory work alone does not satisfy this requirement.
  • Strong professional experience in embedded software engineering, with substantial hands-on responsibility for embedded product cybersecurity.
  • Professional experience securing consumer electronics, medical devices or comparable connected embedded products.
  • Strong understanding of embedded hardware, firmware, bootloaders, operating systems and device security boundaries.
  • Hands-on experience implementing security controls in Embedded Linux, Android/AOSP or comparable embedded platforms.
  • Demonstrated practical experience in several of the following:
    • Secure Boot, Verified Boot or hardware root of trust.
    • Secure key storage, provisioning and cryptographic integration.
    • Embedded Linux security hardening.
    • Secure firmware updates and rollback protection.
    • Device-level threat modeling and attack-surface reduction.
    • Embedded vulnerability analysis and remediation.
  • Strong Linux debugging and embedded systems troubleshooting skills.
  • Proficiency in C/C++ and scripting with Python or Bash.
  • Ability to independently own technical security tasks from design through implementation and verification.
  • Experience working with cross-functional product-development teams.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Ideal background: 12–15+ years in embedded/platform engineering, with broad experience securing Android/AOSP and/or other embedded Linux devices and guiding product-security delivery across multiple programs.
  • Direct experience with consumer electronics, connected devices, smart home products, multimedia devices, wearables or other commercially deployed embedded products.
  • Experience developing or securing medical-device software, connected medical equipment or regulated healthcare products.
  • Practical experience with ARM TrustZone, OP-TEE, TPM, secure elements or hardware security modules.
  • Experience with Yocto/OpenEmbedded, U-Boot, Linux kernel configuration and BSP security integration.
  • Android Verified Boot (AVB), Android security architecture or SELinux policy development.
  • Secure OTA frameworks and firmware-signing infrastructure.
  • Experience with SBOM tooling, CVE assessment and software composition analysis.
  • Familiarity with applicable product-security standards and guidance, such as IEC 62443, ETSI EN 303 645, IEC 81001-5-1, IEC 62304, ISO 14971 or relevant EU Cyber Resilience Act requirements.
  • Experience supporting security verification, technical documentation and product-security audits.
  • Experience working on products requiring long-term security maintenance and vulnerability response.

What We Are Looking For

We are particularly interested in engineers who can demonstrate:

  • Security mechanisms they have personally designed, implemented, integrated or validated.
  • Experience working with actual embedded products rather than security concepts alone.
  • Understanding of how hardware, firmware, operating systems and connectivity affect device security.
  • Ability to investigate vulnerabilities and implement practical remediation.
  • Ownership of technical decisions and security deliverables.
  • Clear communication with embedded engineering and product teams.

Important: This position requires practical embedded product-security engineering experience. General IT security, SOC operations, infrastructure security, penetration testing without embedded-product engineering, or compliance-only experience will not independently meet the role requirements.

Why Join L4B Software?

  • Work on embedded platform and product-security engineering challenges.
  • Contribute to secure software platforms used in complex connected products.
  • Collaborate with international engineering teams.
  • Take ownership of meaningful security design and implementation responsibilities.
  • Work in an environment where technical depth, independent problem-solving and engineering quality matter.

Application

Please share your resume highlighting the embedded products and platforms you have worked on, the security mechanisms you personally implemented, and your experience with production or commercially deployed devices.

Every therapist on the remote caseload starts with six in-person brace fittings on patients from your own current caseload, so you know the devices you will be coaching patients on. Blanchard is headquartered in sunny Southern California, but our reach and our team extend across the US, UK, and beyond.   • Processes contract documents through Blanchard’s contract lifecycle management system (Gateway), Salesforce, and DocuSign.

Coordination and Communication

  • Serves as a point of contact for Sales and Project Managers regarding assigned contracts, timelines, and required information.
  • Communicates professionally with clients as needed to facilitate contract execution and resolve routine questions.

  • Escalation and Collaboration
  • Work in close partnership with the Sales Contracts Manager on non-standard contractual terms, including legal, privacy, and information security-related matters.
  • Coordinates with Sales to obtain approval for changes to pricing, payment terms, or other key business terms.
  • Escalates contractual issues as needed to ensure alignment with company policy and risk tolerance.

Systems and Process Support

  • Uses Salesforce and DocuSign independently from Day 1.
  • Learns and follows internal processes for contract intake, tracking, and record management in Gateway.
  • Maintains organized contract records and document communications as appropriate.
  • Utilization of company-approved AI tools to support contract-related work.

Who You Are:

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in business, legal studies, paralegal studies, or a related field.
  • Prior experience in contract administration, sales contracts, or a similar role preferred.
  • Experience working with Salesforce and electronic signature platforms strongly preferred.
  • Experience using AI-assisted tools in the workplace.
  • Experience with contract lifecycle management systems is a plus.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.
  • Ability to understand, review, and apply contract terms within established guidelines.
  • Comfort working with templates, standardized processes, and defined escalation paths.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities while meeting expected turnaround times.
  • Professional, approachable communication style with both internal stakeholders and clients.
  • Willingness to ask questions, seek clarification, and learn new systems and processes quickly.
  • Ability to work independently while staying closely aligned with the Sales Contracts Manager.

Work Environment: This is a remote role that requires the ability to work independently, manage multiple requests, and collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams in a fast-paced environment. The role requires strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and comfort navigating evolving priorities.

Senior Network Configuration & Integration Engineer

Program: Army Global Unified Network (AGUN)

Location: Remote | Up to 10% Travel, *Please be advised that during the interview, you will be required to keep your camera on, and your interviewer will be taking your picture for identification purposes, if an offer letter is extended to you.

Clearance Required: Active Secret
Citizenship: U.S. Citizenship Required


Help Build the Future of the U.S. Army's Global Network!

Leidos is seeking an experienced Senior Network Configuration & Integration Engineer to support the Army Global Unified Network (AGUN) program.

This is an exciting opportunity to help modernize the Army's global network infrastructure by designing, configuring, integrating, and validating secure enterprise network solutions.

In this role, you'll work with engineering, cybersecurity, operations, and deployment teams to turn approved network designs into standardized, repeatable network configurations and deployment packages supporting APEX, EDGE, and other Army network nodes.

We're looking for a hands-on Senior Network Engineer with strong routing and switching experience, network integration expertise, and the ability to develop reliable, scalable solutions for complex enterprise environments.


What You'll Do

  • Design and develop standardized network configurations, templates, and deployment packages for Army network modernization.
  • Translate approved network architectures into practical hardware, software, and configuration solutions.
  • Configure, integrate, and troubleshoot enterprise routing, switching, SD-WAN, and network security technologies.
  • Define technical requirements for network hardware, software, licensing, connectivity, capacity, and resiliency.
  • Support network integration testing, interoperability validation, and lab testing before deployment.
  • Develop network configuration templates, technical procedures, installation guides, and acceptance test plans.
  • Validate BGP, VRF, network segmentation, security policies, and management connectivity.
  • Evaluate equipment changes, software upgrades, and configuration updates for compatibility and operational impact.
  • Troubleshoot complex network integration, performance, routing, and connectivity issues.
  • Work with Cybersecurity and Configuration Management teams to ensure compliance with DoD security standards and change-control processes.
  • Provide technical guidance and troubleshooting support to network installation and deployment teams.
  • Support deployment readiness reviews, technical acceptance testing, and operational handoffs.
  • Identify opportunities to automate network configurations, improve consistency, and streamline deployments.
  • Collaborate with AGUN Operations to ensure new network capabilities transition successfully into ongoing support.

What We're Looking For

  • Active DoD Secret security clearance and U.S. citizenship.
  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, IT, or a related field with 8–12 years of relevant network engineering experience. Additional relevant experience may be considered in place of a degree.
  • DoD 8570/8140 IAT Level II qualification, as applicable to the assigned work role.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain any required Computing Environment (CE) certification.
  • Strong hands-on experience designing, configuring, integrating, and troubleshooting enterprise networks.
  • Advanced knowledge of routing and switching, BGP, VRF, SD-WAN, network segmentation, high availability, and resiliency.
  • Experience with enterprise networking technologies such as Cisco, Juniper, Palo Alto Networks, or comparable vendors.
  • Experience developing standardized network configurations, deployment templates, and technical integration procedures.
  • Experience integrating network hardware, software, security appliances, and management platforms.
  • Hands-on experience with network integration testing, interoperability validation, and technical troubleshooting.
  • Knowledge of network security controls, configuration management, and change-control procedures.
  • Experience creating network diagrams, implementation guides, technical specifications, and acceptance test documentation.
  • Strong analytical, communication, documentation, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating with engineering, cybersecurity, and deployment teams.

Preferred Qualifications

  • CCNP, CCIE, JNCIP, or equivalent advanced networking certification.
  • Experience supporting U.S. Army, DoD, or federal enterprise network modernization programs.
  • Experience with Ansible, Terraform, Git, Python, or other network automation tools.
  • Familiarity with Zero Trust Architecture, IPv6, and Software-Defined Networking (SDN).
  • Experience integrating networks across geographically dispersed or tactical environments.
  • Experience developing standardized network deployment packages and reusable configuration templates.
  • Experience with lab integration, technical acceptance testing, and operational readiness validation.
  • Experience supporting large-scale network migrations, modernization, and deployment initiatives.
  • Knowledge of DoD STIGs, cybersecurity requirements, and configuration compliance.

Why Join Leidos?

At Leidos, you'll have the opportunity to work on complex enterprise networking technologies while supporting a mission that directly impacts the U.S. Army's global communications.

You'll collaborate with experienced engineers, help standardize critical network infrastructure, and play an important role in delivering secure, reliable network solutions worldwide.

If you're a Senior Network Engineer who enjoys hands-on configuration, complex network integration, and solving technical challenges, we'd like to hear from you!

Join Leidos and help build the next generation of Army network infrastructure. Apply today!

If you're looking for comfort, keep scrolling. At Leidos, we outthink, outbuild, and outpace the status quo — because the mission demands it. We're not hiring followers. We're recruiting the ones who disrupt, provoke, and refuse to fail. Step 10 is ancient history. We're already at step 30 — and moving faster than anyone else dares.
